title: Global System of Trade Preferences (GSTP) among Developing Countries
description:
The Global System of Trade Preferences (GSTP) among Developing Countries establishes tariff concessions among its 42 Parties. It establishes preferential tariffs for energy products, including: 

  • Electric motor parts;
  • Air conditioning appliances; 
  • Cathodes and cathode sections; 
  • Refined copper and copper alloys; 
  • Cobalt mattes and other intermediate products of cobalt's metallurgy;
  • Ferrous waste and scrap; 

Rule of origins apply to qualify for the preferential tariff treatment, notably establishing that:
  • products should be wholly produced or obtained in the exporting participant to the GSTP;
  • products should not incorporate non-originating materials valued above 50% of the Free on Board (FOB) value of the final product

title: US Generalised Scheme of Preferences
description:
The US Generalised Scheme of Preferences (GSP) provides for non-reciprocal, duty-free treatment to developing countries 1974 from 1976 to 2020. Its renewal is currently being discussed.

The original GSP covered industrial products across HS sectors 25 through 96 including : 

  • Aluminium (o/than alloy), unwrought;
  • Lithium primary cells and primary batteries;
  • Primary cells and primary batteries;
  • Parts of primary cells and primary batteries;
  • Other electrical machines and apparatus for electroplating, electrolysis, or electrophoresis;
  • Refrigerators, household absorption-type, electrical;

For a product to qualify for GSP preferential tariff treatment, it need to originate from a beneficiary developing country (BDC). Additionally, the combined cost or value of materials from the BDC and the direct processing costs needed to represent at least 35% of the product's appraised value.

title: Argentina - EU Strategic Partnership on sustainable raw materials value chains
description:
The European Union and Argentina signed a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) focused on cooperation sustainable raw materials value chains. The MoU seeks to bolster a competitive and sustainable mining sector that generates quality employment and fosters economic growth for both parties. The MoU was signed as part of the European Union's Global Gateway strategy, which aims to mobilise up to EUR 300 billion in public and private investments from 2021 to 2027. 
The partnership encompasses five key areas. 

  1. Integrating sustainable raw materials value chains through projects and trade facilitation,
  2. Cooperation in research and innovation, 
  3. Aligning with environmental, social and governance (ESG) criteria and international standards,
  4. Developing infrastructure with minimal environmental impact and 
  5. Strengthening capacities, enhancing skills and education along the value chains.
Following the MoU, the EU and Argentina will work on an operational roadmap to guide cooperation actions carried out by relevant stakeholders from both sides. This partnership complements similar agreements with Canada, Ukraine, Kazakhstan, Namibia and Argentina, promoting secure, sustainable and resilient raw materials value chains to drive the transition to climate-neutral and digitalised economies.

title: Directive 2010/75/EU on industrial emissions - power generation installations limits
description:
The Industrial Emissions Directive aims to achieve a high level of protection of human health and the environment taken as a whole by reducing harmful industrial emissions across the EU. The Directive regulates over 50,000 of the EU's largest industrial installations, including energy industries, production and processing of metals, minerals and chemicals and waste management (Annex I). These installations must operate in accordance with a permit with conditions that are aligned with the principles and provisions of the Directive.

Emission limit values for combustion plants for which permit was granted before January 2013 range from: 
  • Coal, lignite and solid fuels: SO2 to be limited to 200-400 mg/Nm3 // NOx to 200-450 mg/Nm3
  • Biomass: SO2 to be limited to 200 mg/Nm3 //  NOx to 200-300 mg/Nm3
  • Peat: SO2 to be limited to 200-300 mg/Nm3 //  NOx to 200-300 mg/Nm3
  • Liquid fuels: SO2 to be limited to 200-350 mg/Nm3 //  NOx to 150-450 mg/Nm3
  • Gaseaous fuels: SO2 to be limited to 35 mg/Nm3 (with the exception of gas turbines and gas engines) //  NOx to 100-200 mg/Nm3 // CO to 100 mg/Nm3. 
For the remaining plants, emission limit values range from: 
  • Coal, lignite and solid fuels: SO2 to be limited to 150-400 mg/Nm3 // NOx to 200-450 mg/Nm3
  • Biomass: SO2 to be limited to 150-200 mg/Nm3 //  NOx to 150-250 mg/Nm3
  • Peat: SO2 to be limited to 150-300 mg/Nm3 //  NOx to 150-250 mg/Nm3
  • Liquid fuels: SO2 to be limited to 150-350 mg/Nm3 //  NOx to 100-300 mg/Nm3
  • Gaseaous fuels: SO2 to be limited to 35 mg/Nm3 (with the exception of gas turbines and gas engines) //  NOx to 50-100 mg/Nm3 // CO to 100 mg/Nm3. 

The directive was amended in 2022 to provide tighter pollutant emission limit values and extend the scope of industrial facilities.

For power plants licensed to operate between 1996 and 2010, limits for SO2 are 20-640 mg / m3 // NOx to 120-350 mg / m3 // PM to 60-120 mg / m3

title: 2023 Emission Standards for Power Generation Units
description:
Singapore's Energy Market Authority enacted in 2023 its "Final Determination on Emission Standards Framework for New and Repowered Fossil Fuel-fired Generation Units", in order to facilitate the deployment of clean and efficient power generation units in Singapore. 
All new and repowered fossil fuel-fired plants should meet the Tier 1 emission standard of 0.355 tCO2e/MWh on an annual basis.  Plants that are unable to meet Tier 1 standard can opt to be subject to an emissions limit under Tier 2, for which  emissions allowance limit that is equivalent to a Tier 1 advanced CCGT but running at a  Plant Load Factor of 50% on an annual basis.

description:

title: New Source Performance Standards: Greenhouse Gas Emissions from New, Modified, and Reconstructed Fossil Fuel-Fired Electric Generating Units
description:
The US EPA announced in April 2024 updated pollution standards for existing coal-fired and new gas-fired power plants. 

Guidelines for gas-fired power plants set two gradual phases, aiming at a large implementation of carbon capture and storage by 2032. 

Standards and guidelines for new coal-fired power plants on their end set new base load combustion turbines to have until January 1st, 2032 to meet an emission standard based on 90% capture of CO2 emissions. Existing power plants that have committed to cease operations by January 1st, 2039 will have a numeric emission rate limit based on 40% natural gas co-firing that must be met on January 1st, 2030, while those intending to run after 2039 would have to meet a numeric emission rate limit based on application of CCS with 90% capture by 2032.

title: Montreal Protocol - London Amendment
description:
The Montreal Protocol on Substances that Deplete the Ozone Layer is a global agreement to protect the Earth’s ozone layer by phasing out the chemicals that deplete it. 

The 1990 London Amendment: 
  • Added fully halogenated CFCs, carbon tetrachloride, and methyl chloroform to the list of substances. 
  • Mandated the elimination of the production and consumption of CFCs, halons, and carbon tetrachloride by January 1st, 2000, and of methyl chloroform by January 1st, 2005. 
  • Banned trade in these substances with countries that are not Parties to the Protocol. 
  • Created a separate timetable of reductions for developing countries and established a special fund to help developing countries meet their obligations.

title: Montreal Protocol - Copenhagen Amendment
description:
The Montreal Protocol on Substances that Deplete the Ozone Layer is a global agreement to protect the Earth’s ozone layer by phasing out the chemicals that deplete it. 

The 1992 Copenhagen Amendment: 
  • Set the phase-out of consumption and production of CFCs (including fully halogenated CFCs), methyl chloroform, and carbon tetrachloride by January 1st, 1996, and of halons by January 1st, 1994. 
  • Hydrobromofluorocarbons (HBFCs) and methyl bromide were added to the controlled substances list, with the former scheduled for developed-state phase-out by January 1st, 1996, and consumption and production of the latter to be frozen at 1991 levels. 
  • HCFCs were added to the controlled substances list and required to be phased out gradually by 2030.

title: Montreal Protocol - Beijing Amendment
description:
The Montreal Protocol on Substances that Deplete the Ozone Layer is a global agreement to protect the Earth’s ozone layer by phasing out the chemicals that deplete it. 

The 1997 Beijing Amendment: 
  • Added bromochloromethane to the list of substances needing to be controlled and phase-out its production and use by 2002; impose a freeze on the consumption of HCFCs beginning in 2004;
  • Banned all trade of HCFCs and bromochloromethane between Parties to the amendment and non-Parties; 
  • Required each State Party to submit statistical data on the amount of methyl bromide used for quarantine and pre-shipment applications.

title: Regulation 2024/573 on fluorinated greenhouse gases
description:

  • Sets a cap of HFCs production within the EU, aiming at a 15% reduction rate between 2025 and 2036.

title: EU Generalised Scheme of Preferences
description:
The EU Generalised Scheme of Preferences (GSP) was first introduced in 1971 and most recently renewed for the period of 2024 to 2034. 

It provides non-reciprocal tariff preferences for developing countries imports into the EU, based on their level of development and contingent on implementation of core human rights, labour, governance, and other sustainable development conventions. Imports from Least Developed Countries are exempted from border tariffs.

The GSP covers most industrial and energy sector products, including : 

  • Iron and steel articles
  • Aluminium (o/than alloy), unwrought;
  • Nuclear reactors, boilers and machinery
  • Automobiles, motor vehicles, parts and accessories
  • Lithium primary cells and primary batteries;
  • Primary cells and primary batteries;
  • Parts of primary cells and primary batteries;
  • Other electrical machines and equipment including semiconductors, transistors
  • Refrigerators, household absorption-type, electrical;

In line with Regulation(EEC) No 2454/93, a good may benefit from preferential tariff treatment if it the value of the non-originating materials it incorporates is below 15% of its ex-works price.

description: The Vietnamese authorities initiated in June 2024 an investigation regarding the potential implementation of anti-dumping measures on galvanised steel product imports originating from China and South Korea.

title: Investigation on extension of antidumping measures on hot-rolled coil steel
description: In September 2023, the Ministry of Commerce of Thailand initiated an investigation on a potential extension of antidumping measures on hot-rolled coil steel import originating from China.

title: Anti-dumping duty on cold rolled coils and sheets imports
description: In April 2024, the Philippine authorities implemented an anti-dumping duty on cold rolled coils and sheets imports originating from Malaysia.

title: Affirmative Determinations in the Antidumping and Countervailing Duty Investigations of Ferrosilicon imports
description: In June 24, the U.S. authorities determined preliminary dumping rates and subsidy rates in the antidumping duty (AD) and countervailing duty (CVD) investigations conducted on ferrosilicon imports originating from Russia.

title: Antidumping and Countervailing Duty Investigations of Ferrosilicon imports
description: In April 2024, the US authorities initiated investigations of imports of ferrosilicon originating from Brazil, Kazakhstan, Malaysia and Russia.

title: Antidumping and Countervailing Duty Investigations of Crystalline Silicon Photovoltaic Cell imports
description: In May 2024, the US authorities initiated antidumping and countervailing duty investigations of crystalline silicon photovoltaic cell imports from Cambodia, Malaysia, Thailand, and Viet Nam.

description: In 2024, the U.S. Department of Commerce advised against the revocation of the antidumping duty orders on steel concrete reinforcing bar (rebar) imports originating from Belarus, China (China), Indonesia, Latvia, Moldova, Poland, and Ukraine.

title: Government support for domestic clean energy technology manufacturers
description: In June 2024, the Italian government set up a grant scheme to support domestic manufacturers of batteries, solar energy equipment, wind energy equipment, heat pumps, electrolysers,  CCUS equipment and related critical minerals sourcing.

title: Contract for Difference Scheme- Onshore Wind and Solar Photovoltaic
description:
The Romanian government is launching in September 2024 a tender process to allocate contracts for difference for the construction and operation of solar photovoltaic and onshore wind installations. The contracts for difference are designed to run over over the next 15 years. 

The European Commission approved a EUR 3 billion State aid for this scheme, under the State aid Temporary Crisis and Transition Framework
policyType: [{"topic":"Power","family":"Incentives and investments","name":"Government spending in low-carbon electricity","category":"Wind turbines"},{"topic":"Power","family":"Incentives and investments","name":"Government spending in low-carbon electricity","category":"Solar PVs"}]

title: Green Investment Scheme - Wind Turbines and Electrolysers
description: In January 2024, the Danish government granted financial support to five domestic manufacturing projects related to wind energy, and electrolysis (Power-to-X).

title: Italian State Aid for Industrial Hydrogen
description: The European Commission approved an Italian state aid scheme of €550 million to support industrial hydrogen processes, notably substition of methane and other fossil fuels with renewable hydrogen. The aid will be in the form of direct grants, effective till end 2025.
policyType: [{"topic":"Fuels","family":"Incentives and investments","name":"Government spending in hydrogen","category":null}]

title: German State Aid for Decarbonising Steel Production Process
description: The European Commission approved a €2.6 billion German direct grant to SHS Stahl-Holding-Saar GmbH & Co KGaA (‘SHS') in decarbonising its steel production processes. This includes constrcution of a direct reduction plant and two new electric ar furnaces.
policyType: [{"topic":"Industry","family":"Incentives and investments","name":"Government spending for energy efficiency and recycling","category":null}]

title: Renewable Gas Auction
description:
In May 2024, the Portuguese government launched an auction for the centralized purchase of clean hydrogen and biomethane produced by electrolysis of water using  electricity from renewable energy sources. It will be composed of two parcels: 150 GWh/year of biomethane; and 120 GWh/year of hydrogen.
The results of the competitive procedure were published in February 2025.
policyType: [{"topic":"Fuels","family":"Incentives and investments","name":"Government spending in biofuels","category":"Advanced biofuels"},{"topic":"Fuels","family":"Incentives and investments","name":"Government spending in biofuels","category":"Biogas"}]

title: Ozone-depleting Substances and Halocarbon Alternatives Regulations
description:
The Ozone-depleting Substances and Halocarbon Alternatives Regulations aim at setting norms over the import, export, production, use and sale of ozone-depleting substances such as F-gases. 

Last amendment in 2020 translates Kigali Amendment to the Montreal Protocol in the Canadian policy framework, with a scheduled phase-down of HFC consumption in the country.
policyType: [{"topic":"Buildings","family":"Regulations","name":"F-gas regulations","category":null},{"topic":"Industry","family":"Regulations","name":"F-gas regulations","category":null}]

title: Executive Decree No. 44321 on ozone-depleting substances
description:
The decree aims at translating the Kigali Amendment of the Montreal Protocol with regards to imports, exports, use and consumptions of F-gases, notably HFCs. 

  The decree is part of a broader framework regulating other ozone-depleting substances through its 2018 law No. 9522 on the amendment to the Montreal Protocol on Substances that Deplete the Ozone Layer.
policyType: [{"topic":"Buildings","family":"Regulations","name":"F-gas regulations","category":null},{"topic":"Industry","family":"Regulations","name":"F-gas regulations","category":null}]

title: The Ozone Depleting Substances (Regulation and Control) Amendment Rules 2014
description:
The rules aim at regulating the import, export, production and use of ozone-depleting substances, notably F-gases. 

The rules notably set a phase-out schedule per substance and activity.
policyType: [{"topic":"Buildings","family":"Regulations","name":"F-gas regulations","category":null},{"topic":"Industry","family":"Regulations","name":"F-gas regulations","category":null}]

title: Law Concerning the Protection of the Ozone Layer through the Control of Specified Substances
description:
The law aims at set regulations and targets for the import, export, production and use of ozone-depleting substances in Japan. 

The act was regularly amended to reflect the increasing international comitments and amendments done to the Montreal Protocol,  last modified in 2020 to regulate the manufacture and import of HFCs.
policyType: [{"topic":"Buildings","family":"Regulations","name":"F-gas regulations","category":null},{"topic":"Industry","family":"Regulations","name":"F-gas regulations","category":null}]

title: Cooling Action Plan - HFCs regulations
description:
The plan aims at providing strategies and norms to improve energy efficiency and mitigate emissions for cooling use. 

It notably translate the Kigali Amendment to the Montreal Protocol, scheduling a phase down of HFCs emissions from 2024 up to 80% by 2045.
policyType: [{"topic":"Buildings","family":"Regulations","name":"F-gas regulations","category":null},{"topic":"Industry","family":"Regulations","name":"F-gas regulations","category":null}]

title: Ozone Layer Protection Amendment Regulations 2018
description:
The Ozone Layer Protection Amendment Regulations set the norms and targets for the import, export, production and use of ozone-depleting substances. 

Its last revision reflects Kigali Amendment to the Montreal Protocol with the inclusion of HFCs.
policyType: [{"topic":"Buildings","family":"Regulations","name":"F-gas regulations","category":null},{"topic":"Industry","family":"Regulations","name":"F-gas regulations","category":null}]

title: Environmental Protection and Management (Amendment) Act 2021
description:
The act provides an updated framework to notably improve the mitigation of GHG emissions in Singapore.  

Among measures, the government aims at reducing HFCs emissions from the use of refrigerants through restrictions on the supply of refrigeration and airconditioning equipments.
policyType: [{"topic":"Buildings","family":"Regulations","name":"F-gas regulations","category":null},{"topic":"Industry","family":"Regulations","name":"F-gas regulations","category":null}]

title: The Fluorinated Greenhouse Gases Regulations
description: | The regulations aim at setting the norms and quota for the export, import, production and use of  Fluorinated Greenhouse gases (F-gases), notably  Hydrofluorocarbons (HFCs).
policyType: [{"topic":"Buildings","family":"Regulations","name":"F-gas regulations","category":null},{"topic":"Industry","family":"Regulations","name":"F-gas regulations","category":null}]

title: American Innovation and Manufacturing Act
description:
The act aims at phasing down the production and usage of HFCs, targeting a reduction of 85% by 2036.
It notably sets rules and regulations for the import, export and production of HFCs.
policyType: [{"topic":"Buildings","family":"Regulations","name":"F-gas regulations","category":null},{"topic":"Industry","family":"Regulations","name":"F-gas regulations","category":null}]

title: Resolution 814/2013 on minimum energy efficiency standards for air conditioners
description: The resolution sets a minimum energy efficiency for air conditioners whose cooling capacity is less than or equal to 7 kW as of August 1st, 2014.
policyType: [{"topic":"Buildings","family":"Regulations","name":"Minimum Energy Performance Standards (MEPS)","category":"Air conditioners"}]

title: Resolution n°1/2022 on new target programme for air conditioners
description:
The regulation sets updated targets and minimum seasonal cooling performance levels for air conditioners, and is split into two gradual phases. 

Deadlines for manufacturers and importers to comply with step 1 standards as of December 31st, 2022, and up to December 31st, 2025 for step 2 levels. 
Wholesalers and retailers on their end need to comply with step 1 standards as of December 31st, 2024, and up to December 31st, 2027 for step 2 levels.
policyType: [{"topic":"Buildings","family":"Regulations","name":"Minimum Energy Performance Standards (MEPS)","category":"Air conditioners"}]

title: Lithuania State Aid to Support Offshore Wind farms
description: The European Commission approved a Lithuanian state aid of €193 million to support the implementation of a 700MW offshore wind farm in the Baltic Sea. The aid will be in the form of variable premium under two-way contracts for difference ("CfD'), granted by end 2025.
policyType: [{"topic":"Power","family":"Incentives and investments","name":"Government spending in low-carbon electricity","category":"Wind turbines"}]

title: Hungarian State Aid for Domestic Clean Technology Producers
description: The European Commission approved a Hungarian state aid scheme of €2.36 billion to support investments for the production of net-zero transition equipment in the field of in the production of batteries, solar panels, wind turbines, heat pumps, electrolysers, carbon capture usage and storage, and critical mineral production. The aid will be in the form of direct grants and tax advantages, effective till end 2025.
policyType: [{"topic":"Power","family":"Incentives and investments","name":"Government spending in low-carbon electricity","category":"Other"}]

title: Hungarian State Aid to Support Electricity Storage Facilities
description: The Hungarian government is providing financial grants to projects aiming at developing electricity storage installations for industries and households.
policyType: [{"topic":"Power","family":"Incentives and investments","name":"Government spending  in storage","category":"Batteries"}]

title: GB 21454-2021 standard on minimum allowable values of the energy efficiency and energy efficiency grades for multi-connected air-condition (heat pump) units
description:
The standard sets updated minimum energy performance standards for central air conditioning, with revised grades comparable to Japan or US standards.
In January 2024, the National Development and Reform Commission (NDRC) revised the MEPS, expanding their coverage and setting higher 'Energy Saving' and 'Advanced' levels of equipment across 43 products, 8 of which are cooling products.
policyType: [{"topic":"Buildings","family":"Regulations","name":"Minimum Energy Performance Standards (MEPS)","category":"Air conditioners"},{"topic":"Buildings","family":"Regulations","name":"Minimum Energy Performance Standards (MEPS)","category":"Heat pumps"}]

title: Hydrogen Core Network
description:
Germany established a Hydrogen Core Network in June 2024, to be financed through network charges. The Network is meant to build and connect hydrogen production infrastructures.
The German government is providing initial financing - the European Commission approved the provision of EUR 3 billion under EU State aid rules to support the construction of the Hydrogen Core Network (‘HCN').
policyType: [{"topic":"Fuels","family":"Incentives and investments","name":"Government spending in hydrogen","category":null}]

title: Government spending in solar PV and electricity storage development
description: The government of the Slovak Republic set up a call for projects to support the production of electricity and heat from renewable energy sources, as well as electricity storage development.
policyType: [{"topic":"Power","family":"Incentives and investments","name":"Government spending in low-carbon electricity","category":"Solar PVs"},{"topic":"Power","family":"Incentives and investments","name":"Government spending  in storage","category":"Batteries"}]

title: Finland State Aid to Support Methane and Methanol Production
description: The European Commission approved a Finnish state aid scheme of €66 million to support renewable methane and methanol production. The aid is fully financed by the Recovery and Resilience Facility (RRF) and will come in the form of direct grants, granted by end 2025.
policyType: [{"topic":"Fuels","family":"Incentives and investments","name":"Government spending in biofuels","category":"Biogas"}]

title: Regulation 2016/2281 establishing a framework for the setting of ecodesign requirements for energy-related products, with regard to ecodesign requirements for air heating products, cooling products, high temperature process chillers and fan coil units
description:
This Regulation establishes ecodesign requirements for the placing on the market and/or putting into service of:
  • Air heating products with a rated heating capacity not exceeding 1 MW, including air-to-air heat pumps;
  • Cooling products and high temperature process chillers with a rated cooling capacity not exceeding 2 MW;
  • Fan coil units.
policyType: [{"topic":"Buildings","family":"Regulations","name":"Minimum Energy Performance Standards (MEPS)","category":"Heat pumps"}]

title: Energy Efficiency Regulations, 2016 - Heat pumps
description:
The energy efficiency regulations set standards for most appliances, including air conditioners, heat pumps and boilers. 

Standards for heat pumps were regularly updated, with last amendment enacted in 2022 (SOR/2022-265).
policyType: [{"topic":"Buildings","family":"Regulations","name":"Minimum Energy Performance Standards (MEPS)","category":"Heat pumps"}]

title: GB 19577-2024 - Minimum allowable values of the energy efficiency and energy efficiency grades for heat pumps and water chillers
description: The regulation updates minimum energy performance standards for heat pumps and water chillers.
policyType: [{"topic":"Buildings","family":"Regulations","name":"Minimum Energy Performance Standards (MEPS)","category":"Heat pumps"}]

title: Regulation No. 25584 on the Rational Use of Energy - Air conditioners
description:
The regulation sets minimum energy performance standards for a number of appliances, including air conditioners. 
The standard was regularly updated, last in 2017.
policyType: [{"topic":"Buildings","family":"Regulations","name":"Minimum Energy Performance Standards (MEPS)","category":"Air conditioners"}]

title: Notification S.O. 3897 on the Display of Labels of Room Air Conditioners
description: The Bureau of Energy Efficiency (BEE) set new energy performance standards for air conditioners, introducing an Indian Seasonal Energy Efficiency Ratio (ISEER), with minimum energy performance to 2.7 and 3.3 for unitary and split type air conditioners respectively.
policyType: [{"topic":"Buildings","family":"Regulations","name":"Minimum Energy Performance Standards (MEPS)","category":"Air conditioners"}]

title: Germany's Special Climate and Transformation Fund - Transformation of heating networks
description:
The German government is implementing a support scheme for the construction of green district heating networks. 

Direct grants are provided to new and existing district heating network operators and operators to finance the construction and the upgrade of district heating networks. In order to be eligible for public support, the systems need to operate on at least 75% renewable energy and/or waste heat.
policyType: [{"topic":"Buildings","family":"Incentives and investments","name":"Government spending for efficient or cleaner technologies","category":null}]

title: Decree 103/2021 Concerning Minimum Energy Performance Standards and Energy Saving Labels for air conditioning
description: The decree sets Minimum Energy Performance Standards for air conditioning, depending on the type of air conditioner, along with Air Conditioner Energy Saving Label system to be displayed.
policyType: [{"topic":"Buildings","family":"Regulations","name":"Minimum Energy Performance Standards (MEPS)","category":"Air conditioners"}]

title: SI 16147 on heat pumps with electric compressors - tests, performance rating and marking requirements
description: The regulation specifies the norms for performance of heat pumps with electric compressors, including energy efficiency performance rating.
policyType: [{"topic":"Buildings","family":"Regulations","name":"Minimum Energy Performance Standards (MEPS)","category":"Heat pumps"}]

title: Government spending for domestic battery and hydrogen equipment manufacturers
description: The Italian government is providing financial grants to domestic battery and clean hydrogen equipment manufacturers, in the framework of European Important Projects of Common European Interest(IPCEI Batteries 1& 2, IPCEI Hydrogen 1 & 2), which encourages research as well as industrial deployment activities .
policyType: [{"topic":"Power","family":"Incentives and investments","name":"Government spending  in storage","category":"Batteries"},{"topic":"Power","family":"Incentives and investments","name":"Government spending  in storage","category":"Thermal storage"}]

title: Energy cost contribution scheme for energy-intensive SMEs
description: In an effort to shield energy-intensive SMEs from the impact of the global energy crisis, the Dutch government implemented a grant scheme covering part of the electricity and gas bill increase.
policyType: [{"topic":"Just transitions","family":"Incentives and investments","name":"Government spending for energy affordability","category":null}]

title: SASO 2663/2021 - Standard for Air Conditioners
description: The standard SASO 2663/2021 sets updated energy performance standard for air conditioners, along with updated energy labelling for the sell of those appliances.
policyType: [{"topic":"Buildings","family":"Regulations","name":"Minimum Energy Performance Standards (MEPS)","category":"Air conditioners"},{"topic":"Buildings","family":"Regulations","name":"Minimum Energy Performance Standards (MEPS)","category":"Heat pumps"}]

title: Energy Conservation (Regulated Goods and Registered Suppliers) (Amendment) Regulations 2022
description:
The National Environment Agency updated the minimum energy performance standards of a number of appliances. 

This includes refrigerators, clothes dryers, casement and window air-conditioners, and split-type air-conditioners.
policyType: [{"topic":"Buildings","family":"Regulations","name":"Minimum Energy Performance Standards (MEPS)","category":"Air conditioners"}]

title: Communiqué on EcoDesign Requirements for Air Conditioners and Fans
description: The standard updates minimum energy performance requirements for a number of electric appliances, including air conditioners and heat pumps, in conformity with the EU Ecodesign of Energy Related Products.
policyType: [{"topic":"Buildings","family":"Regulations","name":"Minimum Energy Performance Standards (MEPS)","category":"Air conditioners"},{"topic":"Buildings","family":"Regulations","name":"Minimum Energy Performance Standards (MEPS)","category":"Heat pumps"}]

title: Resolution No. 739 on eco-design requirements for air conditioners and fans
description: The Technical Regulation establishes the ecodesign requirements for air conditioners with a nominal power lower than 12 kW, powered from the electric network, intended for cooling or heating air, as well as fans intended for personal comfort with electrical power under 125 W.
policyType: [{"topic":"Buildings","family":"Regulations","name":"Minimum Energy Performance Standards (MEPS)","category":"Air conditioners"}]

title: Regulation 2019/1242 setting CO2 emission performance standards for new heavy-duty vehicles
description:
This regulation aims at setting CO2 emissions performance standards for new heavy-duty vehicles with the following milestones: 
  • 15% reduction compared to 2019 levels for the 2025-2029 period; 
  • 30% reduction compared to 2019 levels for the 2030-2034 period.
policyType: [{"topic":"Transport","family":"Regulations","name":"Fuel efficiency standards","category":"Medium/Heavy-duty vehicles"}]

title: New Heavy Duty Vehicles (Carbon Dioxide Emission Performance Standards) (Miscellaneous Amendments) Regulations 2025
description:
The UK Heavy Duty Vehicles Emissions and Fuel Consumption Regulations aim at reflecting the EU regulation 2019/1242 in the context of the European Union (Withdrawal) Act 2018.

The regulation sets targets to reduce the average CO2 emissions from new HDV vehicles by 15% in 2025 and by 30% in 2030.
policyType: [{"topic":"Transport","family":"Regulations","name":"Fuel efficiency standards","category":"Medium/Heavy-duty vehicles"}]

title: Greenhouse Gas Emissions Standards for Heavy-Duty Engines and Vehicles-Phase 3
description:
The US Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) finalised in 2024 greenhouse gas standards for heavy-duty vehicles for model years 2027 through 2032. 
Vehicle and engine performance standards cover semi-trucks, large pickup trucks, vans, and all types and sizes of buses and work trucks, and see a reduction from phase 2 of 40% and 30% for medium-duty vehicles and heavy-duty vehicles respectively by 2032.
policyType: [{"topic":"Transport","family":"Regulations","name":"Fuel efficiency standards","category":"Medium/Heavy-duty vehicles"}]

title: Law 27640 - Biofuels Regulatory Framework
description: The law updates the biofuels regulatory framework in Argentina, setting a blending mandate valid until 2030 of 12% for bioethanol and 7.5% for biodiesel.
policyType: [{"topic":"Transport","family":"Regulations","name":"Biofuel blending mandate","category":null}]

title: Fuel Regulation 2012
description: The Fuel Regulation set standards for fuel quality and mandates for the general substitution of fossil fuels with renewable energy as biofuels or renewable electricity plus an GHG reduction mandate for fuels brought on the Austrian market. The regulation was last amended in 2024, with an updated GHG reduction mandate of 13% in 2030.
policyType: [{"topic":"Transport","family":"Regulations","name":"Biofuel blending mandate","category":null}]

title: Act on product standards for the integration of energy from renewable sources into fossil fuels intended for the transport sector
description:
The act sets standards for the blending of renewable sources in the fuel industry, and regulates the volume of biofuels on the market.
From 2024 onwards,  the total quantity of diesel or gasoline that each oil company annually releases for consumption shall contain at least 5.7 % biofuels.
policyType: [{"topic":"Transport","family":"Regulations","name":"Biofuel blending mandate","category":null}]

title: Act on Sustainable Biofuels and on the Reduction of Greenhouse Gases from Transport
description:
The act aims at defining obligatory quotas of biofuels in Denmark.

The law was last revised in 2024 to set a biofuel mandate of 7.6% for diesel and gasoline.
policyType: [{"topic":"Transport","family":"Regulations","name":"Biofuel blending mandate","category":null}]

title: Law 1279/2023 on the Act on the Promotion of Biofuels in Transport
description:
The Act on the Promotion of Biofuels in Transport sets obligations to vendors of petrol and diesel to fulfil a defined quota of biofuels.
The act was revised in 2022 and 2023 to set distribution obligation to at least 13.5% in 2024.
policyType: [{"topic":"Transport","family":"Regulations","name":"Biofuel blending mandate","category":null}]

title: Law on the promotion of the use of renewable energy for transport purposes and the reduction of greenhouse gas emissions from energy used in transport
description:
The law sets the regulatory framework for the reduction of emissions in the transport sector. 
It notably targets to reach 14% of the final energy consumption used for transport to be produced from renewable energy sources by 2030, and sets a 6.1% mandate for biofuel blending in gasoline.
policyType: [{"topic":"Transport","family":"Regulations","name":"Biofuel blending mandate","category":null}]

title: Resolution No. 3/2023 on the evolution of the mandatory addition of biodiesel to diesel oil sold to the final consumer
description:
The National Energy Policy Council (CNPE) published in March 2023 new biodiesel blending target, targeting 15% by 2026.
It enacted an increase in April 2023 from 10% to 12%, and schedule an increase to 13% by 2024 // 14% by 2025 // 15% by 2026.
policyType: [{"topic":"Transport","family":"Regulations","name":"Biofuel blending mandate","category":null}]

title: Resolution 40185/2018 which establishes the percentage of fuel alcohol mixture in regular and extra motor gasoline
description:
The regulation sets the biofuel blending mandates for gasoline in Colombia. From March, 1st 2018, biofuel blending mandate reached E10 (10% of fuel to be from renewable sources). 
Resolution 40144 of 2021 set a temporary exemption to this regulation,
policyType: [{"topic":"Transport","family":"Regulations","name":"Biofuel blending mandate","category":null}]

title: Resolution 40447 of 2022 on which establishes the maximum content of a mixture of fuel alcohol
description:
The resolution establishes an ethanol blend mandate that will remain at E4 from July to November 2023, then increases to E6 in December, E8 in January 2023, and finally E10 in February 2024. 
Biofuels are exempt from global tax, VAT, carbon tax and some local surcharge rates.
policyType: [{"topic":"Transport","family":"Regulations","name":"Biofuel blending mandate","category":null}]

title: National Oil Reserves Agency Act 2007 - Renewable Transport Fuel Obligation
description:
The National Oil Reserves Agency Act 2007 includes renewable transport blending fuel obligation and is amended regularly to reflect EU directives. 
The act was revised in 2024 to set a biofuel blending mandate of 21%, and 1% for advanced biofuel.
policyType: [{"topic":"Transport","family":"Regulations","name":"Biofuel blending mandate","category":null}]

title: Decree n. 199 on the promotion of the use of energy from renewable sources
description:
This decree aims at translating the EU directive on the promotion of the use of energy from renewable sources to Italy's legislative framework. 
It notably sets a mandate to suppliers of petrol, diesel and methane to achieve a share of at least 16% of renewable sources by 2030. Starting from 2023, the share of biofuels blended with gasoline shall stand to at least 0.5%, to increase to 3% from 2025 onwards.
policyType: [{"topic":"Transport","family":"Regulations","name":"Biofuel blending mandate","category":null}]

title: Requirements for Conformity Assessment of Petrol and Diesel Fuel
description:
The regulations determine the essential requirements and compliance specifications for ​​gasoline and diesel fuel in Latvia. 
The regulations are regularly updated: since 2019, diesel fuel is allowed to be sold only if biofuel is not less than 6.5% of the volume, while gasoline blending mandate requires at least 9.5% of biofuel mixed.
policyType: [{"topic":"Transport","family":"Regulations","name":"Biofuel blending mandate","category":null}]

title: Law on Energy from Renewable Sources
description:
The Law on Energy from Renewable Sources establishes the legal basis for the regulation, supervision and control of renewable energy sources in Lithuania. 
The law was lastly revised in 2023 to notably update biofuel blending mandates up to 6.6% in petrol and 6.2% in diesel.

title: Regulation concerning the quality of petrol and diesel fuels and the sustainable use of biofuels
description:
The regulation sets norms and standards with regards to the quality of petrol and diesel fuels, along with the use of biofuels. 
It notably sets a 7.7-9.7% blending mandate for biofuels.
policyType: [{"topic":"Transport","family":"Regulations","name":"Biofuel blending mandate","category":null}]

title: Decree energy transport
description:
The decree sets the biofuel blending mandates for the Netherlands. 
It was last updated in 2024, with upgraded share of renewable energy obligation for final consumption of 28.4% in 2024, and up to 28% in 2030.
policyType: [{"topic":"Transport","family":"Regulations","name":"Biofuel blending mandate","category":null}]

title: State Budget 2024 - biofuel blending requirements
description:
The Norwegian parliament updated new requirements for biofuel use in the transport sector. 
It notably mandates a 19% rate for road transport, 0.5% for aviation and 6% for shipping.
policyType: [{"topic":"Transport","family":"Regulations","name":"Biofuel blending mandate","category":null}]

title: Act on biocomponents and liquid biofuels
description:
The act sets regulations and standards for the use of biofuel in the transport sector. 
The minimum share of biocomponent stated in the Act is 3.2% in gasoline oil and 5.2% in diesel oil.
policyType: [{"topic":"Transport","family":"Regulations","name":"Biofuel blending mandate","category":null}]

title: Decree n°84/2022 establishing targets for the consumption of energy from renewable sources
description:
The decree translates the 2018 EU directive on renewable energy use to the Portugal legal framework. 
It notably sets blending requirement to fuel suppliers, of 11% in 2022 // 11.5% in 2023 // 13% in 2025 // 14% in 2027 // 16% in 2029.
policyType: [{"topic":"Transport","family":"Regulations","name":"Biofuel blending mandate","category":null}]

title: Act no. 309/2009 Coll. on the promotion of renewable energy sources and high efficiency cogeneration as amended

title: Renewable Transport Fuels Obligation
description:
The Renewable Transport Fuel Obligation is the UK Government's main policy for encouraging the use of low carbon fuels in road vehicles, non-road mobile machinery, and other surface transport modes. It works by setting annual obligations for fuel suppliers to require a certain perceptage of their fuel comprises sustainable low carbon fuel.
 
 The obligation has two elements: the 'main obligation', currently 14.054%, and the 'development fuel target', currently 1.619%. Fuel suppliers can meet their obligation by redeeming Renewable Transport Fuel Certificates, or by paying a fixed sum for each litre of fuel for which they wish to 'buy-out' of their obligation. These obligations under the scheme are currently set to increased out to 2032, before levelling off. The UK Department for Transport is currently (2024-25) undertaking a statutory review of the scheme.

title: Prevailing Wage and Apprenticeship Bonus Provisions
description:
The U.S. Department of the Treasury and the Internal Revenue Service (IRS) released final rules  on prevailing wage and registered apprenticeship (PWA) requirements in the Inflation Reduction Act. 
As part of the Biden-Harris Administration's Investing in America agenda, the final rules will help build a strong pipeline of highly-skilled workers to support the growth of the clean energy economy and ensure clean energy jobs are good-paying jobs.  inal rules from Treasury – which were developed in close partnership with the Department of Labor (DOL) – provide clarity and certainty on the PWA requirements to ensure the clean energy transition is centered around workers. In general, if taxpayers pay prevailing wages to laborers and mechanics and hire registered apprentices for projects supported by most of the Inflation Reduction Act’s clean energy tax incentives, then taxpayers can claim an increased credit equal to five times the base incentive. This includes projects utilizing the investment and production tax credits that help finance utility-scale wind, solar, and battery storage projects, as well as for credits for carbon capture, utilization, and storage and clean hydrogen projects.

title: Transferability Bonus Provisions
description:
The U.S. Department of the Treasury and the Internal Revenue Service (IRS)  released final rules on transferability. The Inflation Reduction Act created two new credit delivery mechanisms—elective pay (otherwise known as “direct pay”) and transferability—that are enabling state, local, and Tribal governments; non-profit organizations; Puerto Rico and other U.S. territories; and many more businesses to take advantage of clean energy tax credits. 
The Inflation Reduction Act’s transferability provisions allow businesses to transfer all or a portion of any of 11 clean energy credits to a third-party in exchange for tax-free immediate funds, so that businesses can take advantage of tax incentives if they do not have sufficient tax liability to fully utilize the credits themselves. Entities without sufficient tax liability were previously unable to realize the full value of credits, which raised costs and created challenges for financing projects.

title: National Electric Vehicle Infrastructure (NEVI) Formula Program
description:
The U.S. Department of Transportation’s (DOT) Federal Highway Administration (FHWA) NEVI Formula Program provides funding to states to strategically deploy electric vehicle (EV) charging stations and to establish an interconnected network to facilitate data collection, access, and reliability. Funding is available for up to 80% of eligible project costs, including:

-The acquisition, installation, and network connection of EV charging stations to facilitate data collection, access, and reliability;
-Proper operation and maintenance of EV charging stations; and,
-Long-term EV charging station data sharing.

EV charging stations must be non-proprietary, allow for open-access payment methods, be publicly available or available to authorized commercial motor vehicle operators from more than one company, and be located along designated FHWA Alternative Fuel Corridors (AFCs). If a state and DOT determine that all AFCs in the state have been fully developed, then the state can propose alternative public locations and roads for EV charging station installation.

The focus includes solar PV technologies to support French industry, floating offshore wind, electricity grid management, and nuclear energy, such as Small Modular Reactors, through calls for proposals. The program also supports around 400 companies, aiding their projects with industrial potential in all renewable energy sectors, especially those involving highly innovative technologies, but also certain existing technologies.
policyType: [{"topic":"Technology R&D and innovation","family":"Resource push","name":"Grants","category":"Grants for R&D projects"}]

title: International collaborative projects as part of the national bioeconomy strategy
description: As part of the National Bioeconomy Strategy, Germany has issued a call for proposals for bioeconomy-related R&D grants for teams composed of German and non-EU international partners. Research institutions and private companies, especially small and medium-sized enterprises, are eligible to apply. This initiative aims to promote international partnerships to support the transition to a sustainable bio-based economy.
policyType: [{"topic":"Technology R&D and innovation","family":"Resource push","name":"Grants","category":"Grants for R&D projects (co-funded by more than one government)"}]

title: CoalCO2-X
description: The CoalCO2-X program is a collaborative mechanism co-funding a project involving three German and five South African partners, coordinated by Germany's Fraunhofer Institute. The program focuses on converting CO2 emissions from South Africa's coal-fired power plants into various commodity chemicals and fertilizers using green ammonia and hydrogen. By capturing and transforming CO2 and other pollutants, the program aims to reduce the environmental impact of these power plants and serve as a key enabler for the decarbonization of the chemical and energy sectors. The project is planned to be conducted between September 2022 and August 2025.
policyType: [{"topic":"Technology R&D and innovation","family":"Resource push","name":"Grants","category":"Grants for R&D projects (co-funded by more than one government)"}]

title: Off Grid Access to Electricity
description: India has funded projects through a call for proposals for electricity system-related grants aimed at R&D, standards, capacity building, and technical assistance, as part of one of Mission Innovation's challenges, with a total funding size of USD 5 million. The goal is to promote affordable and accessible clean energy from off-grid electricity for individuals and communities with no or limited access to grid-connected power. Project teams must include at least one Indian partner and one partner from another Mission Innovation country.
policyType: [{"topic":"Technology R&D and innovation","family":"Resource push","name":"Grants","category":"Grants for R&D projects (co-funded by more than one government)"}]

title: Technology Business Incubators
description: The Indian government supports selected not-for-profit Technology Business Incubators (TBIs) in various technology areas, including energy, through grants. This creates an independent channel for directing other policy measures to start-ups, allowing the incubators to choose how to support start-ups and reinvest proceeds. The Department of Science & Technology provides financial assistance of up to Rs. 20 million as grants in aid for seed support to suitable TBIs through calls. Eligible incubatee start-ups can receive support in the form of soft loans, equity, or a combination of these, in addition to business assistance services.
policyType: [{"topic":"Technology R&D and innovation","family":"Resource push","name":"Grants","category":"Grants to business incubators and accelerators"}]

title: Italian Hydrogen Research Strategy (SIRI)
description: Italian Hydrogen Research Strategy (SIRI) aims toenhance Italian competitiveness in hydrogen technologies and includes R&D targets, such as to reduce operating temperatures of solid oxide electrolysers from the current 750-800°C to 600°C.
policyType: [{"topic":"Technology R&D and innovation","family":"Socio-political support","name":"Targets","category":"Technology performance or cost targets"}]

title: ALCA-Next
description: ALCA-Next is a fund designed to reward promising research ideas in priority areas for carbon neutrality, with a budget of 1.6 billion yen for FY2024. The program focuses on exploring challenging key technologies that have not been actively researched by industries but have the potential to become innovative technology game-changers and improve technology readiness. Initially, the program will adopt multiple projects with relatively smaller budgets for a "small start" phase lasting 3.5 years. After this period, approximately one-third of the projects will be selected through stage-gate evaluations to receive increased funding, ensuring a continuous funding stream for projects that pass the evaluation.
policyType: [{"topic":"Technology R&D and innovation","family":"Resource push","name":"Grants","category":"Grants for R&D projects"}]

title: GteX
description:
GteX promotes R&D in designated technology areas critical to achieving industrial competitiveness and carbon neutrality by 2050. This initiative funds a 'team' approach to create consortia of academics and companies across various organizations and sectors in Japan for integrated R&D. Calls for proposals made in 2023 and 2024 focus on batteries, hydrogen, and biomanufacturing. The designated areas will be reviewed based on policies, industrial trends, and R&D trends as needed.
Under a project management system consisting of a program director, advisors, and appointed committees, the progress of projects is evaluated during their execution, and the continuation and funding of projects are reviewed accordingly. The fund amounts to 49.6 billion yen for the coming five years.
policyType: [{"topic":"Technology R&D and innovation","family":"Resource push","name":"Grants","category":"Grants for R&D projects"}]

title: Legislation on subsoil and subsoil use
description: Companies in the extractive industries must allocate 1% of their total annual income to R&D. To improve accountability and transparency, this was updated in 2021 with a government decision to allocate the 1% directly to the state budget for allocation to projects by the Ministry of Energy and the Ministry of Industry.
policyType: [{"topic":"Technology R&D and innovation","family":"Regulations","name":"Regulation","category":"R&D spending obligation"}]

title: Energy Innovation Companies
description: Target and funds to support 4 000 clean energy start-ups by 2025m including via a dedicated investment fund
policyType: [{"topic":"Technology R&D and innovation","family":"Resource push","name":"Finance","category":"Equity fund for start-ups"}]

title: Mission-Centric Strategic Roadmap for Critical and Emerging Technologies
description: The Mission-Centric Strategic Roadmap for Critical and Emerging Technologies identifies clear priorities for pan-government policies on R&D of strategic technologies to secure strategic advantages. It lists 16 key technologies where a fierce race for technological supremacy is taking place, including secondary batteries, advanced mobility, next-generation nuclear energy, advanced biotechnology, aerospace and marine technologies, and hydrogen. The roadmap also outlines mission strategies to be achieved by 2030 for these identified technologies, focusing on R&D investment milestones, international cooperation, talent acquisition, and improvement.
policyType: [{"topic":"Technology R&D and innovation","family":"Framework legislation","name":"Strategic plans","category":"Technology R&D roadmaps"}]

title: National Climate Technology Center
description: The National Climate Technology Center, part of the Korea Institute of Energy Research, serves as the national think tank for developing climate change technologies by establishing policies and strategies, creating master plans and technology maps, planning national R&D projects, managing R&D networks, and analyzing market and industry trends.
policyType: [{"topic":"Technology R&D and innovation","family":"Framework legislation","name":"Strategic plans","category":"Framework innovation strategy"}]

title: Special Act on National Strategic Technology Development
description: The Special Act on National Strategic Technology Development commits the government to formulating a five-year master plan for fostering and protecting national strategic technologies. This plan includes annual detailed implementation plans for each strategic technology field. Strategic technologies are identified and managed through consultations with relevant administrative agencies and deliberations by the designated Science and Technology Advisory Council. The development of these technologies will be supported by designated agencies and research institutions, the creation of regional technology innovation hubs to foster a research ecosystem, linking industries, and operating specialized educational institutions.
policyType: [{"topic":"Technology R&D and innovation","family":"Framework legislation","name":"Strategic plans","category":"Framework innovation strategy"}]

title: Mexican Energy Innovation Centers
description:
The Mexican Energy Innovation Centers (CEMIEs) are virtual hubs that bring together the best and most specialized departments from 120 higher education institutions, research centers, companies, and government entities. These centers focus on applied research and technological development in five key areas: bioenergy, geothermal, wind, marine energy, and solar energy.
Each center operates independently, guided by its medium and long-term scientific and technological plans and strategies, while they are supervised by the Ministry of Energy and the National Council of Science and Technology. Each center is coordinated by its own Steering Group and supported by various evaluation, monitoring, and follow-up committees.
policyType: [{"topic":"Technology R&D and innovation","family":"Knowledge management","name":"Networking and sharing","category":"Connecting innovators and potential customers"}]

title: Advisory on Innovation and Development
description: An account manager is assigned to every start-up that applies to Innovation Norway. These advisers help the start-ups navigate and understand the programmes offered by Innovation Norway (including grants and loans) to find the best match. Start-ups can apply any time of the year.
policyType: [{"topic":"Technology R&D and innovation","family":"Resource push","name":"Advice and services","category":"Advice on access to resources"}]

title: Gassnova SF
description: Gassnova SF is a state-owned enterprise owned by the Ministry of Energy. Gassnova Sf works to ensure that capture, transport and storage of CO2 (CCS) can become a relevant solution in mitigating climate change. The main goal is to promote cost-effective and future-oriented solutions for CCS. By facilitating technology development and sharing experience from developing the “Longship” CCS Project in cooperation with the industry players. Gassnova also acts as a strategic advisor to the Ministry of Energy, and its mandate is to share its expertise with subsequent projects and government agencies.
policyType: [{"topic":"Technology R&D and innovation","family":"Resource push","name":"Grants","category":"Funding for public research institutions"}]

title: SkatteFUNN R&D
description:
The SkatteFUNN R&D tax incentive scheme is a government program designed to stimulate research and development (R&D) in Norwegian trade and industry. The incentive is a tax credit and comes in the form of a deduction from a company’s payable corporate tax. To be eligible for the program, companies need to be based in Norway and liable to pay corporate tax to Norway. Furthermore, the company must seek to develop a new or improved product, service, or production through a dedicated R&D project that will generate new knowledge, skills, and capabilities within the company.

Most of the projects that utilize the scheme are small- and medium-sized enterprises. The largest thematic area is the energy system and utilization of energy sources. Most of the projects focused on utilizing energy sources are concentrated on offshore wind. Hydropower and solar power are also large areas, and there has been increased growth in projects within batteries and hydrogen.
policyType: [{"topic":"Technology R&D and innovation","family":"Incentives and investments","name":"Tax incentives","category":"R&D tax incentives"}]

title: Energy Market Authority's R&D Grants
description: Singapore's Energy Market Authority (EMA) works with successful applicants to competitive calls for grants to test-bed and develop innovative technologies and solutions to support the Singapore Energy Transition. Project topics funded to date to support Singapore's decarbonisation efforts include hydrogen and digital twin grids.
policyType: [{"topic":"Technology R&D and innovation","family":"Resource push","name":"Grants","category":"Grants for R&D projects"}]

title: Higher Education Innovation Fund
description: A fund, in partnership with UNDP, to make entrepreneurship services available in the higher education sector in South Africa, with an emphasis on job creation and spin-off companies.
policyType: [{"topic":"Technology R&D and innovation","family":"Resource push","name":"Advice and services","category":"Advice on access to resources"}]

title: Global Cleantech Innovation Programme for SMMEs in South Africa
description: The Global Cleantech Innovation Programme for SMMEs in South Africa (GCIP-SA) is part of a global initiative that aims to address the most pressing energy, environmental, and economic challenges of our time by promoting clean technology innovation and supporting Small and Medium-sized Enterprises and start-ups through an annual competition and a business accelerator program, where winners receive grants and business support. Specific areas of focus are energy efficiency, renewable energy, waste beneficiation (including e-waste), water efficiency and green buildings, green transportation, and environmental protection (air, sea, and land).
policyType: [{"topic":"Technology R&D and innovation","family":"Knowledge management","name":"Awards","category":"Awards to recognise innovation"}]

title: Department of Science and Innovation Strategic Plan
description: The Department of Science and Innovation's Strategic Plan sets the strategic agenda for R&D funding and budgets for key technology areas, including the bioeconomy, hydrogen, and fuel cells, for the period from 2020 to 2025. The plan was updated and revised in the 2022 annual report to adjust the technology focus areas and performance evaluation metrics. These metrics include scientific outputs such as expenditure on R&D, PhD graduates, publications, patent awards, and other indices, to identify key achievements and areas needing improvement. The plan also evaluates the impact on social challenges such as poverty, inequality, and unemployment.
policyType: [{"topic":"Technology R&D and innovation","family":"Framework legislation","name":"Strategic plans","category":"Framework innovation strategy"}]

title: Green Hydrogen Commercialisation Strategy
description: The Green Hydrogen Commercialisation Strategy guides a path and actions towards the commercialization of hydrogen technologies with targets for cost, production, and deployment. The strategy's pillars include investing in R&D and scaling up green hydrogen as a key contributor to early decarbonization  through grants, concessional debt, and contracts for difference, to ensure fair allocation of climate finance to this industry. The strategy also aims to establish South Africa as a global key producer through technological advancement and establishing a regulatory framework while fostering the local industry and ensuring a just transition.
policyType: [{"topic":"Technology R&D and innovation","family":"Framework legislation","name":"Strategic plans","category":"Technology R&D roadmaps"}]

title: Green Paper on the Advancement of New Energy Vehicles in South Africa
description: The Green Paper on the Advancement of New Energy Vehicles establishes a clear policy foundation that will enable the country to coordinate a long-term strategy that will position South Africa at the forefront of advanced vehicle and vehicle component manufacturing. Its focus includes ensuring R&D investments are strategically targeted at activities likely to give South Africa a competitive advantage in the transition from the internal combustion engine to electro-mobility solutions.
policyType: [{"topic":"Technology R&D and innovation","family":"Framework legislation","name":"Strategic plans","category":"Technology R&D roadmaps"}]

title: Just Energy Transition Framework
description: The Just Energy Transition Framework provides a structure to monitor the socio-economic impacts of the transition and to support the decarbonization of the mining and energy sectors in a socially acceptable manner while contributing to the economic development of the country in line with the Integrated Resource Plan (IRP) 2019 targets until 2030. The framework includes an investment plan for innovation and R&D with the aim of creating green and quality jobs.
policyType: [{"topic":"Technology R&D and innovation","family":"Framework legislation","name":"Strategic plans","category":"Framework innovation strategy"}]

title: Remarinos Demos
description: Funding to establish open access test facilities for marine renewables.
policyType: [{"topic":"Technology R&D and innovation","family":"Resource push","name":"Grants","category":"Grants for R&D projects"}]

title: Grants for projects of new business models in the energy transition
description: Competitive grants for companies to explore new business models for the energy transition, with scoring based on the level of innovation, the scalability, the team’s capabilities and contributions to just transitions.
policyType: [{"topic":"Technology R&D and innovation","family":"Resource push","name":"Grants","category":"Grants for new business scale-up"}]

title: CIUDEN
description: A public R&D institution to support and promote international cooperation through strategic research partnerships (with industry, SMEs, universities and research institutions) and establishment of test facilities.
policyType: [{"topic":"Technology R&D and innovation","family":"Resource push","name":"Grants","category":"Funding for public research institutions"}]

title: SOUR
description: Grants for small, unconventional, original, alternative and high-risk research projects that are potential game-changers for the Swiss energy system. They target technology topics that are complementary to the SWEET programme.
policyType: [{"topic":"Technology R&D and innovation","family":"Resource push","name":"Grants","category":"Grants for R&D projects"}]

title: Living Lab
description:
Living Lab is a network of thousands of households ready to participate in trials of new clean energy innovations. This network allows innovators without a large customer base to capture energy data from homes via smart meters, smart heating controls, battery storage, solar PV, electric vehicles and chargers, and heat meters.
The Living Lab combines network emulation and real-time simulations of future energy system scenarios, enabling the testing and analysis of innovative technologies' impact and performance under future market conditions. The lab can be used by all organizations, including small to large-scale companies, retailers, network operators, financial institutions, policymakers, and regulators.
In addition to product and service trials, participants can receive consultancy services from within the Catapult, an independent research and technology organization that runs the lab. These services include consumer insight, systems integration, data science, business model innovation, and expertise in markets, policy, and regulation. The program is managed with government funding.
policyType: [{"topic":"Technology R&D and innovation","family":"Knowledge management","name":"Networking and sharing","category":"Connecting innovators and testers"}]

title: Climate Innovation Pull Facility (CIPF)
description: Through pull finance, this facility will support innovation, scale up and market building for climate change mitigation solutions for developing country contexts, focusing on innovative clean energy technologies and business models in a small number of specific applications/sectors, where the evidence shows support is most needed. The planned facility is up to £185m, and subject to approvals. If agreed would be part of the Departments International Climate Finance portfolio and funded with Official Development Assistance (ODA).
policyType: [{"topic":"Technology R&D and innovation","family":"Market pull","name":"Public procurement","category":"Advance market commitments for products carrying technology risk"}]

title: Small Business Voucher Pilot Programme
description: Gives small businesses access to technical assistance from national labs. Small businesses in the clean energy sector can request assistance from a national lab, and if accepted, a voucher is issued that allows the applicant to access a unique skill or facility.
policyType: [{"topic":"Technology R&D and innovation","family":"Resource push","name":"Access to facilities","category":"Lab vouchers"}]

title: Regional Innovation Engines
description: Grants to educational institutions to improve the opportunities for spin-offs from their R&D, including training a local workforce.
policyType: [{"topic":"Technology R&D and innovation","family":"Resource push","name":"Education and training","category":"Professional / Vocational training and certification"}]

title: USPTO Climate Change Mitigation Pilot Program
description: The United States Patent and Trademark Office (USPTO) has launched the Climate Change Mitigation Pilot Program, which prioritizes the processing of patent applications related to technologies that reduce, remove, prevent, and/or monitor greenhouse gas emissions. This program aims to expedite the innovation process for climate change mitigation technologies. The USPTO will accept petitions under this program until either June 7, 2027, or when a total of 4,000 applications have been granted, whichever comes first.
policyType: [{"topic":"Technology R&D and innovation","family":"Knowledge management","name":"Intellectual property regimes","category":"Faster IP processing"}]

title: European Innovation Council (EIC)
description: The European Commission established the European Innovation Council (EIC) Fund in 2020 to make direct equity and quasi-equity investments in TRL 9 “European high-impact and deep-tech start-ups and scaleups” accepted into the EIC Accelerator. Investments are between EUR 0.5 million (USD 0.6 million) and EUR 15 million (USD 17 million), up to 25% of the voting shares, and with a relatively long time horizon of 7-15 years. Funds come from the Horizon Europe budget and the project represents a new means of using the EU R&D framework programme, alongside its traditional focus on grants. "Challenges" on specific topics are used to select recipients.
