title: Incentive for sustainable biomethane
description: The Ministerial Decree of 15 September 2022 aims to promote the incentives for biomethane fed into the natural gas network through capital support (equal to a maximum of 40% of the expenses incurred) and an energy account incentive (incentive tariff applied to the net production of biomethane). The following can benefit from the incentives provided by the Ministerial Decree newly built biomethane production plants, agricultural or waste-based, and interventions for the reconversion to biomethane (total or partial) of existing agricultural electricity production plants fuelled by biogas. It will be possible to submit the communication of entry into operation for the request for access to incentives only for plants that have been placed in a useful position in the rankings of public competitive procedures drawn up by the GSE on the basis of specific access requirements and priority criteria.

title: Social electricity bonus
description:
It is a compensation scheme for expenses incurred by domestic customers regulated by the Regulatory Authority for Energy, Networks and the Environment (ARERA). Families are entitled to it for reasons of economic hardship and/or physical hardship. All domestic customers can obtain the bonus, for a single gas supply (residence), not necessarily coinciding with the Municipality of residence, belonging to:
• a family unit with an ISEE indicator not exceeding 9,530 euros (15,000 for 2023);
• a family unit with more than 3 dependent children and an ISEE indicator not exceeding 20,000 euros;
• with a gas meter of class not exceeding G6
The social bonus is valid exclusively for supplies of natural methane gas distributed to the network and not for gas in cylinders or for LPG.

title: Discounts for Energy-Intensive Users
description: The Ministerial Decree of 21/12/2017 provides for incentives to reduce the tariff component (A3 now Asos) for energy-intensive companies defined as companies that consume > 1GWh and have an electrical intensity on the gross added value >20% or are particularly exposed to international competition (ceramics). Legislative Decree no. 131 of 29 September 2023 "DL Energia" reforms and redefines, with effect from 1 January 2024, the mechanism of incentives recognized in favor of energy-intensive companies. The contribution levels are applied according to two alternative methods: application of a discounted Asos rate (ex-ante mechanism), which consists in the reduction of the Asos rates on a monthly level. Application of a contribution percentage proportional to the gross added value of the company VAL, a mechanism that provides for the payment of two installments of the same amount to be paid in advance by 30 June and 31 December of year t, equal to 100% of the minimum contribution level provided for depending on the class of membership.

title: National Energy Income Fund
description: The National Energy Income Fund is a public incentive, aimed at low-income families, which allows the installation of photovoltaic panels on homes, with a contribution of up to 100% of the expense. The goal is to reduce the cost of bills, thanks to the self-production of electricity. The National Energy Income Fund was established with resolution no. 7 of 17 March 2020 of the Interministerial Committee for Economic Planning and Sustainable Development (CIPESS). On 27 December 2022, the Interministerial Committee for Economic Planning and Sustainable Development finalized the financial structure of the MASE, giving the green light to the transfer of 200 million from the Development and Cohesion Fund which will go to feed the National Energy Income Fund. The GSE is the managing body of the "National Energy Income Fund", established with the Ministerial Decree of 8 August 2023.

title: Hydrogen valleys
description: The investment aims to support the local production and use of green hydrogen in industry, SMEs and local transport, thus creating new hydrogen valleys (hydrogen districts), especially in Southern Italy, where hydrogen is produced from local renewable sources and used locally. The aim of the measure is to repurpose abandoned industrial areas into experimental units for the production of hydrogen in local RES plants, located in the same industrial complex or in neighboring areas. Through the implementation of the planned interventions, the aim is to incentivize the production of electrolytic hydrogen from renewable energy sources (pursuant to Directive (EU) 2018/2001) or from grid electricity, promote the reuse of unused industrial areas and foster the economic recovery of local economies. The total amount of the Investment is equal to 500 million euros.

title: Use of hydrogen in hard-to-abate sectors
description: The 2 billion euro investment aims to promote research, development and innovation in the field of industrial processes, in order to develop initiatives for the use of hydrogen in industrial sectors that use methane as a source of thermal energy (cement, paper mills, ceramics, glass industries, etc.). In particular, a specific tender is expected to be launched to support research, development and innovation in the steel production process through an increase in the use of hydrogen. The production of electrolytic hydrogen from renewable energy sources pursuant to Directive (EU) 2018/2001 or from grid electricity is also supported. Natural gas does not receive any funding under the project.

title: Diversification and strengthening of electrical interconnections
description: 'Adriatic link: CC connection between Abruzzo and Marche was authorized by decree of January 31, 2024, scheduled for operation in 2028. Adriatic backbone (Foggia – Villanova power line) is in the authorization phase with operation scheduled for 2028-30. Montecorvino – Avellino Nord – Benevento power line in the planning phase with operation scheduled for 2028/29. Reorganization of the northern Calabria network in the planning phase with operation scheduled for 2030. Aliano – Montecorvino electrode planned with operation scheduled for 2032. Northern Benevento area power line planned with operation scheduled for 2035.

title: Hydrogen backbone
description: The government plans to build 2300km of H2 pipelines (Hydrogen Backbone) with start of operation scheduled for 2030. The government is also investing in electrolysers in Sicily and Puglia for 1.7 GW of which 1.5 GW for injection into the Hydrogen Backbone, with start of operation scheduled for 2026-2031.

title: Hydrogen refueling stations
description: The aim is to promote the creation of refueling stations for testing hydrogen in road transport. At least 40 refueling stations will be developed, giving priority to strategic areas for road transport: along motorways, near ports and near logistics terminals.
policyType: [{"topic":"Fuels","family":"Incentives and investments","name":"Government spending in hydrogen","category":null}]

title: FER-X Decree
description: The Transitional FER-X Decree, effective from 28 February 2025, allocates €9.7 billion to support renewable energy plants in Italy with generation costs close to market levels. It offers 20-year Contracts for Difference (CfDs) for technologies like solar, wind, hydro, and biogas, with access via auctions for plants over 1 MW and direct access for smaller ones. The scheme includes regional and installation-specific bonuses, supports new builds and upgrades, and excludes projects already under construction or financially distressed companies. It runs until the end of 2025 or until a 3 GW cap is reached for small plants.

description: The measure is aimed at encouraging the reconversion of Italian refineries into biorefineries, in line with increasingly ambitious EU objectives and with the increase in domestic demand for advanced biofuels used both in blends with fossil products and in purity.

description: The ministerial decree promotes renewable thermal energy plants through competitive auctions. It offers financial incentives such as fixed tariffs or premiums, subsidies, and green certificates to support the development of technologies like biomass, geothermal, and solar thermal.

title: Consolidated Energy Law
description: On 30 December 2024, the Consolidated Law on Renewable Energy, Legislative Decree no. 190 of 25 November 2024, came into force, which regulates the administrative regimes for the production of energy from renewable sources. Regions and local authorities have 6 months to adapt to the new provisions, until 28 June 2025, being able to establish specific rules for the further simplification of the administrative regimes and/or raising the power thresholds envisaged, as an alternative to the application of this decree.

title: White Certificates - Energy Efficiency Certificates
description: White certificates are titles that certify the achievement of savings in end-use energy through interventions to increase energy efficiency. The interventions promoted mainly concern those carried out in the industrial sector, but also in other sectors such as network infrastructure, transport, civil and behavioral measures. The mechanism is based on an obligatory quota placed on energy distribution companies that can fulfill either by carrying out energy efficiency interventions or by purchasing certificates on the centralized GME market or through bilateral contracts with other entities (companies, ESCos, etc.) that have received certificates for the energy efficiency interventions carried out. The measure is regulated by the DM 21 May 2021 which modifies and updates the previous decrees that started the mechanism since 2005.

title: National Energy Performance Strategy
description: The National Energy Performance Strategy establishes a framework for long-term coordinated action to deliver the government’s vision that ‘all Australians enjoy the economic, climate and health benefits of improved energy performance’. The Strategy aims to improve energy performance outcomes for Australia’s businesses, households and the energy system, including through energy efficiency, electrification or fuel switching, and demand flexibility.

title: National Recovery and Resilience Plan (PNRR)
description: The PNRR outlines Italy's strategy to utilize approximately €191.5 billion in EU grants and loans, complemented by an additional €30.6 billion in national co-financing, totaling €222.1 billion. The implementation of the PNRR is set to continue through 2026, with periodic assessments and fund disbursements contingent upon the achievement of specified milestones and targets .

title: National Recovery and Resilience Plan/ Transition 4.0
description: Transizione 4.0 is a plan that aims to stimulate businesses (in particular micro, small and medium-sized businesses and innovative start-ups) to invest in innovation through tax breaks and relief. The main objective of the plan is to encourage investments in new machinery and devices with high technological content. The eligible goods also include solutions strictly connected to energy efficiency, such as: components, systems and intelligent solutions for the management, efficient use and monitoring of energy and water consumption and for the reduction of emissions and software, systems, platforms and applications for plant intelligence that guarantee energy efficiency and decentralization mechanisms in which the production and/or storage of energy can be delegated (at least in part) also to the factory.

title: Obligation to make the public lighting system more efficient
description: The intention is to build an energy efficiency program, starting first and foremost with public lighting. In this sector, the program will include a set of interventions, aimed at Local Public Bodies, aimed at accelerating the ongoing process for the replacement of light sources and the installation of consumption monitoring systems, together with a more efficient reprogramming of the hours of use. In this regard, the Budget Law for 2018 established that public bodies are required to upgrade public lighting systems by 31 December 2023, ensuring a reduction in electricity consumption of at least 50% compared to the average consumption in 2015-2016. The companies involved in the development of the interventions can take advantage of the incentives provided by the Revolving Fund for the support of companies and investments in research, where 300 million euros have been allocated for the granting of subsidized loans.

title: Program for the Energy Requalification of Central Public Administration Buildings (PREPAC)
description: The Interministerial Decree of 16 September 2016 defined the implementation methods of the Central Public Administration Energy Requalification Program (PREPAC), with a specific focus on the identification and selection of interventions eligible for funding and on the information needs of the PAs and technical assistance. To access the funding, the Public Administrations must develop intervention proposals for the energy requalification of buildings. The PREPAC program will continue in the period 2021-2030, taking into account the experience gained during the start-up phase of the mechanism.

title: Obligation for renewable integration in new or existing buildings
description:
Annex 3 of Legislative Decree no. 28 of 2011, transposing the RED Directive, identifies the obligations to integrate energy from renewable sources in new buildings or buildings undergoing major renovation, in force since 31 May 2012. The requirements are currently set in terms of percentages (increasing per year) of coverage with renewable energy sources of the thermal energy needs of the building. In particular, it is expected that in the case of new buildings or buildings undergoing major renovation, at least 50% of thermal energy consumption is met from renewable sources.
With the entry into force on 15 December 2021 of Legislative Decree no. 199 of 8 November 2021, which implements EU Directive 11/12/2018, no. 2001 (known as RED II), new provisions are introduced regarding renewable sources and new buildings or buildings subject to significant renovations. The Decree increases the coverage of energy consumption from renewable sources to 60% (up from the previous 50%). This percentage is valid for private buildings, and its achievement becomes mandatory 180 days after the date of entry into force, i.e. from 13 June 2022. For public buildings, the quota to be met is 65%.

title: Sustainable Urban Mobility Plans (PUMS)
description: Italy's Piani Urbani della Mobilità Sostenibile (PUMS) are strategic plans mandated for municipalities with populations over 100,000. Aligned with EU guidelines, PUMS aim to develop integrated, sustainable urban transport systems that enhance accessibility, reduce environmental impact, and improve quality of life. These plans emphasize active public involvement, coordination with urban and environmental planning, and measurable outcomes to foster inclusive, low-emission mobility solutions.

title: Development of LNG in maritime transport and port services
description: The measure aims to develop and promote the use of LNG for maritime and inland navigation and for port services. Among the various actions, it is expected: the issuing of tax relief rules for the construction of LNG depots and/or distributors in ports; the definition of suitable port tariffs to facilitate the use of LNG-powered maritime vehicles; agreeing with the EU on forms of financing aimed at the construction of LNG depots and vehicles in line with EU policies; incentives for LNG shipbuilding; removal of barriers, including authorizations, to the installation of infrastructure for the supply of LNG on the road network and within ports; facilitation of the supply phase by promoting the construction of small-scale coastal depots.

title: Incentive for non-photovoltaic renewable electricity sources
description: Through the decree of 23/6/2016, plants are incentivised based on the energy fed into the grid: those up to 1 MW with all-inclusive tariffs; those over 1 MW with an incentive equal to the difference between a reference tariff and the hourly zonal price of energy. Depending on the power of the plants, access to incentives is subject to the plants being registered in registers or participating in competitive auctions, while in the case of smaller plants access is direct. The competitive procedures (auctions, registers) are carried out in three different sessions, making approximately 5.4 GW of power available, of which 2.5 GW in auctions.

title: Agri-photovoltaic Park
description: The measure “Parco Agrisolare”, Mission 2 “Green revolution and ecological transition” of the PNRR, Component 1 “Circular economy and sustainable agriculture”, Investment 2.2, aims to support investments for the construction of photovoltaic solar electricity production plants in the agricultural and agro-industrial sector, excluding land consumption.

title: Identifying suitable areas for renewable resources
description:
The Ministerial Decree of 21 June 2024 (DM Suitable Areas), implementing art. 20, paragraphs 1 and 2 of Legislative Decree no. 199 of 2021, has the purpose of:
a) identifying the distribution among the regions and autonomous provinces of the national objective for 2030 of an additional power equal to 80 GW from renewable sources compared to 31 December 2020, necessary to achieve the objectives set by the PNIEC and respond to the new objectives resulting from the implementation of the "Fit for 55" package, also in light of the "Repower EU" package;
b) establishing uniform principles and criteria for the identification by the regions of the surfaces and areas suitable and unsuitable for the installation of renewable energy plants functional to the achievement of the objectives referred to in letter a), in line with the principle of technological neutrality

title: National Recovery and Resilience Plan/ Green Islands
description:
The PNRR provides for an investment (3.1), called "Green Islands", for the financing and implementation of projects in the fields of energy (such as renewable sources, the electricity grid, energy efficiency), water (such as desalination), transport (cycle paths, zero-emission buses and boats) and waste (e.g. separate waste collection) in 19 small islands not connected to the mainland.
The beneficiaries of the intervention are the 13 municipalities of the 19 small islands referred to in Article 2, paragraph 1 of Annex 1 Part A of Ministerial Decree no. 390, dated 25 November 2021.
The total amount of the Investment is equal to 200,000,000 euros; to access the resources, it is necessary to carry out at least three of the types of eligible interventions on each island.

title: Simplification of authorisation procedures for renewable energy source plants
description:
Legislative Decree 387/2003 first, Legislative Decree 199/2021 then, are the main provisions that have defined and updated the cornerstones of the authorization framework envisaged for renewable energy plants, with differentiated procedures by type of plant. The legislator has intervened on the permitting of FER-E plants in order to simplify environmental procedures, reduce procedural times, improve coordination and definition of the powers of intervention of the various administrations (e.g. the role of the Ministry of Culture), homogenise and digitise the procedures envisaged at territorial level, and therefore ultimately facilitate the installation of new renewable energy plants, the repowering of existing plants, the creation of storage systems. 

The last of these acts of reorganization and rationalization of the permitting for FER is constituted by the Consolidated FER Law, approved with Legislative Decree no. 190 of 25 November 2024.

title: Australian Government National Hydrogen Strategy 2024
description: The National Hydrogen Strategy, released in September 2024, provides a framework to guide Australia’s production, use and export of hydrogen an aims at positioning Australia to become a global hydrogen leader. The 2024 National Hydrogen Strategy represents a comprehensive formal review and update of the 2019 National Hydrogen Strategy. The new strategy focusses on accelerating clean hydrogen industry growth, through increasing global cost competitiveness by supporting industry development at scale.

title: First Nations Renewable Hydrogen Engagement Fund
description: The Government has established a new $4 million Fund to deliver support to First Nations communities to engage effectively with renewable hydrogen projects. The Fund provides resourcing for community-developed projects aimed at delivering a wide range of local benefits, including but not limited to specialised training and resources, cultural and technology knowledge exchange, and engagement within and between communities and project developers.

title: Agri-photovoltaic Decree
description: The PNRR includes a specific measure (M2C2.1) for the development of agrivoltaics. The investment measure specifically includes: i) the implementation of hybrid agriculture-energy production systems that do not compromise the use of land dedicated to agriculture, but contribute to the environmental and economic sustainability of the companies involved, also potentially enhancing water basins through floating solutions; ii) monitoring of the implementation and their effectiveness, with the collection of data on both photovoltaic systems and on underlying agricultural production and activity, in order to evaluate the microclimate, water savings, recovery of soil fertility, resilience to climate change and agricultural productivity for the different types of crops. The objective of the investment is to install a production capacity from agrivoltaic systems of 1.04 GW, which would produce approximately 1,300 GWh per year, with a reduction in greenhouse gas emissions estimated at approximately 0.8 million tonnes of CO2.

title: Auctions for large plants with mature technologies
description: In line with what was implemented in the Ministerial Decree of 4/7/2019, a measure is envisaged with competitive tender mechanisms for mature technologies (e.g. wind, photovoltaic, hydroelectric), adopting a neutral approach between groups of technologies with similar structures and cost levels, possibly with safeguard mechanisms where technologies deemed necessary to achieve the objectives were systematically unsuccessful, it being understood that one of the purposes of this mechanism is to accompany market parity. The tenders will be aimed at stipulating contracts for difference based on the overall value of the tariff recognized following the procedure, according to the "two-way" criterion (i.e. recognition of the difference between the tariff and the market price of electricity where the difference is positive; restitution by the producer if the same difference is negative).

title: Promotion of PPAs for large renewable energy sources plants
Australian Regional Hydrogen Hubs Program
description:
The Australian Government is investing around $500 million to support the development of hydrogen hubs in regional Australia. This investment will fund the implementation of hubs as well as design and development studies for future hubs. Hydrogen hubs are a key element of the 2024 National Hydrogen Strategy. They support the clean hydrogen industry to grow and scale, to enable our net zero transition. 

Regional Hydrogen Hubs Program: 7 Hydrogen Hubs (located in Gladstone, the Hunter Valley, Bell Bay, Port Bonython, Kwinana and the Pilbara) and 9 Development & Design projects announced for funding across regions of Australia ($441.8 million total). An additional Hydrogen Hub in Townsville, Queensland has also been launched, with approximately $70 million committed as part of the 2022-23 October Budget).

title: National Recovery and Resilience Plan / District heating
description:
To exploit the potential of district heating in the technological mix necessary to achieve environmental objectives in the heating and cooling sector, Component 3 - Measure 3 of Mission 2 of the PNRR finances projects relating to the construction of new networks or the extension of existing networks, in terms of customers supplied, including the plants for their power supply. To this end, priority is given to the development of efficient district heating, i.e. based on the distribution of heat generated from renewable sources, waste heat or cogenerated in high-performance plants.
The investment objective is aimed at the development of 330 km of efficient district heating networks and the construction of plants or connections for the recovery of waste heat for 360 MW, assuming that 65% of the resources are allocated to the networks (cost 1.3 million per km) and 35% is dedicated to the development of new plants (cost 0.65 million per MW).

title: 2024-25 Budget allocation: Support for Australian Renewable Energy Agency to accelerate renewable energy uptake and energy decarbonisation
description:
In the 2024–25 Budget, the Australian Government committed $7.1 billion for budgeted programs to be administered by ARENA including:

$1.9 billion boost to ARENA’s baseline funding
$2 billion for round two of the Hydrogen Headstart program
$1.7 billion for the Future Made in Australia Innovation Fund
$1 billion previously announced for the Solar Sunshot program
$500 million for the Battery Breakthrough Initiative

title: Social gas bonus
description:
Compensation scheme for expenses incurred by domestic customers regulated by the Regulatory Authority for Energy, Networks and the Environment (ARERA). Families are entitled to it for reasons of economic hardship and/or physical hardship. All domestic customers can obtain the bonus, for a single gas supply (residence), not necessarily coinciding with the Municipality of residence, belonging to:
• a family unit with an ISEE indicator not exceeding 9,530 euros (15,000 for 2023);
• a family unit with more than 3 dependent children and an ISEE indicator not exceeding 20,000 euros;
• with a gas meter of class not exceeding G6
The social bonus is valid exclusively for supplies of natural methane gas distributed to the network and not for gas in cylinders or for LPG.

title: Overcoming the National Single Price (PUN)
description: Considering the management complexities and the constraints that the PUN introduces into the electricity market, especially in view of the growing integration of European markets based on market coupling and greater participation of demand in the market, the usefulness of overcoming the PUN in the medium term is confirmed, evaluating the evolution of future network structures also in relation to the effects of the growing penetration of generation from renewable sources and foreseeing the preventive implementation of specific interventions aimed at reducing network congestion and/or possible competitive disadvantages of specific territorial areas.

title: Market liberisation - role of consumers
description: The liberalization of the final sales markets, started in 2003 for gas and in 2007 for electricity, will be completed in 2024.

title: Internal market reform
description: The measure is aimed at adapting the electricity market to the widespread use of distributed renewable generation plants and promoting a more aware and active electricity demand. Among the lines of action, it is foreseen: the overcoming of the PUN and the development of European market coupling, the development of futures markets and ancillary services.

title: Plan for the replacement of school buildings and energy requalification
description: Mission 2 “Green revolution and ecological transition” – Component 3 “Energy efficiency and building redevelopment” of the National Recovery and Resilience Plan provides for investments (investment 1) for the replacement of school buildings and their energy redevelopment. The measure aims to build new schools, through building replacement, to have more innovative, sustainable, safe, inclusive and energy efficient buildings.

title: Energy efficiency improvement of judicial buildings
description: The PNRR measure (M2C3I1.2) aims to intervene by mid-2026 on 290,000 m2 of offices, courts and judicial citadels, making 48 structures more efficient, technologically improving the provision of services and recovering the historical heritage that often characterizes the administration of Italian justice.

title: Simplification and acceleration of procedures for the implementation of energy efficiency measures
description:
The measure (PNRR M2C3 - Reform 1.1) aims to promote the rapid energy conversion of the real estate stock, encouraging deep requalifications and transformation into "nearly zero-energy buildings" (nZEB), in line with the strategy for the energy requalification of the national real estate stock. The measure is aimed at overcoming those barriers that are not economic in nature and that reduce investment choices in energy requalification interventions of buildings or that slow down the execution of the works. The measure includes the following interventions:
1) Ref 1.1.a: Launch of the national portal for the energy efficiency of buildings
2) Ref 1.1.b: Training and information plan for energy efficiency
3) Ref 1.1.c: FNEE reform
4) Ref 1.1.d: PREPAC reform
5) Ref 1.1.e: authorization simplification (simplified CILA - Simplifications Decree 2021)
6) Ref 1.1g: Construction waste management ministerial decree
2) Ref 1.1.f: quota reduction in condominium meetings (August 2020 Decree and LB 2021)

title: Improve energy efficiency in cinemas, theaters, and museums
description: 300 million euros which is allocated through the National Recovery and Resilience Plan (M1C3 – Investment 1.3 “Improving energy efficiency in cinemas, theaters and museums”) aims to improve the energy efficiency of buildings related to the cultural and creative sector, which are often located in old and obsolete structures. Italian public and private cinemas, museums and theaters will have a reduced environmental impact and will help the recovery of the construction sector.

title: National CER Roadmap
description: On 19 July 2024, Energy Ministers agreed to publish the National Consumer Energy Resources (CER) Roadmap. The roadmap sets out an overarching vision and plan to unlock CER at scale across Australia. The roadmap's implementation plan outlines priority reforms through four workstreams: consumers, technology, markets, power system operations. The roadmap provides a national approach to reforms to ensure Australians are able to harness the full potential of CER. If consumer resources are coordinated effectively, they can help lower costs for all consumers by offsetting the need for billions of dollars in grid-scale investment. The Energy Ministers agreed to the development of the roadmap in November 2023. The CER Working Group, made up of state and territory government officials, produced the roadmap.

title: Aggregation of generation plants and users
description:
Legislative Decree 102/2014 (transposed from EU Energy Efficiency Directive (2012/27/EU)) provides for the possibility of creating aggregates of generation plants and users for access to the aggregate offer and to provide flexibility services, entrusting them to entities capable of effectively guaranteeing such aggregation. Network operators must define the rules for organizing the participation of these new formations.
The Authority has activated pilot projects that will allow the acquisition of useful elements for the reform of dispatching and concern the participation in the dispatching services market, also in aggregate form, of demand and production units that are not currently authorized, including production units powered by non-programmable renewable sources.

title: Capacity market
description: The Capacity Market is a mechanism for regulating the capacity of the electricity market, which provides remuneration for operators based on the energy they are able to make available on the grid. The objective of this system, defined by the Ministerial Decree of 28 June 2019, is to guarantee the availability of electricity production capacity in the long term, in order to cope with the evolution of consumption. The actors most involved are operators who own gas-fired thermoelectric plants but also renewable sources, including for example pumped hydroelectric plants or those with an accumulation system. This new market represents an important contribution to guaranteeing long-term price signals and conditions of adequacy of the electricity system consistent with the decarbonisation objectives.

title: Research and development on hydrogen
description:
PNRR measure (M2C2, Measure 3; investment 3.5). The measure aims to improve knowledge of hydrogen-related technologies in all phases (production, storage and distribution), experiment and create prototypes for the industrialization phase to progressively reduce costs and increase competitiveness. The planned interventions are:
• production of green and clean hydrogen;
• development of technologies for storage and transport and for transformation into other derivatives and green fuels;
• development of fuel cells and mobility applications;
• improvement of the resilience and reliability of hydrogen-based infrastructures

title: Single model for photovoltaic systems integrated on building roofs
description:
For the construction, connection and operation of small photovoltaic systems integrated on the roofs of buildings, a single model can be used to send to the network operator (which interfaces with the competent bodies in the respective areas, such as the Municipality and the GSE).

This goes in the direction of simplifying the process for installing photovoltaic systems on buildings and reducing the obligations for proponents.

The model was initially designed for systems up to 20 kW, then it was extended under certain conditions up to 50 kW and up to 200 kW. The first provision was the Ministerial Decree of 19 May 2015; the latest provision is Ministerial Decree no. 297 of 2 August 2022.

title: New charging stations in cities and highways to encourage the use of electric vehicles
description: The PNRR, mission 2 investment 4.3, plans to build the infrastructure needed to promote the development of electric mobility, increase the number of zero-emission vehicles (public and private) and reduce the environmental impact of transport, creating over 20,000 rapid charging points on highways and in urban centers by 2026.

title: Electric charging facilitation
description:
Resolution 541/2020/R/EEL of ARERA describes the general terms of this innovative experiment, the operational management of which has been entrusted to the Energy Services Manager (GSE).
From 1 July 2021 to 30 June 2027, it is possible to charge your electric vehicle with a power of approximately 6 kW available, at night, on Sundays and on other holidays, without having to request an increase in power from your electricity supplier, and therefore without having to bear additional fixed costs due to the increase in power.
The aim of the experiment is to promote the "smart" charging of electric vehicles in a way that is compatible with the characteristics of existing electricity networks, exploiting the potential offered by electronic meters and the most advanced charging devices, which are able to regulate the charging speed based on commands provided by external actors (for example by aggregators or by the local distributor, subject to the customer's authorization), or automatically.

title: National electricity system research
description:
The National Electricity System Research (RdS) was conceived with the aim of promoting research and development activities in the electricity sector and improving its cost-effectiveness, safety and environmental compatibility.

Decree no. 139 of 12 April 2024 reforms the management mechanisms of System Research in the electricity sector and applies to the activities relating to the 2025-2027 Three-Year Plan and to those of subsequent Plans. For the activities relating to the previous three-year plans, the Decree of 16 April 2018 applies.

The current decree defines the new methods for the selection and financing of research projects to be admitted to the allocation of the funds referred to in Article 11 (Research Fund), paragraph 1, of the Decree of 26 January 2000 and the methods for verifying the progress of the activities and the results achieved.

title: Future Made in Australia - Guarantee of Origin (Renewable Electricity Guarantee of Origin)
description:
The Future Made in Australia (Guarantee of Origin) Act 2024 received Royal Assent on 10 December, 2024. It passed through Parliament on 28 November 2024. The Acts establish the voluntary Guarantee of Origin (GO) scheme. The GO scheme is an Australian Government-backed emissions accounting framework. This framework supports the development of Australia’s green industries. The GO scheme empowers Australian producers to make confident, objective and credible claims about: the renewable electricity they generate or use, and the products they make.

It supports consumers of renewables and low-emission products with a publicly accessible record. This provides Australian producers access to emerging domestic and export low-emissions markets.

Australian businesses register and apply for two types of GO certificates under the scheme. Product GO (PGO) certificates display the emissions intensity of particular commodities. Renewable Electricity GO (REGO) certificates contain information about when, where and how renewable electricity was produced. The GO scheme commences with renewable electricity and hydrogen. It expands to products such as low carbon liquid fuels and green metals.

title: National Recovery and Resilience Plan/ Renewables and batteries
description:
As part of Mission 2 – Component 2 “Renewable energy, hydrogen, network and sustainable mobility” – Investment 5 “Development of international, industrial and research and development leadership in the main transition supply chains”, Investment 5.1 “Renewables and batteries”, with a financial endowment of 1 billion euros, aims to develop industrial supply chains in the photovoltaic, wind and battery sectors, through the following three sub-investments:
-  “PV technology (PhotoVoltaics)”: supports private investments in the production sector of innovative high-performance photovoltaic panels (with a financial endowment of 400 million euros);
- “Wind industry”: supports private investments in the production sector of new-generation, medium-large size wind turbines (with a financial endowment of 100 million euros);
- “Battery sector”: supports private investments in the battery production sector (with a financial endowment of 500 million euros)

title: National Recovery and Resilience Plan / Electrolysers
description: PNRR Measure (Mission 2 Component 2, Investment 5.2). The measure, with a financial endowment of 450 million euros, was prepared for the construction in Italy of a large industrial plant for the production of electrolysers, the electrochemical devices that allow water molecules to be broken by separating hydrogen from oxygen.

title: Energy cluster
description: The Italian Ministry of University and Research (MUR) focuses on fostering technological innovation and industrial competitiveness through national technological clusters. These clusters, established in 2012, bring together public and private entities to enhance research, training, and technology transfer in strategic areas such as aerospace, agrifood, green chemistry, and smart communities. They aim to mobilize excellence, optimize resource use, attract investments, and promote sustainable economic growth. Subsequent clusters were added in 2016 to cover cultural heritage, design, marine economy, and energy, aligning with national and European research priorities.

title: National Renewable Energy Priority List
description: The Priority List was developed in collaboration with states and territories to provide a focal point for targeting government resources and support to priority renewable energy projects across Australia as they navigate regulatory planning and approval processes.

title: Cheaper Home Batteries Program
description:
The $2.3 billion Cheaper Home Batteries Program will support Australian households and small businesses with a discount on the cost of installing small-scale battery systems. The program aims to:

  • help households to make the most of cheap and clean solar power by storing it for when it is needed
  • reduce costs for everyone - not just those who install a battery - because it means less expensive gas power generation, poles and wires.
From 1 July 2025, the program will provide around a 30% discount on the upfront cost of installing eligible small-scale battery systems. The discount will be based on the battery’s usable capacity and will gradually decrease until 2030.

title: Electric buses
description:
Measure M2C2, Investment 5.3 of the PNRR, with a financial allocation of 300 million euros, promotes the technological transformation of the bus production chain to ensure the production capacity needed to replace outdated public transport with new electric and connected models, reducing the environmental impact of public transport.
Following the changes made to the PNRR, 25 million euros are earmarked for the implementation of the intervention within the allocation of investment M7-I12 of the PNRR of a total of 100 million. The allocation replaces the one initially allocated for the measure, equal to 80 million of a total of 300, within measure 5.3 of the PNRR M2C2 "Energy transition and sustainable mobility".

title: Facilitations supporting research and development projects for the reconversion of production processes within the circular economy
description: The intervention of the Sustainable Growth Fund for research and development projects in the field of the circular economy, activated with the decree of 11 June 2020, supports research, development and testing of innovative solutions for the efficient and sustainable use of resources, with the aim of promoting the conversion of production activities towards a circular economy model in which the value of products, materials and resources is maintained for as long as possible, and waste production is reduced to a minimum.

title: National Recovery and Resilience Plan/ Support for start-ups and venture capital active in the ecological transition
description:
The PNRR 5.4 investment “Support for start-ups and venture capital active in the ecological transition”, with a financial endowment of 250 million euros in grants, is aimed at stimulating the growth of the Italian innovation ecosystem, with particular attention to the ecological transition sector, through direct and indirect venture capital investments.
The investment involves the creation of a Green Transition Fund (GTF), managed by CDP Venture Capital SGR S.p.A. and endowed with 250 million euros. The GTF’s investment strategy is aimed at the sectors of renewables, circular economy, mobility, energy efficiency, waste disposal, energy storage and similar.

title: National Recovery and Resiliency Plan/ Hydrogen experimentation for road and railway transport
description: The measure aims to convert non-electrified railway lines with high passenger traffic and a strong use of diesel trains to hydrogen, such as in Lombardy, Puglia, Sicily, Abruzzo, Calabria, Umbria and Basilicata. The most advanced projects, those in Valcamonica and Salento, involve the integrated testing of production, distribution and purchasing of H2 trains.

title: National Plan for the reconversion of greenhouse systems into agro-energy sites and forms and methods of connection with the PNRR
description: The national plan for the reconversion of greenhouse plants into agro-energy sites, as established by Legislative Decree 17/2022, art. 11-bis, converted into law with Law 7 April 2022, n. 34, aims to combat environmental and landscape degradation resulting from the progressive structural deterioration of the national greenhouse heritage and to promote its reconversion for efficient reuse.

title: Guarantees of Origin
description:
Adaptation of the discipline of the Guarantees of Origin (GO), currently regulated by the Ministerial Decree of 14 July 2023, to the provisions of the Ministerial Decree of 7 August 2024 which establishes the national certification system for the sustainability of biofuels, the certification of renewable fuels of non-biological origin and that of fuels from recycled carbon. Extension of the discipline to the production of thermal and/or cooling energy from renewable sources.

For each MWh of renewable electricity fed into the grid by IGO qualified plants, the GSE (Energy Services Manager) issues a GO title. The Ministerial Decree of 14 July 2023 regulates the mechanism of guarantees of origin (GO), which provides for the issuing, recognition and cancellation of guarantees of origin to produce energy from renewable sources, biomethane and hydrogen.

title: Electrification of port berths for the reduction of ship emissions during berthing (cold ironing)
description: The investment is planned to create a network to supply electricity to docks in port areas, along with the necessary infrastructure to connect this network to the national electricity transmission system.
policyType: [{"topic":"Power","family":"Incentives and investments","name":"Government spending in electricity networks","category":null}]

title: Interventions on grid climate resilience
description: The measure is aimed at carrying out preventive interventions on 4,000 km of infrastructure to increase the resilience of the electrical system, in order to reduce the duration and extent of power outages in the event of extreme weather events.

title: Interventions for the environmental sustainability of ports (Green Ports)
description: The aim of the investment is to make port activities more compatible and harmonious with urban activities and life, thanks to interventions to reduce energy consumption and increase environmental sustainability, also using renewable energy. These measures will contribute to reducing greenhouse gas emissions.

title: Smart grid
description: The measure aims to improve the reliability, safety and flexibility of the national energy system, so as to bring the amount of energy coming from renewable energy plants (FER) to at least 4,000 MW, convert at least 1,500,000 users to electrification of consumption and open up new scenarios in which prosumers, energy consumers-producers, can also play a role.

title: Partnerships - Horizon Europe
description: The measure aims to support research, development and innovation projects identified within the framework of the Horizon Europe programme, because transnational research initiatives can be a driver of development for research, development and innovation activities in the strategic sectors for the recovery of the Italian economy.

title: National recovery and resilience plan/ Funding for industrial transition
description: The Industrial Transition Support Fund aims to support the adaptation of the Italian production system to EU policies on the fight against climate change. Investment programs must be aimed at pursuing, exclusively, an improvement in terms of environmental protection of business processes.

title: CO2 capture and transport for hard-to-abate sectors
description: In accordance with the provisions of paragraph 3 of Article 7 of Legislative Decree no. 181 of 9 December 2023, converted with amendments by Law no. 11 of 2 February 2024, the Ministry of the Environment and Energy Security is preparing a study on the national supply chain for the capture, transport and storage of CO2 (CCS). The study is preparatory to the technical and economic regulation of the CCS sector.

title: Operating incentive mechanisms to promote renewable hydrogen production
description: Article 11, paragraph 2, of Legislative Decree no. 199 of 2021, provides for the issuance of a ministerial decree aimed at supporting the production of hydrogen of renewable origin intended for use in the transport sector and in the hard-to-abate sectors, through the recognition of the contribution to the operating account.

title: Reform of the authorization system for hydrogen production plants
description: The reform consists in the entry into force of a legal framework to promote hydrogen as a renewable energy source.

title: Incentive for centralized storage under Futures Storage Market (MACSE)
description: The Futures Storage Market (MACSE) allows Terna to procure electricity storage capacity through new large-scale storage facilities. The measure is intended to ensure the safety and adequacy of the system in the face of increased penetration of non-programmable renewables.

title: National portal on building energy performance
description: The update of Legislative Decree 19 August 2005, n. 192 with Legislative Decree 10 June 2020, n. 48, which implements European Directive 2018/844/EU, introduces further indications for the promotion of the improvement of the energy performance of buildings, taking into account external local and climatic conditions, as well as the requirements relating to the climate of internal environments and the cost-effectiveness of the planned actions, optimising the ratio between costs and benefits for the community. This updated Decree, in Article 4-quater, introduces the National Portal on the energy performance of buildings. At present, the Portal provides an overview of ENEA statistics relating to the energy performance of buildings divided by year.

title: Presidential Decree 74/2013 on the management of heating systems: minimum requirements and management of heating systems
description:
Presidential Decree no. 74/2013 defines the general criteria for the operation, maintenance and inspection of heating systems, as well as the professional requirements of experts and bodies to be entrusted with the inspection tasks of the same, introducing, among other measures, the specific obligation relating to energy efficiency control for winter air conditioning systems with a power greater than 10 kW, or 12 kW for summer air conditioning systems, according to specific time frequencies. Furthermore, the provision defines the operating limits of heating systems for winter air conditioning, establishing the periods and methods for switching them on and off.

As provided for by Article 6, paragraph 1, of Legislative Decree 10 June 2020, no. 48, implementing Directive (EU) 2018/844 on the energy performance of buildings, Presidential Decree 74/2013 is currently being updated. The draft decree updates the general criteria provided for by Presidential Decree 74/2013, in order to minimize the administrative burdens on building owners and tenants, ensure optimal environmental, energy and safety performance of small-scale heating systems, and simplify administrative procedures.

description: The Commonwealth Government has been negotiating bilateral Renewable Energy Transformation Agreements (RETAs) with states and territories since late 2023. RETAs build on collaboration through the National Energy Transformation Partnership and support common goals in the energy transition. Through RETAs, governments commit to working together to deliver new renewable generation and storage to support achieving 82% renewable electricity nationally by 2030, including through agreed minimum allocations of capacity for states as part of the Capacity Investment Scheme.

title: Home Energy Ratings Disclosure Framework
description:
| The Home Energy Ratings Disclosure Framework sets out a national approach to implementing disclosure schemes across Australia. It does this by:
 - defining how energy ratings are provided to households at the point of sale or lease
 - outlining policy parameters for disclosure schemes that governments can implement
 - giving guidance on developing a supportive market environment. 
 Providing a home’s energy performance rating at the point of sale or lease will help Australians choose a more comfortable and energy efficient home that is cheaper to run.
 A pilot to test implementation of the Disclosure Framework is due to commence in the second half of 2025.

title: Minerals Strategy for New Zealand and Critical Minerals List
description:
The Minerals Strategy adopts a lens out to 2040, focusing New Zealand’s approach to the development of our minerals estate, with a delivery roadmap to get us there. It outlines actions that will be taken to position the minerals sector to deliver for New Zealanders, focused on three key outcomes of productivity, value, and resilience. The Strategy is guided by overarching principles to honour Te Tiriti o Waitangi obligations and responsible practices.

There are 37 minerals included on the Critical Minerals List, which identifies minerals that are essential to New Zealand’s economy. New Zealand has the potential to produce 21 of these, which will enable us to contribute to the growing critical minerals market as a trusted and reliable partner, particularly in the support of global mineral supply chains of minerals needed for clean energy technologies.

title: Updated Slovak National Energy and Climate Plan
description:
The final updated NECP 2021-2030 was approved by the Slovak Government on April 2, 2022 and subsequently was submitted to the European Commission on April  15, 2025. 
The NECP update states that the Slovak Republic aims to achieve climate neutrality by 2050. By 2030, the Slovak Republic must reduce its emissions from sectors covered by the Effort Sharing Regulation by at least 22.7% compared to 2005 levels. The NECP update also includes a net removal target of 0.5 million tCO2e by 2030 under its obligations under the Land Use, Land Use Change and Forestry (LULUCF) Regulation. Other Union-level targets contributing to that climate target are at least 42.5 % of the share of energy from renewable sources (‘RES’) in gross final consumption of energy, the national energy efficiency contribution, a 11.7 % reduction in primary and final energy consumption and electricity interconnectivity is set more than 50%.

description:
The Integrated National Energy and Climate Plan (NECP) serves as the national strategic guidance tool that integrates energy and climate policy with a time horizon extending to 2030, in accordance with national and European regulations.
Spain's indicative energy planning, as detailed in the Integrated National Energy and Climate Plan (NECP), outlines the country's targets for energy generation and supply, including the massive integration of renewable energy sources and the modernization of the electricity grid. title: Royal Decree 36/2023, of 24 January, establishing a system of Energy Efficiency Certificates
description:
On 26 January 2023, came into force, the Royal Decree 36/2023, of 24 January, establishing a system of Energy Efficiency Certificates (CAE System in Spain) in development of the provisions of article 71.2 of Spanish Law 18/2014, of 15 October and transposing the European Directive on Energy Efficiency (EED) into national law. The CAE System is a mechanism designed for accrediting the achievement of energy savings with the aim of contributing to the fulfilment, by 2030, of the final energy savings targets set by the EED.
The CAE System  emerge to facilitate investment in energy efficiency technologies and foster a market in this sector. This system applies to investments in every sector, not only private or public, but also industry, buildings, transport or service sector.

This includes improving consumer protection, creating the conditions to grow the market, lowering emissions, improving the performance of heat networks, and building up skills in the sector to encourage investment and jobs growth.

  •  Lowering energy costs for all
  •  Completing the Energy Union
  •  Attracting investments and ensuring delivery

title: Public Charge Point Regulations
description:
The Public Charge point Regulations 2023 came into force in November 2023, mandating simpler pricing information. From November 2024, these regulations added further requirements, including to achieve an average reliability of 99% across their network of chargeponts of 50 kW and above, offer contactless payment options, and give access to free helplines.
 
 From 2025,  the Public Charge Point Regulations will require that chargepoint operators open up their networks to roaming partners, further simplifying the charging experience. The UK Government anticipates that measures will help consumers get free, up-to-date and reliable information at all times, and enable them to access chargepoints through a variety of providers and apps, helping to improve their charging experience as the public charging network grows.

title: Sustainable Aviation Fuel (SAF) Mandate
description:
The Sustainable Aviation Fuel (SAF) Mandate is the UK's key policy to decarbonise aviation fuel by mandating the supply of sustainable aviation fuels. It secures demand for SAF by obligating the supply of an increasing amount of SAF in the overall UK aviation fuel mix, and incentivising SAF supply through award of tradeable certificates with a cash value.
 
 It started in 2025 at 2% of total UK jet fuel demand, increasing linearly to 10% in 2030 and then to 22% in 2040. From 2040, the obligation is currently set to remain at 22% of total UK jet fuel demand.

title: Sustainability certification of biofuels
description: With the Ministerial Decree of 14/11/2019, the national certification system for the sustainability of biofuels was established. The system aims to measure and verify the environmental performance of fuels during all the main phases of the product life cycle, production, fuel production and end use, including raw materials.

title: Sustainable Aviation Fuel Revenue Certainty Mechanism
description: The UK Government has introduced legislation to support sustainable aviation fuel production in the UK through an industry-funded revenue certainty mechanism, to encourage investment in the construction of sustainable aviation fuel plants across the UK. The Bill was introduced on 14 May 2025, with an expectation for legislation to be in place by the end of 2026.

title: Infrastructure reinforcement (regional railway transport)
description: The measure is to strengthen interconnected regional railway lines to improve safety levels, strengthen the railway system used as local public transport, and include interventions to strengthen the connection of regional lines with the national high-speed network.

The UK Government and the UK's Civil Aviation Authority are now working with National Air Traffic Services with a shared ambition for the UK Airspace Design Service to be in place by the end of 2025.

title: Maritime Decarbonisation Strategy
description:
The UK's Maritime Decarbonisation Strategy was published on 25 March 2025 and sets out the Government's plans for decarbonisation of the domestic maritime sector. It includes goals of zero emissions by 2050, a 30% reduction in lifecycle greenhouse gas emissions by 2030, and an 80% reduction by 2040 - compared to 2008 levels. 
 
 The Strategy set out a range of policies that will support meeting the goals including: 
 - Implementing fuel regulations;
 - Introducing emissions pricing;
 - Taking action on emissions at berth;
 - Addressing emissions from smaller vessels;
 - Improving energy efficiency.

title: Incentive for collective self-consumption groups and energy communities
description: This measure concerns renewable energy communities and self-consumer groups, regulated by Legislative Decree 162/19 (Article 42bis) and the related implementing provisions, such as Resolution 318/2020/R/eel of ARERA and the Ministerial Decree of 16 September 2020 of the MiSE, which defined the incentive tariffs. title: Regulation of sustainability requirements and verification of biofuels, liquid bio-energy carriers and fuels produced from biomass
description: According to Government Decree 821/2021. (XII. 28.) between 1 January and 31 December 2025 the mandatory blend rate of biofuels is 8.9%, of which the mandatory minimum share of advanced biofuels, biogas is 1% in 2025 and 3.5% in 2030.

title: Reform of legislation on the installation of wind farms
description: Enactment of a legislative amendment that removes unnecessary restrictions on the installation of wind turbines in areas with wind energy densities greater than 460 W/m.

title: Solar Plus Programme
description: The program, with a budget of 75 billion HUF, supports households subject to gross settlement starting from January in the establishment of solar panels and energy storage. According to the call for proposals, the program covers two-thirds of the family's costs, up to a maximum grant value of 5 million HUF. The support can be provided for investments carried out on the permanent residence family house or in a building section of a row house, semi-detached house, or a condominium with up to 6 apartments. Eligible expenses include application administration, planning, permit costs, equipment and material costs, and installation labor. Only one grant can be awarded per property, exclusively for new investments; therefore, it cannot be used for expanding, replacing, or renovating existing systems.

title: Support for the purchase of electric vehicles for companies
description: Hungary offers various incentives for Battery Electric Vehicles (BEVs), including exemptions from company car tax, registration tax, annual vehicle tax, and property transfer tax for green plate vehicles. Businesses can deduct costs related to electric charging infrastructure and 50% of VAT on BEV operating expenses. A €79.1 million subsidy programme supports BEV purchases, with grants ranging from €5,500 to €10,500. Additionally, Hungary is expanding its EV charging network with a €72 million programme, installing over 100 public charging points outside Budapest, and encouraging the integration of solar panels and battery storage. Most municipalities also offer free public parking for green plate vehicles.

description: This is a position paper outlining the strategy of the Austrian government to push Geothermal Energy (petro- and hydrothermal). Legal framework adoption, research gaps and funding instruments need rapid adoption to push geothermal energy production.

title: Renewable Energy Communities
description: Energy communities allow collective use and distribution of locally generated renewable energy among participants in a community to increase efficiency and sustainability. Following the Clean Energy Package for all Europeans (2019), the necessary energy policy framework was implemented in Austria in 2021 through the Renewable Energy Expansion Act (EAG) and an amendment to the Electricity Industry and Organization Act (ElWOG).

title: Electricity Sector Act 2010 (ElWOG 2010)
description:
The Electricity Security of Supply Strategy (Elektrizitäts Versorgungssicherheitsstrategie, E-VSS) was drawn up in accordance with section 88a of the Electricity Sector Act 2010 (ElWOG 2010) and identifies fields of action and measures for the long-term resilience of the electricity system. One of the most important measures is the transformation of the energy system towards indigenous renewable energy sources. Other areas include: flexibility and storage to provide for times when sun and wind do not complement each other optimally; optimising the grid infrastructure to keep pace with dynamic developments; and adapting to the effects of climate change on energy production.
The strategy was developed by the Ministry in consultation with the Regulator E-Control and the Control Area Manager Austrian Power Grid AG, and in cooperation with all relevant stakeholders in the Austrian electricity market, on the basis of the ElWOG 2010 and published in 2024. Due to the high demands on system stability and security of supply, the measures will be regularly evaluated on a yearly basis in the form of a status report. This will identify any need for adjustments and provide valuable insights for a future revision of the strategy. The E-VSS will be updated every five years.

title: Risk-Preparedness Plan for the Electricity Sector
description: The plan contains a presentation of the most relevant electricity crisis scenarios as well as national and regional measures to prevent and manage them. The plan follows the regulation (EU) 2019/941 of the European Parliament and of the Council of 5 June 2019 on risk-preparedness in the electricity sector and repealing Directive 2005/89/EC.

title: Climate-friendly district heating and district cooling systems
description:
Since summer 2022, there has been the possibility of funding of “optimisation measures in climate-friendly district heating networks”. This exists if at least 50% of the heat originates from renewable sources, waste heat or 75% of the heat originates from cogeneration plants or 50% of it from a combination of the abovementioned sources. For the climate-friendly networks concerned, a decarbonisation path must be submitted, demonstrating how a proportion of 60% renewable energy will be achieved in the district heat supply by 2030 and a proportion of 80% by 2035. The funding in this area amounts to 20% of the eligible costs. It should be taken into account that the minimum investment sum is set at €50,000.
In 2023, eight projects were funded. A funding cash value of €2.3 million triggered the investment volume of approximately €9.4 million. The annual CO₂ savings thereby achieved amount to approximately 8,050 tonnes.

title: Zero-Emission Commercial Vehicles and Infrastructure (ENIN)
description: Zero-Emission Commercial Vehicles and Infrastructure (ENIN) is a funding program initiated by the Austrian Federal Ministry for Climate Action, Environment, Energy, Mobility, Innovation and Technology (BMK). Its primary objective is to significantly increase the proportion of zero-emission commercial vehicles within Austria’s vehicle fleet. By transitioning from conventionally fossil-fueled commercial vehicles to zero-emission alternatives—such as electric vehicles, overhead line trucks, or hydrogen fuel cell-powered vehicles—while ensuring the exclusive use of renewable energy, the program aims to drastically reduce greenhouse gas emissions.

With an initial budget of €7 million, LADIN is part of Austria’s comprehensive strategy to promote sustainable transport and complements other national initiatives like EBIN and ENIN.

title: Bill 5, Protect Ontario by Unleashing our Economy Act, 2025
description:
Bill 5, titled the Protect Ontario by Unleashing our Economy Act, 2025, is an Ontario law principally aimed at accelerating the permitting of infrastructure and mining projects in the province. Through this bill, Ontario aims to shorten the approval process currently averaging 15 years, in line with Canada’s efforts to increase the supply of critical minerals.

Bill 5 creates governmental authority to designate “special economic zones” where companies and projects can be exempted from provincial and municipal regulations. It also establishes a new mining permitting model that aims to cut government review time by half, grants the government the power to deny mining leases to protect strategic supply chains, and replaces the Endangered Species Act, 2007 with a new Species Conservation Act, 2025, among other provisions.

The statute could minimise regulatory costs and delays by exempting projects under the “special economic zones” designation, fast-tracking resource development in Ontario.

The reference warming trajectory for adaptation to climate change so far anticipates an increase in the average temperature in mainland France of 4°C by the end of the century. With regard to vitally important operators (OIVs), the transposition into French law of Directive (EU) 2022/2557 on the resilience of critical entities will make it possible to integrate these challenges into entity planning through the revision of national security directives.

title: Strategic contract for the French automotive industry
description: As a continuation of the 2018–2022 Strategic Contract for the Automotive Industry, the new 2024–2027 contract was signed in early May 2024. The objectives set by the General Secretariat for Ecological Planning (SGPE), in line with France’s commitment to reduce its greenhouse gas emissions by 50% between 1990 and 2030, translate for the automotive sector into several key targets to be achieved by the end of the contract period: quadrupling the sales of fully electric passenger cars, multiplying by six the sales of fully electric light commercial vehicles, doubling the market share of electric buses by 2027, and reaching at least 25,000 charging points of 50 kW or more by the end of 2027 along major national roads and in urban charging hubs.

title: Regulation (EU) 2023/1804 Alternative Fuels Infrastructure Regulation
description: This regulation establishes binding targets for the deployment of publicly accessible recharging and refueling infrastructure across the EU. It aims to ensure the development of a dense, interoperable, and user-friendly network to support the transition to zero-emission mobility. Starting from 2025, fast charging stations (≥150 kW) must be available every 60 km along the core TEN-T road network for passenger cars, with higher capacity requirements by 2030. For heavy-duty vehicles, charging hubs with a minimum total power output must be deployed every 120 km from 2025 and increase significantly by 2030. The regulation also sets targets for hydrogen refueling stations and mandates clear rules on payment methods, price transparency, and real-time availability of charging points to improve user experience and confidence.

title: Benefit-in-Kind (BIK) Advantages for Electric Vehicles
description: The benefit-in-kind taxation for company cars has been significantly reduced for electric vehicles (EVs) to encourage their adoption. According to the updated provisions under the 2024 Finance Act and reinforced by the PLF 2025, the taxable benefit for fully electric vehicles is capped at a lower value compared to internal combustion engine vehicles. From 2025/02/01, the taxable benefit value for electric company cars that are eligible to the environmental score is limited to 30% of the vehicle’s running costs, compared to 50% for other cars. This measure aims to reduce the fiscal burden on employees using EVs, accelerating the green transition of company fleets.

This tax targets companies with large fleets, incentivizing the replacement of polluting vehicles by zero- and low-emission alternatives. The tax imposes higher rates on fleets that do not meet progressive environmental performance thresholds, based on CO₂ emissions and vehicle types. The evolving framework encourages companies to integrate more electric and hybrid vehicles to reduce their tax liability, supporting national climate goals.

title: Exceptional tax deduction for acquiring or leasing new low-emission vehicles
description: Under Article 39 of the French General Tax Code, companies can benefit from an exceptional tax deduction—known as “suramortissement”—when investing in new low-emission heavy-duty vehicles (electric or hydrogen). This measure allows businesses to deduct more than the asset’s standard depreciation from their taxable income, helping offset the higher purchase cost of cleaner technologies. As revised by the 2025 Finance Act, the deduction now applies to the additional cost of zero-emission vehicles compared to conventional ones, with rates depending on vehicle weight. The scheme runs until 31 December 2030 and supports the transition to cleaner fleets by improving the financial viability of sustainable vehicle investments.

title: Standardised energy savings certificate (CEE) operation sheets
description: Several standardised operations sheets (fiches d’opérations standardisées) were introduced under the French Energy Savings Certificates (Certificats d’économies d’énergie – CEE) scheme as of January 1st, 2025, to support the deployment of electric vehicles. These sheets define eligible actions and corresponding energy savings, allowing obligated parties (mainly energy suppliers) to offer financial incentives or “CEE bonuses” to beneficiaries. The new operations include the purchase or long-term lease of new electric vehicles (both light and heavy-duty), as well as electric retrofit operations. These measures are accessible to private individuals, legal entities, and local authorities, and aim to reduce the upfront cost of electric mobility by leveraging the energy savings generated.

title: Tariff for use of the public electricity network for charging infrastructure
description: The Mobility Orientation Act stipulates that the maximum amount covered by the Tariff for use of the public electricity network (TURPE) is set at 75% for requests for connection to the electricity network submitted to the project owner before December 31, 2025, for the connection of public electric and plug-in hybrid vehicle charging infrastructure installed in service areas on expressways and motorways. A decree of May 12, 2020 provides for such a reduction in connection costs for IRVEs and extends the deadline to December 31, 2025 for service areas on expressways and motorways. Another decree of February 6, 2023 increases this reduction in connection costs to 75% until the end of 2025 for IRVEs included in a validated charging infrastructure master plan (SDIRVE).

description: The purpose of this Law is to mitigate the negative socio-economic impact related to the increase in energy resource prices on the welfare of low-income and moderately low-income household.  The Law prescribes the State aid measures that mitigate the negative impact caused by the exceptional increase in energy resource prices on low-income and moderately low-income households and the conditions by which the aid for the reduction of payments for such consumed energy resources is applied to such households.

title: Law on the Vehicle Operation Tax and Company Car Tax
description: The Law on the Vehicle Operation Tax and Company Car Tax stipulates that lower tax rates are applied to vehicles with lower emissions.

title: Public Transport Concept 2021–2030
description: The use of clean vehicles is promoted in public transport services. In Latvia, starting from August 2021, uniform quality standards for regional public transport services are gradually being implemented, setting minimum EURO classes (not lower than Euro IV) and maximum vehicle age. Some of the buses are specially adapted for the transport of passengers with mobility impairments, as well as equipped with bicycle racks or are emission-free transport.

title: Law on the Road User Charge
description: Latvia has adopted Law on the Road User Charge to introduce a road user charge - a specified amount payment of which confers the right for a vehicle to use for a given period the road infrastructure mentioned in Annex 1 of Law on the Road User Charge. The road user charge rate in Latvia depends on the emission limits for the vehicle engine, the laden weight of the vehicle and the period of using roads.

title: 5th Basic Science and Technology Master Plan
description: The 2023-2027 Korean Basic Science and Technology Master Plan identifies 12 national strategic technologies, including batteries, nuclear power, and hydrogen. It sets out different coordination approaches and legal frameworks for implentation, including R&D strategies, strategic investments and plans for responding to new information and evaluating achievements.
