title: Hazardous and Other Wastes (Management and Transboundary Movement) Second Amendment Rules, 2025
description:
The Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change has issued amendments to the Hazardous and Other Wastes (Management and Transboundary Movement) Rules, 2016 to come into effect on 1 April 2026.

The amendment introduces Extended Producer Responsibility (EPR) for scrap of non-ferrous metals, defined to mean aluminium, copper, zinc or their alloys. 

The amendment covers manufacturers, producers, collection agents, refurbishers and recyclers of non-ferrous metals and introduces the following obligations on these stakeholders:
  • Producers are required to ensure collection, transport, and recycling of scrap of non-ferrous metals. They must also meet a specified recycling target in respect of their products, including by purchasing EPR certificates from registered recyclers. The recycling target by weight starts at 10% in 2026–2027, rising to 75% by 2032–2033.
  • Manufacturers are required to collect scrap of non-ferrous metals and waste generated during manufacturing and ensure its recycling or disposal. They must also use domestically recycled materials for the manufacture of new products as per specified minimum use rates.
  • Collection agents are required to collect end of life scrap of non-ferrous metals from manufacturers, producers, bulk consumers and supply it to the registered recycler. 
  • Refurbishers may collect scrap or used products of non-ferrous metals and their components, consumables, parts or scrap and ensure its refurbishing in an environmentally sound manner. Waste generated during refurbishing is to be handed over to a recycler or disposal facility.
  • Recyclers are required to ensure environmentally sound storage, transportation, and recycling of scrap of non-ferrous metals and dispose of the residue generated during recycling in accordance with prevalent rules. 
  • Bulk consumers are required to set up collection points to facilitate collection and hand over scrap to registered recyclers, refurbishers, producers or collection agents.

Other key highlights of the amendment include:
  • Mandatory Registration: All stakeholders are required to register on a portal maintained by the Central Pollution Control Board. The portal would track EPR certificates and transactions, act as a repository for returns and reports, and be the platform for EPR certificate trading.
  • Reporting: All stakeholders are required to maintain records as specified and file regular reports with respect to their EPR compliance. 
  • Penalties: Non-compliance with the rules may result in revocation of registration, imposition of environmental compensation and / or legal action including imprisonment up to 5 years or fine up to EUR 1 000 or both (with additional fines if the contravention continues).

  • Passenger automobiles models from 2017 to 2025: CO2e emission target values will be reduced on average by 5% annually initially using the 2016 model year as the reference.
  • Light trucks: CO2 emission targets values will be reduced by 3.5% per year for models from 2017 to 2021, then by 5% per year for models from 2022 to 2025.

title: Clean Industry State Aid Framework (CISAF)
description:
The new policy aims to simplify state aid rules, building on the now-expired Temporary Crisis and Transition Framework (TCTF). Unlike the TCTF, this scheme would be permanent, with no deadlines for granting aid or starting projects.

RFNBO projects could receive up to 45% of eligible costs, rising to 55% for medium-sized and 65% for small companies. Industrial decarbonization projects, including hydrogen, could get up to 50%.

Electrolyzer manufacturing aid depends on location: up to 35% (max €175M) in disadvantaged areas, and up to 15% (max €75M) elsewhere.

title: Third auction of European Hydrogen Bank (EHB)
description: Up to EUR 1.1 billion tender to be launched in Q3 2025. EUR 400 million will be exclusively allocated to RFNBO, EUR 400 million will be open to both RFNBO and low-carbon electrolytic hydrogen that meets the 70% GHG emissions reduction threshold, EUR 200 million will be open to both RFNBO and low-carbon hydrogen that is used in the maritime sector. Grant will be for 10 years, without indexation, at least 75% of the electrolyzers (the individual components, not the entire plant) must originate in a country different than China, 8% completion guarantee, maximum of EUR 200 million to be granted per bid, no offtake restrictions (other than the EUR 200 million for the maritime sector), pay as bid, ceiling price of EUR 4/kg, maximum time for reach FID is 2.5 years after signing the grant agreement and 5 years to start operations.

title: Hydrogen Mechanism (platform to support market development and for supply-demand connection)
description:
The H2 Mechanism aims to accelerate hydrogen and derivative markets (including ammonia, methanol, and eSAFs) to support industrial and transport decarbonization. It targets infrastructure developers and financiers, offering a transparency and matchmaking platform—no funding is provided.

It will run 3–4 rounds per year, with separate calls for supply and demand. Demand will be aggregated by location to help suppliers identify opportunities.

The platform offers three services: connecting supply and demand, gathering interest in infrastructure and storage, and linking to financial support. Only European offtakers can register on the demand side, while all producers can join on the supply side.

Registrations opened in July 2025, with operations expected to start in September.

The ministry’s plan envisions more than half of South Korea’s coal-fired thermal power plants, or at least 24, using a fuel mix consisting of 20 percent ammonia as early as 2030. By 2035, local gas-fired thermal power plants will use a mix of liquefied natural gas and 30 percent hydrogen. The role of the Office is to advance all aspects of hydrogen projects and facilitate hydrogen’s role across British Columbia’s energy systems. title: Planning for hydrogen network development
description:
In October 2024, the BNetzA approved plans for a 9040 km to be gradually in operation from 2025 to 2032. The feed-in and exit capacity are 100 GW and 87 GW respectively once the network has been fully developed. Hydrogen demand by 2032 is expected (by FNB) to be 191 TWh/a with a network capacity of 278 TWh/a by the same year. The network also includes 470 km of distribution pipelines. The share of repurposed pipelines is 56%. The total cost of the network is estimated to be EUR 18.9 billion. The roll-out plan will be reviewed every 2 years via the network development plan process fpr natural gas and hydrogen.

The length of the network has decreased over time with the original version from 2023 having 11200 km and the one from July 2024 having 9667 km. The decrease from July 2024 is due to 313 km from withdrawal of regional distribution networks and 293 km that were either redundant or provided connection to individual companies.

description: From January 2025 to April 2025, the GSO proposal was open for consultation (shipper in this context refer to gas TSOs). The GSO is intended to be the long-term funding mechanism for initial hydrogen production projects. It may also fund further hydrogen projects, subject to future decisions on the hydrogen programme and its funding arrangements. Prior to the GSO’s implementation, HPBM payments are intended to initially be funded by the government. The GSO will initially be placed on licensed gas shippers in Great Britain only. The government may consider the potential expansion of the GSO to NI gas suppliers in the future, subject to further engagement with relevant stakeholders and decisions on the funding of future hydrogen projects. The GSO is expected to be introduced in 2027, subject to legislation being in place. The government estimates that about GBP 150 million per year will be needed to fund HAR1 projects from 2028. HSBM: For geological hydrogen storage (e.g. salt caverns). Uses a Cap and Floor model. Final design expected in 2025, targeting up to two projects by 2030.

title: Methodology to determine the regulated asset base of the network
description: The Belgian energy regulatory (CREG) has established a methodology for calculating the value to be included in the regulated asset base in the event of the purchase by the hydrogen transport network manager of a pipeline for which there is already a valid transport authorisation. The CREG methodology for valuing existing pipelines acquired for hydrogen transport in Belgium is based on the fair value principle. This means the value included in the regulated asset base (RAB) is determined primarily by the price paid for the asset or its fair market value, reflecting the economic benefit the asset provides in its current or optimal use. The methodology applies only to acquisitions of pipelines with valid transport permits, including those under the 1965 gas law. The methodology is effective from 1 August 2024
policyType: [{"topic":"Fuels","family":"Infrastructure","name":"Other infrastructure policies","category":"Hydrogen"}]

title: Land lease incentives for hydrogen plots
description:
Reduced land fees stated in the questionniare as: 80% discount during development phase and 100% discount during contruction phase. ICV incentive fee to decrease with increase level of Oman share
[August 2025] Fiscal incentives for Round 3 include 90% land lease fees reduction during development, early year royalty relief and corporate tax exemption for up to 10 years
policyType: [{"topic":"Fuels","family":"Resource push","name":"Administrative measures","category":"Hydrogen"}]

title: UBA (German Environment Agency) RFNBO recognition to contribute to GHG quota
description: The 37th Ordinance for the Implementation of the Federal Immission Control Act (37. BImSchV) is an ordinance on the offsetting of electricity-based fuels, co-processed biogenic oils and RFNBOs against the GHG Quota for the transport sector as defined in the Federal Imissions Control Act (BImSchG)​. The latest revision (approved by Parliament in March 2024) of the 37th BImSchV expands the scope of fuels that can be counted towards the GHG reduction quota to include RFNBO. The EU delegated acts to Art. 27 (2023/1184) and Art. 28 (2023/1185) are nationally implemented through the revision. For RFNBOs a multiplier of 3 was introduced.
policyType: [{"topic":"Fuels","family":"Market pull","name":"Mandates and quota","category":"Hydrogen"}]

title: Public hydrogen utility (California)
description: Californian cities of Lancaster and Industry have launched together a public hydrogen utility (called First Public Hydrogen) that would act as a bridge between producers and public agencies that may otherwise be too small to pursue their own supply. The utility is a joint power authority which allows government bodies to operate as a stand-alone structure. The utility will buy the hydrogen at wholesale prices and sell to individual consumers. The utility aims to sign its first customer agreement in January 2025 with delivery starting within 24 months
policyType: [{"topic":"Fuels","family":"Regulations","name":"Market formation regulations","category":"Hydrogen"}]

title: Financing of the hydrogen network
description:
A two-tier tariff system was adopted:

Regional clusters – tariffs set individually to reflect varying early-stage network costs and users
National infrastructure – broader, unified tariff structure
This approach ensures cost reflectivity during the development of small, diverse hydrogen networks.
policyType: [{"topic":"Fuels","family":"Infrastructure","name":"Other infrastructure policies","category":"Hydrogen"}]

title: Amendments of the Electricity Supply Act
description:
Two changes relevant for hydrogen:

Refunds for PtX systems (paragraph 4(b) and (c)): Pilot plants using renewable energy (up to 200 MW) benefit temporarily if no electricity is re-fed into the grid.
Partial exemption for hydrogen storage used as electricity storage (Article 14a, paragraph 4(a)): Grid operators must reimburse usage fees for electricity that is stored and later fed back into the grid.
Amendments are expected to be fully in place by 2026.
policyType: [{"topic":"Fuels","family":"Resource push","name":"OPEX support","category":"Hydrogen"}]

title: Royal Decree 445/2024: Simplified environmental assessment elgibility
description: Purpose of the Decree is to identify sectors and projects subject to a simplified environmental assessment necessary for permitting. Hydrogen production from electrolysers is one of them
policyType: [{"topic":"Fuels","family":"Resource push","name":"Administrative measures","category":"Hydrogen"}]

title: Hanseatic Hydrogen Center for Aviation and Maritime
description: The Hanseatic Hydrogen Center for Aviation and Maritime (H2AM) has received funding notice in March 2025, with a volume of about EUR 70 million. The technology center shall be established in Hamburg, Bremen/Bremerhaven and Stade and focuses on aviation and maritime technologies.
policyType: [{"topic":"Fuels","family":"Resource push","name":"Grants for R&D projects","category":"Hydrogen"}]

title: Funding Guideline Offshore Electrolysis
description: Germany’s funding guidelines for offshore electrolysis projects support the development of innovative technologies adapted to challenging marine conditions, where components previously tested on land require further adaptation. The scope includes both offshore electrolysis systems and associated infrastructure. Project selection follows a two-stage process: the first stage evaluates proposals based on the lowest capital expenditure (CAPEX), while the second stage involves a qualitative assessment to determine final funding decisions.
policyType: [{"topic":"Fuels","family":"Regulations","name":"Market formation regulations","category":"Hydrogen"}]

title: First amendment to Energy Industry Act (EnWG)
description: First amendment to The Energy Economy Act regulates the initial approval of the hydrogen core network by the Federal Network Agency (Bundesnetzagentur, BNetzA).  The hydrogen core network shall comprise key hydrogen infrastructure projects that are to be operational by 2032. All German regions are to be taken into account. The hydrogen core network is modeled  by (gas) transmission system operators (TSOs). The TSOs' results is subjected to broad consultation with the public, the federal states and various market players. The final design of the network will be approved by the Federal Network Agency
policyType: [{"topic":"Fuels","family":"Infrastructure","name":"Planning","category":"Hydrogen"}]

title: Second amendment to Energy Industry Act (EnWG)
description:
Second amendment to the Energy Economy Act further sets the basis for financing of hydrogen infrastructure via hydrogen network tariffs. For an interim phase an amorization account is established to prevent that high initial tariffs slow down the hydrogen infrastructure development. The law creates the legal basis for integrated network development planning for hydrogen and natural gas. In addition to the planning and construction of the hydrogen core network, this is an important further step towards a rapid ramp-up of the hydrogen network infrastructure.  This will ensure close dovetailing of the grid development processes for hydrogen and natural gas as well as better synchronization with electricity grid development planning.
The law sets also the basis for the BNetzA to set regulations regarding to hydrogen grid balancing and accounting base model and the basic model and processing of network access (WaSabi and WaKandA).
policyType: [{"topic":"Fuels","family":"Infrastructure","name":"Other infrastructure policies","category":"Hydrogen"}]

title: National Quality Policy
description: The Revised National Quality Policy emphasizes the development of a robust hydrogen economy as a key component of its strategy. It aims to establish high standards for hydrogen production, storage, and distribution to ensure safety, efficiency, and environmental sustainability. The policy sets goals to promote innovation, enhance infrastructure, and foster international cooperation in the hydrogen sector.
policyType: [{"topic":"Fuels","family":"Regulations","name":"Market formation regulations","category":"Hydrogen"}]

title: Net-Zero Domestic Harbour Craft Target
description: In support of Singapore’s 2050 national net-zero target, the Maritime and Port Authority of Singapore (MPA) will require all new harbour craft operating in our port waters from 2030 to be  fully electric, be capable of using B100 biofuel, or be compatible with net-zero fuels such as hydrogen. MPA is developing hydrogen value-chains to offer zero-emission fuel solutions for international shipping and plans to power Tuas Port operations with hydrogen and other low or zero-carbon energy sources by 2050. These initiatives align with Singapore’s commitment to decarbonizing the maritime industry and supporting global climate goals.
policyType: [{"topic":"Fuels","family":"Regulations","name":"Market formation regulations","category":"Hydrogen"}]

title: Environmental Protection Act
description: With the revision of the CO2 Act adopted by Parliament on 15 March 2024, Article 35d of the Environmental Protection Act was also revised. Among other things, this links the placing on the market of renewable fuels to compliance with ecological requirements. Furthermore, the article gives the Federal Council the authority to also set ecological requirements for the placing on the market of low-emission fuels (including hydrogen)
policyType: [{"topic":"Fuels","family":"Regulations","name":"Market formation regulations","category":"Hydrogen"}]

title: Hydrogen Skills and Standards for Heat programme
description: The Hydrogen Skills and Standards for Heat program aims to develop technical standards and training specifications for hydrogen gas installations, enabling the safe repurposing of existing natural gas systems for hydrogen use. The program’s goals include defining criteria for hydrogen-safe equipment, designing new hydrogen-safe infrastructure, and training a competent workforce of hydrogen gas installers. This initiative supports future hydrogen trials and explores hydrogen as a potential decarbonization pathway, contributing to the UK’s Net Zero Innovation Portfolio.
policyType: [{"topic":"Fuels","family":"Regulations","name":"Market formation regulations","category":"Hydrogen"}]

title: ÖVGW H E510 guideline
description: The ÖVGW H E510 guideline focuses on the design, construction, and testing of hydrogen refueling stations, emphasizing safety and technical standards for handling hydrogen. It allows for up to 10% hydrogen blending with natural gas in the existing gas grid, ensuring compatibility and safety. The guideline aims to support Austria's transition to a hydrogen-based energy system, with goals to reduce carbon emissions and enhance energy sustainability. Quantitative targets include maintaining the integrity of the gas infrastructure and ensuring safe operation at the specified blending limit
policyType: [{"topic":"Fuels","family":"Regulations","name":"Market formation regulations","category":"Hydrogen"}]

title: Hydrogen Infrastructure Network Plan (Établissement de réseaux de transport d'hydrogène)
description: (Bill 8298) Luxembourg's strategy for establishing hydrogen transport networks, emphasizing the importance of hydrogen for decarbonizing the economy. Key goals include creating a legal framework for hydrogen infrastructure, granting at least one network management license, and ensuring interconnections with neighboring countries. a procedure for the designation of a hydrogen network operator is foreseen. The National Regulatory Authority is mandated to regulate the future hydrogen market. Targets are set to increase hydrogen consumption from 15 GWh (fossil) to 230 GWh (renewable) by 2030, with significant investments planned to support this transition
policyType: [{"topic":"Fuels","family":"Infrastructure","name":"Planning","category":"Hydrogen"}]

title: Incentives for hydrogen storage
description: White paper estimating the storage needs (2-7 TWh by 2030 and 76-80 TWh by 2050) suggests some of the incentives that could be used including CfDs, investment guarantees and direct grants.
policyType: [{"topic":"Fuels","family":"Infrastructure","name":"Other infrastructure policies","category":"Hydrogen"}]

title: Planning of the national hydrogen network
description: Plan to build a 2600 km hydrogen network with FID in 2027 and starting operations in 2030. The estimated investment is EUR 2.6 billion (USD 2.95 billion). A call for interest was launched in 2023 with results from around 650 projects indicating an electrolysis capacity of 23.3 GW and hydrogen production of 2.5 Mtpa (out of which 1 Mtpa would be for domestic demand) by 2030. In April 2025, an engagement plan for public participation was launched, which will be open for 18 months
policyType: [{"topic":"Fuels","family":"Infrastructure","name":"Planning","category":"Hydrogen"}]

title: Hydrogen transmission tariffs
description: The Dutch energy regulator, ACM, published a market report in May 2025 with an assessment of the hydrogen transmission tariffs. From 2033 at the latest, ACM will set tariffs based on actual incurred costs. Before that period, some of the options to deal with the low utilisation from early stages are to use an intertemporal cost allocation (i.e. spreading the cost recovery for the network over time), direct government subsidies to the network operators and indirect government support through, for example, loan guarantees
policyType: [{"topic":"Fuels","family":"Infrastructure","name":"Other infrastructure policies","category":"Hydrogen"}]

title: CCS regulation
description: Presidential Regulation 14/2024 expands the regulatory framework for CCS beyond the upstream oil and gas sector (which is covered by MEMR Regulation 2/2023), paving the way for developments such as blue hydrogen/ammonia.
policyType: [{"topic":"Fuels","family":"Regulations","name":"Market formation regulations","category":"Hydrogen"}]

title: Regulatory proposals for geologic hydrogen
description: The Government is currently reviewing regulations to determine whether changes are needed to support natural hydrogen exploration and the development of orange hydrogen. Any updates to the regulatory framework are expected to begin in mid-2025. Two main options are being considered: one would classify hydrogen as a mineral, giving private owners the rights to develop it; the other would exclude hydrogen from that definition, allowing its development to focus on broader goals like reducing emissions or enhancing energy security.
policyType: [{"topic":"Fuels","family":"Regulations","name":"Market formation regulations","category":"Hydrogen"}]

title: Hydrogen Fuel Electric Train Unites Tender
description: In April 2025, Romania's  hydrogen-powered train project, under 522M USD worth European funding through the National Recovery and Resilienve Plan(PNRR), received its  first eligible offer from Siemens Mobility, now under technical evaluation.
policyType: [{"topic":"Fuels","family":"Market pull","name":"Public procurement","category":"Hydrogen"}]

title: LNG Acceleration Act (LNG-G)
description: The law is part of the measures to quickly replace gas that is no longer imported from Russia. In order to be able to obtain LNG from other supplier countries, LNG terminals and the necessary pipelines must be created in Germany in the short term. The law speeds up approval, award and review procedures. It allows exemptions from an environmental impact assessment. Further, the existing regulations for the future climate-friendly subsequent use of land-based LNG terminals have been concretised. The law requires that the land-based LNG terminals and the natural gas pipelines required for the connection are already suitable for subsequent conversion to hydrogen.
policyType: [{"topic":"Fuels","family":"Infrastructure","name":"Governance","category":"Hydrogen"}]

title: Industry Standards Development and Revision Plan in the Energy Sector
description:
Public consultation till 1st Aug 2025 with a list of new and revised standarization project plans in energy sector, which includes 14 hydrogen or fuel cell related. All shceduled for completion by 2027.

(1)Design and planning guidelines for green hydrogen-ammonia-methanol systems using wind, solar. and biomass 
(2)Post-evaluation guidelines for renewable power to hydrogen projects
(3)Technical specification for sealing of hydrogen pressure equipment
(4)Safety specification for onshore steel H2 pipelines
(5)Cost estimation and budgeting guidelines for renewable hydrogen projects
(6)Perfomance testing methods for SOFC/SOEC
(7)As-built drawing compilation guidelines for renewable hydrogen projects
(8)Evaluation methods for SOFC module design
(9)Safety guidelines for fixed SOFC systems (>10kW)
(10)Electrochemical method for testing hydrogen permeation resistance of coatings
(11)Testing methods for PEM fuel cell gas diffusion layers
(12) Testing methods for Tubular SOFC
(13)Carbon footprint accounting technical specification for renewable power-to-Hydrogen Projects 
(14)(revised, new section added)technical code for electric power construction-part6:water treatment and hydrogen supply equipment and systems
policyType: [{"topic":"Fuels","family":"Regulations","name":"Certification scheme methodology","category":"Hydrogen"}]

title: LuFo Klima program (German aviation research program)
description: The LuFo program is Germany's Federal Aviation Research Program managed by the Federal Ministry for Economic Affairs and Climate Protection (BMWK). It aims to enhance the technological and economic foundation of the aviation industry by supporting research and technology development projects in civil aviation. The program's goals include developing sustainable and efficient air transport systems, strengthening innovation and expertise in research, development, and production, and improving Germany's competitiveness in the global aviation market. Currently the program is in its 7th year. The central objective of the seventh national civil aviation research programme, LuFo Climate VII, is to significantly reduce the climate impact of aviation through aviation-induced greenhouse gases and non-CO2 effects.
policyType: [{"topic":"Fuels","family":"Resource push","name":"Grants for R&D projects","category":"Hydrogen"}]

title: Anhui Province allows free passage for low-carbon/zero-carbon vessels on the Jianghuai Canal (from Aug 2025 till Dec 2027)
policyType: [{"topic":"Fuels","family":"Resource push","name":"Administrative measures","category":"Hydrogen"}]

title: R&D support for hard-to-electrify sectors
description: More than USD 11 million were awarded to five clean hydrogen projects covering geological and above-ground storage, hydrogen distribution, power generation and use for ferries
policyType: [{"topic":"Fuels","family":"Resource push","name":"Grants for R&D projects","category":"Hydrogen"}]

title: Luxembourg ambition on Hydrogen
description: Explore ways of converting solar energy directly into hydrogen, rather than the current process of having to produce energy to convert into electricity, which is then used to produce hydrogen
policyType: [{"topic":"Fuels","family":"Framework legislation","name":"Master Energy Plan","category":"Hydrogen"}]

title: New Zealand funds 22 projects in emission-free transport
description: The Low Emission Vehicles Contestable Fund offers up to $6.5 million a year to projects that will accelerate the uptake of electric vehicles (EVs) and other low emission vehicles. The fund is administered by the Energy Efficiency and Conservation Authority (EECA). Projects are co-funded with private and public sector partners in areas where commercial returns aren’t yet strong enough to justify full private investment.It’s a Government fund administered by the Energy Efficiency and Conservation Authority (EECA). It’s one of several government activities paid for via a levy on petrol and engine fuels
policyType: [{"topic":"Fuels","family":"Market pull","name":"Grants for demand","category":"Hydrogen"}]

title: National Energy System Plan (NPE)
description: The National Energy System Plan aims to lay out a plan to create a climate-neutral, reliable, and affordable energy system in the Netherlands by 2050, focusing on maximizing renewable energy sources, improving energy efficiency, developing infrastructure, fostering international cooperation, and engaging all stakeholders in the transition. Hydrogen is one of the four main 'energy chains' discussed in the Plan, next to electricity, carbon carriers and heat
policyType: [{"topic":"Fuels","family":"Framework legislation","name":"Energy and climate strategy","category":"Hydrogen"}]

title: Plan de déploiement de l'hydrogène pour la transition énergétique
description: The action plan is divided in three pillars: hydrogen production via electrolysis for industrial uses (mainly refineries and chemicals), supported by R&D and innovation; develop hydrogen mobility complementarily to electrification of transport; accelerate the testing of hydrogen blending and hydrogen use in the power sector with the aim to use it, in the long term, as a storage and grid stabilization system.
policyType: [{"topic":"Fuels","family":"Framework legislation","name":"Master Energy Plan","category":"Hydrogen"}]

title: The Netherlands invest DKK1 billion in large scale Power-to-X plants in Denmark
description: The climate ministers of Netherlands and Denmark signed, in June 2020, an agreement (MoU) on the development of large-scale Power-to-X plants. The Netherlands planned to invest DKK 1 billion in 100 MW Danish plants producing synthetic fuels from renewable electricity. The cooperation combines Denmark wind resources with Dutch experience in hydrogen production, and it will also help the Netherlands meet their renewable energy targets.
policyType: [{"topic":"Fuels","family":"International collaboration","name":"Collaboration on projects","category":"Hydrogen"}]

title: KfW (IPEX-Bank and DEG)
description:
KfW operates mainly through two units: IPEX-Bank, which focuses on export and project finance linked to German and European interests, and DEG, which provides loans and equity to private companies in developing countries, similar to the IFC model. Together, they account for over 90% of KfW’s lending. Recent hydrogen-related financing includes:

EUR 325 million for Saudi Arabia’s NEOM project 
EUR 23 million for a hydrogen funding program in South Africa 
EUR 187.5 million loan to H2 Green Steel (now Stegra) in Sweden 
EUR 25 million loan to ACWA Power for a 20-MW electrolyser in Uzbekistan
EUR 100 million subsidized loan for Chile’s H2V Green Hydrogen Facility, part of a €1 billion public funding effort to mobilize €12.5 billion in private capital
policyType: [{"topic":"Fuels","family":"Market pull","name":"Loan and loan guarantees for demand","category":"Hydrogen"},{"topic":"Fuels","family":"Resource push","name":"Loan and loan guarantees for supply","category":"Hydrogen"}]

title: Scotland - Hydrogen's potential and export plan
description: It showcases some of the current efforts and potential market outlook for supply, infrastructure, demand and enablers such as innovation, workforce and investment. It specifies 12 broad areas of action to achieve the export goals. Some of the aspirational targets include 5-GW of low carbon hydrogen production by 2030 and 25 GW by 2040. By 2045, Scotland could produce 3.3 Mtpa of renewable hydrogen with 2.5 Mtpa of that exported to the rest of the UK or Europe. No plans to develop a Scotland-specific standard and certification scheme but seeking alignment within the UK
policyType: [{"topic":"Fuels","family":"Framework legislation","name":"Import strategy","category":"Hydrogen"}]

title: Scotland - Hydrogen action plan
description: The plan describes the hydrogen opportunity in terms of renewable resource quality and exports. It presents an overview of the project pipeline and potential hubs. It defines some actions across production, domestic market, sectoral coupling, supply chain, workforce, international partnerships and innovation. Aspirational targets of 5 GW of renewable and low-carbon hydrogen (450 ktpa) by 2030 and 25 GW by 2045. This could create a gross value added of GBP 5-25 billion and 70 000 - 300 000 jobs could be protected or created by 2045. Rnewable hydrogen production alone could reach 3.3 Mtpa in 2045 with 2.5 Mtpa of that exported to the rest of the UK and Europe. GBP 100 million of public funding made available for hydrogen projects
policyType: [{"topic":"Fuels","family":"Framework legislation","name":"Hydrogen strategy","category":"Hydrogen"}]

title: Scotland - Green Industrial Strategy
description: Strategy to create the maximum economic benefit from the opportunities created by the transition to a net zero energy system. The strategy identifies hydrogen as one of the five priority areas. The supporting actions include R&D, investment, workforce and supply chain. It identifies broad actions which will be detailed in subsequent documents. These include measures to shift existing demand in industrial applications to low-emissions hydrogen, support the development of hubs (co-location of supply and demand), maximize export opportunities including partnerships with importers and infrastructure development, support the development of the hydrogen supply chain and support innovation
policyType: [{"topic":"Fuels","family":"Framework legislation","name":"Energy and climate strategy","category":"Hydrogen"}]

title: Scotland - Hydrogen Policy Statement
description: Policy support for the development of 5 GW of renewable and low-carbon hydrogen by 2030 and 25 GW by 2045. Hydrogen industry will be supported with GBP 100 million investment over 2021-2025. It specifies some of the policy priorities across the supply chain to develop the hydrogen industry (without timelines or quantitative targets) and highlights some of the current initiatives and funding available
policyType: [{"topic":"Fuels","family":"Framework legislation","name":"Hydrogen strategy","category":"Hydrogen"}]

title: Certification roadmap for Latin America
description: Funded by Chile and the European through the "ADELANTE 2" program. Countries involved: Argentina, Chile, Colombia, Panama. Scope: Renewable hydrogen and derivatives. To be completed by the end of 2025
policyType: [{"topic":"Fuels","family":"Regulations","name":"Certification scheme thresholds","category":"Hydrogen"}]

title: Subsidy program for electrolysis in Baden-Wurttemberg
description: The ELY program offers €100 million in funding to support hydrogen projects. Eligible projects must have a minimum size of 1 MW. Incentives include up to €10 million per project, covering up to 45% of eligible investment costs. Funding also applies to balance of plant CAPEX, with storage and compressors eligible for up to 30% of total CAPEX.
policyType: [{"topic":"Fuels","family":"Resource push","name":"Grants for supply","category":"Hydrogen"}]

title: Loan guarantee from Loan Program Office for Plug Power
description: USD 1.66 billion loan guarantee to Plug Power to help finance the construction of up to six facilities across several states to produce clean hydrogen using the proprietary technology. The loan comprises of USD 1.55 billion in principal and USD 107 million in capitalized interest
policyType: [{"topic":"Fuels","family":"Resource push","name":"Loan and loan guarantees for supply","category":"Hydrogen"}]

title: Update of National Hydrogen Strategy
description: The 2030 target for electrolysis deployment was revised to 4 GW (from 6.5 GW) and the 2035 target revised to 8 GW (from 10 GW). One reason for this downward revision was a slower deployment than expected both domestically and globally. The strategy highlights the importance of hydrogen production from electrolysis using electricity from nuclear as a pathway contributing to emissions reduction. The low-emissions hydrogen demand estimated for 2030 is 320-520 ktpa (in comparison to a current demand of about 400 ktpa). A support mechanism of EUR 4 billion (USD 4.4 billion) to support the deployment of 1 GW of electrolysis was confirmed
policyType: [{"topic":"Fuels","family":"Framework legislation","name":"Hydrogen strategy","category":"Hydrogen"}]

title: EIB loan for Galp
description: EUR 180 million (USD 187 million) as a loan from the EIB to Galp. Loan will be used for the construction of a 100 MW electrolyser producing 250 ktpa in Portugal with a total investment of EUR 250 million
policyType: [{"topic":"Fuels","family":"Resource push","name":"Loan and loan guarantees for supply","category":"Hydrogen"}]

title: Hydrogen in Aviation Regulatory Challenge
description: The UK Civil Aviation Authority (CAA) is undertaking a program of work with industry and academia to build the evidence base on the use of hydrogen in aviation. Through a regulatory sandbox intiative the CAA are working with 13 organisations to prepare for the regulation of hydrogen use in aircraft and airports. The program is supported by UK Government funding
policyType: [{"topic":"Fuels","family":"Framework legislation","name":"Master Energy Plan","category":"Hydrogen"}]

title: Austria's Government Program 2020-2024
description: Austria’s government program for 2020-2024 includes a strong focus on hydrogen as part of its climate and energy strategy, aiming to become the number one hydrogen nation through a technology offensive, digitalization, and innovation, with hydrogen playing a crucial role in achieving climate neutrality by 2040. The program goals includes the 1-Million-Roofs Photovoltaic Program to support hydrogen production through renewable energy sources.
policyType: [{"topic":"Fuels","family":"Framework legislation","name":"Energy and climate strategy","category":"Hydrogen"}]

title: German Government Coalition Agreement for the 21st legislative period
description: The coalition agreement of the federal government for the 21st legislative period contains an ongoing commitment to a fast hydrogen ramp-up in general and the hydrogen core network in particular.
policyType: [{"topic":"Fuels","family":"Framework legislation","name":"Master Energy Plan","category":"Hydrogen"}]

title: National hydrogen import strategy
description: The import strategy for hydrogen and hydrogen derivatives sets out a clear and reliable framework for the urgently needed imports of hydrogen and hydrogen derivatives to Germany. It complements Germany’s National Hydrogen Strategy.
policyType: [{"topic":"Fuels","family":"Framework legislation","name":"Import strategy","category":"Hydrogen"}]

title: National Wealth Fund
description:
The UK has allocated £27.8 billion through a new fund, with £500M for renewable hydrogen, £1B for carbon capture, £1.8B for ports, £1.5B for gigafactories, and £2.5B for green steel. The fund aims to mobilize private capital at a 3:1 leverage ratio and brings together the UK Infrastructure Bank and British Business Bank.

As of March 2025, £5.8 billion is earmarked for hydrogen, carbon capture, green steel, gigafactories, ports, and advanced manufacturing.
policyType: [{"topic":"Fuels","family":"Market pull","name":"Loan and loan guarantees for demand","category":"Hydrogen"},{"topic":"Fuels","family":"Resource push","name":"Loan and loan guarantees for supply","category":"Hydrogen"}]

title: Discussion on Hydrogen Guarantee of Origin certification scheme
description: The Government released a discussion paper on the design of a Hydrogen Guarantee of Origin (GO) certification scheme. The aim is to measure and track the emissions form hydrogen production. The scheme will cover a variety of ways in which hydrogen can be produced, including methods using fossil fuels with substantial carbon capture.
policyType: [{"topic":"Fuels","family":"Regulations","name":"Guarantees of origin","category":"Hydrogen"}]

title: Queensland invest AUD2billion of its recovery plan into hydrogen and renewable energy
description: Queensland government announces AUD 2 billion investment in renewable energy and hydrogen as part of the COVID-19 economic recovery plan. The investment will include projects in hydrogen and renewable industries and increasing demand for the resources sector, especially for critical minerals’ mines in the North-West Province.
policyType: [{"topic":"Fuels","family":"Resource push","name":"Grants for supply","category":"Hydrogen"}]

title: Guarantee of origin broadened to hydrogen and renewable gases
description: The GoO scheme was expanded as part of the Renewable Energy Expansion Act (sections 81 and 83), which was approved in July 2021. The Act regulates support schemes and GoO. The process is overseen by E-Control Austria (E-Control Austria für die Regulierung der Elektrizitäts- und Erdgaswirtschaft), the national energy regulator. E-Control is responsible for issuing, managing, and verifying guarantees of origin for gas and hydrogen under the EAG. Only guarantees issued through E-Control’s system, in line with Section 81 EAG, are valid for disclosure and certification purposes
policyType: [{"topic":"Fuels","family":"Regulations","name":"Guarantees of origin","category":"Hydrogen"}]

title: Roadmap to net-zero carbon concrete by 2025
description: Canada’s Net-zero Carbon Concrete Roadmap, published in November 2022, was developed by an Industry-Government Working Group, co-led by the Cement Association of Canada and Innovation, Science and Economic Development Canada. The Roadmap charts the course to reducing greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions from the cement and concrete sector by 15 million tons by 2030 and achieving net-zero concrete by 2050. In the longer term, priority actions include, continuing to deploy clinker substitutes and alternative clinker technologies. Actions also include harnessing new energy sources such as biogenically-derived fuels, clean hydrogen and electricity, and utilizing innovations to maximize concrete's ability to sequester carbon via a variety of carbon mineralization approaches.
policyType: [{"topic":"Fuels","family":"Framework legislation","name":"Master Energy Plan","category":"Hydrogen"}]

title: Ontario's Low-Carbon Hydrogen Strategy
description: Ontario strategy is focused on producing hydrogen for grid resiliency and for end use in hard to abate sectors where electrification may find challenges. Through their eight actions, Ontario’s hydrogen strategy is expected to increase the amount of annual production capacity of low-carbon hydrogen eight-fold in the province and support the  market to meet its potential.
policyType: [{"topic":"Fuels","family":"Framework legislation","name":"Hydrogen strategy","category":"Hydrogen"}]

title: Russia Hydrogen Strategy
description: Russia hydrogen strategy sees the country as one of the world leaders in production and exports of hydrogen, targeting 20% of the global market by 2030 with hydrogen exports of 2 million mt/year by 2035 and 15-50 million mt/year by 2050. Russia is considering developing hydrogen projects based on nuclear, natural gas and renewables, and plans to capitalize on domestic resources, existing energy supply routes, and proximity to potential future consumers in Europe and Asia.
policyType: [{"topic":"Fuels","family":"Framework legislation","name":"Hydrogen strategy","category":"Hydrogen"}]

title: German Important Project of Common Interest (IPCEI) Hy2Tech
description: EUR 550 million for 4 German projects under the Hy2Tech IPCEI. The funds are earmarked for the development and industrialisation of high-performance PEM fuel cell stack modules for heavy-duty applications, the development of fuel cell trucks, the development and construction of production facilities for the series production of stationary fuel cells, and the expansion of industrial production of electrolysers.
policyType: [{"topic":"Fuels","family":"Market pull","name":"Grants for demand","category":"Hydrogen"}]

title: Loans and subsidies for hydrogen infrastructure
description: DKK 7.4 billion (USD 1.03 billion) as loans for the hydrogen pipeline to Germany and operating subsidies of up to DKK 8.3 billion (USD 1.2 billion)
policyType: [{"topic":"Fuels","family":"Infrastructure","name":"Loan and loan guarantees for infrastructure","category":"Hydrogen"}]

title: Quebec's Green Hydrogen and Bioenergy Strategy
description: Québec released its Green Hydrogen and Bioenergy Strategy in 2022. Hydrogen will be prioritized for uses where other decarbonization options are limited: substitution of high-carbon hydrogen and other uses in industrial processes (iron, steel and petroleum), in the production of derivatives like methanol and synthetic fuels, use of hydrogen in heavy transport to complement direct electrification and as part of regional clean energy hubs. Québec is primarily targeting the use of hydrogen for domestic decarbonization, with exports looked upon as a long-term objective.
policyType: [{"topic":"Fuels","family":"Framework legislation","name":"Hydrogen strategy","category":"Hydrogen"}]

title: British Columbia's Hydrogen Strategy
description: British Columbia released its hydrogen strategy – a blueprint for how renewable and low-carbon hydrogen will support its climate goals and create new jobs in B.C.’s growing clean-tech sector. Part of CleanBC, the B.C. Hydrogen Strategy includes 63 actions for government, industry and innovators to undertake during the short term (2020-25), medium term (2025-30) and long term (2030 and beyond). The strategy’s immediate priorities include scaling up production of renewable hydrogen, establishing regional hydrogen hubs and deploying medium- and heavy-duty fuel-cell vehicles.

title: Alberta Hydrogen Roadmap
description: The Alberta Hydrogen Roadmap aims to integrate clean hydrogen into Alberta’s energy system by 2030, leveraging its natural gas reserves, CCUS infrastructure, and renewable energy sector. The plan targets hydrogen use in transportation, heating, power generation, and industrial processes, with a goal to reduce GHG emissions by 14 Mt annually. Alberta aims to become a global leader in hydrogen exports, with projections to produce 45 million tonnes of clean hydrogen per year and export 1 million tonnes by 2030. The roadmap outlines seven policy pillars, including building market demand, enabling CCUS, de-risking investment, and pursuing hydrogen exports.

title: New Brunswick Hydrogen Roadmap
description: New Brunswick released its Hydrogen Roadmap in early 2024. The roadmap is a five-year plan outlining 13 actions, using the province’s location, natural resources and existing capabilities, to develop the hydrogen industry and position New Brunswick as a leader in producing hydrogen for consumption domestically and abroad
policyType: [{"topic":"Fuels","family":"Framework legislation","name":"Hydrogen strategy","category":"Hydrogen"}]

title: Nova Scotia Green Hydrogen Action Plan
description: The Green Hydrogen Action Plan,  outlines Nova Scotia’s strategy to develop a green hydrogen sector using renewable electricity to produce hydrogen through electrolysis, emitting only water and heat. The plan emphasizes leveraging the province’s natural resources, such as offshore wind, to produce green hydrogen for both domestic use and export. It aims to support sustainable prosperity, align with climate goals, and ensure community benefits. The plan includes goals for creating a competitive export market, ensuring environmental sustainability, fostering community engagement, prioritizing safety, investing in workforce development, and supporting research and innovation in green hydrogen technologies.

title: National Hydrogen Strategy

title: Newfoundland and Labrador Wind-Hydrogen Fiscal Framework
description: The Government of Newfoundland and Labrador released a new wind-hydrogen fiscal framework applicable to wind-hydrogen projects in the province. The fiscal framework provides a predictable and transparent fiscal system to inform investment decisions and resource development for wind-hydrogen projects. The plan provides for a sharing of financial returns between investors and the Provincial Government to achieve a balance between benefits to the province for use of its resources (land, wind and water) while recognizing project investment and risk.

title: Canada's 2030 Nationally Determined Contribution (NDC)
description: Canada’s 2035 NDC commits to reducing emissions by 45-50% below 2005 levels by 2035. This builds on the 2030 target of 40-45% below 2005 levels. Three key policy approaches highlighted for domestic use are  carbon markets (e.g. for industrial emitters),   foundational regulations, and  incentives that promote access to and broad uptake of clean technologies, including clean hydrogen. Canada will also continue to explore new areas to reduce emissions, and will work with international partners to drive global ambition

title: Austria's Government Program 2025-2029
description: Austria’s government program for 2025-2029 reaffirms the ambitious national target of reaching climate neutrality in 2040. Important support mechanisms for industry are emphasized as well

title: World Bank loan for Colombia's energy transition
description: The World Bank Board approved USD 1 billion in financing for Colombia to help the country accelerating its energy transition, promoting sustainable land use, and enhance climate resilience and adaptation. The loan has a 20-year term with a three-and-a-half-year grace period. The aid will support a reform program to assist Colombia’s moves to lower its carbon emissions, particularly in the energy and transport sectors. It aims to increase non-conventional renewable energy production output and develop a green hydrogen industry in the country.

title: 2022-23 Budget includes funding for hydrogen
description:
The 2022-23 Budget includes:
- $300 million to support low emissions LNG and clean hydrogen production at Darwin, together with associated carbon capture and storage infrastructure. Darwin is positioned to become one of the world’s leading low-cost clean energy hubs, with access to excellent onshore and offshore natural gas and greenhouse gas storage resources, including the Beetaloo and Petrel basins and the Barossa and Bayu-Undan fields.
- $247.1 million to support private sector investment in low emissions technologies including hydrogen, the continued development of a hydrogen Guarantee of Origin scheme.
- $200 million to enhance Australia’s supply chain security through new low emissions manufacturing facilities (using hydrogen and hydrogen-derivatives like ammonia, as well as carbon capture utilisation and storage) in the Pilbara region.
- $100 million to support pre-Final Investment Decision activities and early works to make the Port of Newcastle ‘hydrogen ready’.

The goals include deploying 40,000-50,000 hydrogen passenger cars and 870 hydrogen buses by 2030, supported by 80 hydrogen refueling stations. Key measures involve promoting hydrogen vehicle adoption, building necessary infrastructure, and enhancing regulatory frameworks to facilitate hydrogen technology integration. The focus is on creating a sustainable hydrogen ecosystem to reduce emissions and support clean mobility.

title: National Strategy on Hydrogen

It will also address research and innovation, infrastructure development, workforce training, and sustainability standards to position the country as a competitive player in the global hydrogen economy.

description: The climate strategy stimulates innovation and climate-friendly technologies, supports development and promotes exports of and investments in green, climate-friendly technologies (e.g. hydrogen technologies). This will strengthen the long-term competitiveness of German industry, as the necessary decarbonization of the global economy will lead to greater demand for these technologies. It also supports German companies in developping international hydrogen projects.

title: Funds for energy transition program

Through two cooperation agreements, Ecopetrol, the Ministry of Science, Technology and Innovation (MinCiencias) and the Ministry of Mines and Energy (MinEnergía) will promote science, technology and innovation (CTeI) actions in areas such as carbon capture, hydrogen generation and technology transfer processes to improve industry. - Process studies for the generation of low-emission hydrogen, articulated with capacity building processes.
- Measurement of carbon sequestration and other ecosystem services based on natural CNS climate solutions. These must be articulated with capacity building processes, value generation and have the participation of ethnic or rural communities.

title: Hydrogen policy in Wales
description:
In February 2025, the government published a draft policy on hydrogen production, storage, and transport. It supports hydrogen use when it helps decarbonization, meets the Low Carbon Hydrogen Standard, and supports a just transition for communities.

The policy is:

Technology neutral
Focused on absolute emissions
Allows limited fossil-based hydrogen only if it accelerates low-carbon alternatives
It will be integrated into future Planning Policy and Carbon Budgets.

title: National Energy and Climate Plan (NECP) - Update 2024

It is estimated that the contribution of renewable hydrogen in final energy consumption in Greece will reach 1.2 TWh in 2030, 5.6 TWh in 2040 and 20.2 TWh until 2050. With regard to the use of renewable fuels of non-biological origin (RFNBO) for transport, a target of 0.9% in the energy consumption of the Greek transport sector by 2030 has been set, increasing to 11.5% by 2040 and 30.9% by 2050

title: Public investment in transmission network
description:
The Netherlands plans to invest €750 million by 2031 to co-fund a national hydrogen network, with Gasunie as the TSO. The total investment need is €1.5 billion, and part of the network should be operational by 2026.

As of February 2025, costs have risen to €3.8 billion due to fewer repurposed pipelines, higher material and labor costs, and stricter environmental rules. Tariffs will be regulated from 2031–2033 and depend on user numbers. Lower-than-expected electrolysis capacity (1.2–1.5 GW vs. 4 GW) may require additional government support or adjusted tariff design to avoid high early costs.

title: Law Promoting hydrogen innovation, production, storage and use (Decree 1476)
description:
This decree provides more details on articles 21 and 23 of Law 2099 of 2021 which were left as actions for the government in that law. Defines mechanisms, conditions, and incentives for local development, innovation, research, production, storage, transport, distribution, and use of hydrogen for electricity, energy storage, and decarbonization across sectors like transport, gas, hydrocarbons, mining, and industry. Hydrogen is considered an energy vector for storage, fuel, or industrial input
The Law designates the Ministry of Environment and Sustainable Development and the Ministry of Mines and Energy to (a) define a threshold for low-emissions hydrogen; (b) adopt a mechanism to certify hydrogen (and be able to grant the incentives from Law 2099). It does not specify a maximum period to do so
The Law also designates the Ministry of Transport, with the Ministry of Environment and Sustainable Development to define incentives and conditions for hydrogen use in transport (without a specific time limit)

title: 3-Up Strategy for Hydrogen Economy Growth
description: The “Future Strategy for Hydrogen Technology in Korea,” outlines South Korea’s ambitious plans to become a global leader in hydrogen technology. The strategy focuses on three main goals: Scale-Up, Build-Up, and Level-Up. The Scale-Up goal aims to expand the clean hydrogen ecosystem by establishing a global supply chain and creating large-scale hydrogen demand in power generation and transportation. title: Hydrogen Society Promotion Act
description:
The Act introduces three support options for hydrogen projects:

15-year CfD for domestic and imported hydrogen, requiring at least 10 years of post-subsidy operation
Development expenditure (DEVEX) support for shared infrastructure used by at least two users (min. 10 ktpa)
Regulatory exemptions via standard documentation
Applicants can choose any of the three. CfD reference prices are based on conventional fuels (new uses) or historical fossil hydrogen prices (existing uses). Eligible offtakers must be in hard-to-abate sectors with a minimum size of 1 ktpa.

The Act also includes a certification scheme aligned with EU thresholds (e.g., 3.4 kg CO₂-eq/kg H₂). In 2025, amendments to the JOGMEC Act established the legal basis for promoting low-carbon hydrogen and derivatives in Japan.

The NSW Hydrogen Strategy sets a vision and path for developing a thriving green hydrogen industry in NSW. - Hydrogen price under AUD$2.80 per kilogram
- 110,000 tonnes per annum of green hydrogen produced
- 700 MW of electrolyser capacity
- 12 gigawatts (GW) of renewable energy capacity
- 10% hydrogen (by volume) gas network blending
- 10,000 hydrogen vehicles
- 100 hydrogen refuelling stations
- 20% hydrogen vehicles in the NSW Government heavy vehicle fleet

title: Northern Territory renewable hydrogen strategy
description:
In October 2021, the Northern Territory Government released the Northern Territory Renewable Hydrogen Master Plan. The Master Plan charts a pathway for the Government to accelerate the development of a renewable hydrogen industry and outlines the enabling activities needed to secure private sector investment, including:

Demonstration phase: The Government is collaborating with proponents to progress research and trials.
Targeted application: The second phase will see the development of hydrogen production and end-use technologies.
Large-scale production for export: The final stage will see production and use technologies sufficiently developed so they are cost competitive.
Priority action themes in the Masterplan include local industry development, resource management, grow and harness demand, support innovation, and responsive regulation.

title: Hydrogen Transport and Storage (T&S) Networks Pathway
description: Sets out the next steps in the government's vision for the strategic development of UK hydrogen T&S infrastructure. It targets up to two hydrogen storage projects and associated regional pipeline infrastructure to be in operation or under construction by 2030

title: 10th Basic Energy Plan for Electricity Supply and Demand (2023-2036)
description: Revised targets for electricity generation for 2030 with 13 TWh from co-firing of hydrogen and ammonia at existing gas and coal power plants (equivalent to about 2.1% of electricity generation) and 16 TWh from stationary fuel cells using natural gas and hydrogen. title: Power Development Master Plan VIII
description: The plan gives an indication of the foreseen capacities for 2050 including thermal power using biomass and ammonia (25.6-32.4 GW), domestic gas-fired thermal power running entirely on hydrogen (7 GW), LNG thermal power plant with hydrogen combustion (4.5-9 GW), LNG thermal power converted to run entirely on hydrogen (16.4-20.9 GW)
policyType: [{"topic":"Fuels","family":"Framework legislation","name":"Energy and climate strategy","category":"Hydrogen"}]

title: National electricity system development program 2023-2037
description: Increase the share of hydrogen in the fuel input mix combined-cycle gas turbine (CCGT) plants to 30% by 2036, supported by converting 1 024 MW of CCGT capacity to being able to co-fire 30% of hydrogen by 2036
policyType: [{"topic":"Fuels","family":"Framework legislation","name":"Energy and climate strategy","category":"Hydrogen"}]

title: Public procurement under Industrial Deep Decarbonisation Initiative (IDDI)
description: India is introducing timebound procurement commitments for low-emission steel, cement, and concrete in public construction, aiming to indirectly stimulate demand for low-emissions hydrogen. These commitments are guided by emissions thresholds based on life cycle assessment (LCA) methodologies, aligned with the country’s net-zero targets for public buildings and infrastructure. This approach is expected to create a predictable market signal for cleaner industrial materials and support the scale-up of hydrogen-based production technologies.
policyType: [{"topic":"Fuels","family":"Market pull","name":"Public procurement","category":"Hydrogen"}]

title: Basic Hydrogen Strategy (update)
description: Interim target for 12 Mt of hydrogen demand by 2040 (complementing previous targets for 3 Mt by 2030 and 20 Mt by 2050). Target to install 15 GW of electrolysis globally. Shift focus from FCEVs to the use of hydrogen in applications, notably in steel and petrochemical industries
policyType: [{"topic":"Fuels","family":"Framework legislation","name":"Hydrogen strategy","category":"Hydrogen"}]

title: Hydrogen roadmap
description: Electrolyser target of 5 MW by 2030 and 485 MW by 2050 with investment needs (for production only) of USD 9 million by 2030 and USD 454 million by 2050. Estimated maximum hydrogen demand of 4.2 ktpa for steel, 12 ktpa for cement, and 52.5 ktpa for road transport
policyType: [{"topic":"Fuels","family":"Framework legislation","name":"Hydrogen strategy","category":"Hydrogen"}]

title: National Hydrogen Strategy
description: Roadmap identifying 18 actions across 4 areas to be implemented before 2026. Actions include enabling measures such as power market design and development guides for project construction, and deployment targets such as 10 pilot projects and 2 hydrogen valleys by 2026
policyType: [{"topic":"Fuels","family":"Framework legislation","name":"Hydrogen strategy","category":"Hydrogen"}]

title: National Low-Carbon Hydrogen Strategy
description: Targets 1.5 Mtpa of renewable hydrogen by 2030. Focus on industry, transport and export. 40 Mtpa CO2 emissions reduction resulting from hydrogen use by 2040, and GDP growth of USD 10-18 billion
policyType: [{"topic":"Fuels","family":"Framework legislation","name":"Hydrogen strategy","category":"Hydrogen"}]

title: Hydrogen Roadmap
description: Roadmap for hydrogen deployment across three phases until 2050. Targets for the pilot phase (until 2030) include 3-5 hydrogen refuelling stations (HRS) and 2-40 ktpa of renewable hydrogen
policyType: [{"topic":"Fuels","family":"Framework legislation","name":"Hydrogen strategy","category":"Hydrogen"}]

title: Hydrogen and e-fuels roadmap
description: Targets domestic hydrogen demand in 2030 of 12 ktpa plus another 24 ktpa to satisfy 10% of demand from international aviation. Satisfying this with renewable hydrogen would require 237 MW of electrolysis. Investment needs for 2030 of USD 1.8-3.2 billion. 2040 demand is estimated to be ten times larger (with almost 80% from international aviation)
policyType: [{"topic":"Fuels","family":"Framework legislation","name":"Hydrogen strategy","category":"Hydrogen"}]

title: National hydrogen strategy
description: Strategy based on three drivers (decarbonisation, energy security, and exports), with nine action areas including hubs, hydrogen use in mini-grids and power generation, a carbon pricing scheme, and definition of a hydrogen certification scheme. policyType: [{"topic":"Fuels","family":"Framework legislation","name":"Hydrogen strategy","category":"Hydrogen"}]

title: National hydrogen strategy
description: Potential demand for 2050 is estimated to be 0.6-2.2 Mtpa with the bulk (between 35% and 65%) coming from aviation (for electro-sustainable aviation fuel [e-SAF])
policyType: [{"topic":"Fuels","family":"Framework legislation","name":"Hydrogen strategy","category":"Hydrogen"}]

title: Hydrogen strategy
description: Hydrogen demand in 2050 ranging from 580 ktpa to 5.3 Mtpa (equivalent to 10-100% of Israel’s final energy demand in 2021) with the difference coming from the power sector. Introduction of a 5.5% combined target for synthetic fuels and biofuels by 2033 is under consideration
policyType: [{"topic":"Fuels","family":"Framework legislation","name":"Hydrogen strategy","category":"Hydrogen"}]

title: Concept of development of hydrogen energy in the Republic of Kazakhstan until 2040
description: Concept note defining broad areas of action for development, with 6 target indicators to measure results, including a 10 GW electrolyser target and up to KZT 5 trillion (Kazakhstani Tenge) (USD 11.3 billion) of investments in hydrogen by 2040 and a 20% share of domestic supply of technologies
policyType: [{"topic":"Fuels","family":"Framework legislation","name":"Hydrogen strategy","category":"Hydrogen"}]

title: Roadmap for low-carbon hydrogen industry
description: Target of 1.5% of the global hydrogen market and up to 1% of the global “green” steel market by 2050. Explicit production targets for hydrogen, ammonia, “green” steel, methanol and ammonium nitrate. Hydrogen production targets of 1.2 Mtpa by 2030 (almost exclusively for exports), increasing to 6.5 Mtpa by 2050 (of which 4.3 Mtpa are for export)
policyType: [{"topic":"Fuels","family":"Framework legislation","name":"Hydrogen strategy","category":"Hydrogen"}]

title: National Hydrogen Strategy and the Action Plan for its implementation
description: Action plan for implementation of the roadmap with 33 actions across 4 objectives (decarbonisation; “clean” hydrogen production, skills and innovation; sectoral coupling and renewables integration). 2030 targets include 34.4 ktpa of renewable hydrogen by 2030, 21 500 heavy- and medium-duty trucks, and 1.6 GW of combined-cycle gas turbine (CCGT) capacity with 50% renewable hydrogen co-firing
policyType: [{"topic":"Fuels","family":"Framework legislation","name":"Hydrogen strategy","category":"Hydrogen"}]

title: National strategy for the development of green hydrogen and its derivatives
description: Targets 8.3 Mtpa of total hydrogen production and 87 GW of electrolysis by 2050, including 6 Mtpa for export. Intermediate milestones for 2030 include 320 ktpa of hydrogen production, 3.9 GW of electrolysis, and 5 GW of renewables. Short-term use is in chemicals and refining, with long-term use in aviation (e-SAF), shipping and power. Investment needs for 2050 total USD 130 billion

title: Update of National Hydrogen Strategy
description: Update based on the latest market conditions and EU legislation. The third focuses on new production pathways.

title: National Strategy for the development of hydrogen
description: Target to produce and export 30-40 TWh of hydrogen and hydrogen-based fuels by 2040. Focus on pilot projects until 2030 to start up the sector
policyType: [{"topic":"Fuels","family":"Framework legislation","name":"Hydrogen strategy","category":"Hydrogen"}]

title: Triennial Work Plan for hydrogen [PNH2] (2023-2025)
description: The 2023-2025 Triennial Work Plan of the National Hydrogen Program defines the strategy of the country, with three timeframes: by 2025, deploy low-carbon hydrogen pilot plants across the country; by 2030, consolidate Brazil as a competitive low-carbon hydrogen producer; and by 2035 consolidate low-carbon hydrogen hubs in Brazil
policyType: [{"topic":"Fuels","family":"Framework legislation","name":"Hydrogen strategy","category":"Hydrogen"}]

title: Action Plan for green hydrogen (2023-2030)
description: 81 actions across 18 lines of action aiming to promote renewable hydrogen. Responsible institutions are defined for each action. policyType: [{"topic":"Fuels","family":"Framework legislation","name":"Master Energy Plan","category":"Hydrogen"}]

title: Green hydrogen strategy and roadmap

Phase 1 (2023-2027) includes 20% imported nitrogen fertlisers to be renewable (100 kt), 100% imported methanol to be renewable (5 kt), 150 MW of renewable capacity dedicated to ELY and 100 MW of ELY. policyType: [{"topic":"Fuels","family":"Framework legislation","name":"Hydrogen strategy","category":"Hydrogen"}]

description:

title: Hydrogen action plan
description: Follow-up of the hydrogen strategy from June 2020, the plan has some recommendations from the National Hydrogen Council (NWR) for efficient implementation of the hydrogen strategy. title: Oman Green Hydrogen Strategy
description: This document lays out Oman's National hydrogen strategy developed by Hydrom, government institution tasked with developing the strategy, that identifes "green" hydrogen production targets, electrolyser capacity needed, and renewable electrical capacity needed for 2030, 2040, and 2050.  The strategy also introduces broadly the new public auction system for land for renewable hydrogen production, which is classified as "market strucutre". title: Guarantees of origin system for renewable fuels (incl. hydrogen)
description:
On September 2023, the Parliament decided to amend the Energy Act and the Electricity Supply Act within the framework of the Federal Act on a Secure Electricity Supply Based on Renewable Energies. Several laws were adapted including the one on guarantees of origin (including RFNBO, non-renewable hydrogen and low-emission aviation fuels). The changes to the GoO scheme came into effect in January 2025. This GoO scheme is not a certification scheme and it is meant to contribute to transparency, avoidance of double counting and emissions reduction. The GOs are standardized with the Energy Community and the system is based on the AIB requirements.
The Ordinance on the Placing on the Market of Renewable and Low-Emission Thermal and Motor Fuels (RFO or IBTV in German) specifies the requirements for the sale of these types of fuels. In this regard, the EU voluntary schemes (RED) can also be used as proof of compliance with the requirements. IBTV (Article 3) specifies a minimum of 40% GHG reduction in comparison to the conventional fossil fuel

title: Conditional commitment for loan guarantee for Wabash Valley Resources

policyType: [{"topic":"Fuels","family":"Resource push","name":"Loan and loan guarantees for supply","category":"Hydrogen"}]

title: Andhra Pradesh incentives for AM's ammonia plant
description: A USD 215 million subsidy package has been introduced to support renewable ammonia production, offering up to 25% of CAPEX, capped at INR 18.5 million (USD 215,400) per 1 ktpa of capacity—though the total estimated CAPEX of USD 1.5 billion means the subsidy won’t reach the full 25%. The support is disbursed over five years post-commissioning. Additional incentives include a 20% CAPEX subsidy for desalination plants, exemptions from stamp duty, reduced water supply charges, a five-year exemption from state GST on renewable hydrogen sales, and reimbursement of electricity duties. This initiative contributes to the state’s goal of producing 1.5 Mtpa of renewable hydrogen by 2047, as outlined in its 2023 Integrated Clean Energy Policy.

30% CAPEX subsidy for ammonia and methanol plants (capped per ktpa, max INR 300 million)
Discounts on water, electricity, taxes, and duties

title: Hydrogen roadmap
description: Peru plans to develop four pilot hydrogen projects by 2030—located in Callao, Piura, Matarani, and Ica—with a combined electrolyzer capacity of 256 MW. While exports are expected to begin in 2040, domestic hydrogen demand is projected to grow from 7–23.6 ktpa in 2030 to 131–1167 ktpa by 2050. Cement will be the largest demand sector by 2050 (25%), followed by road transport (86 ktpa, ~20%) and mining. Around 50% of demand will be concentrated near Lima. Export demand is assumed to be four times higher than domestic demand. The levelized cost of hydrogen (LCOH) is projected to fall from USD 2/kg in 2030 to USD 1.2/kg by 2040.

title: National Low-Carbon Hydrogen Policy (Law 14948)
description:
This law is part of the broader National Energy Policy. It establishes an overarching legal framework for low-carbon hydrogen defining the principles, objectives, governance, incentives. There are 4 instruments  National Hydrogen Program (PNH2);  The Low Carbon Hydrogen development program (PHBC); Certification (SBCH2);Special incentive regime for the production of low-carbon hydrogen (Rehidro)
For Rehidro, the main incentive instrument is the suspension, for five years from 1 January 2025, of the levying of PIS/Pasep and Cofins on activities related to low-carbon hydrogen carried out by its beneficiaries

title: Integrated National Energy and Climate Plan Update 2023-2030
description: The National Energy and Climate Plan identifies Spain's voluntary targets to meet Spain's contribution to the EU's 2030 targets under the Renewable Energy Directive. The plan also identifies the policies, measures, and potential funding earmarked for these policies
policyType: [{"topic":"Fuels","family":"Framework legislation","name":"Energy and climate strategy","category":"Hydrogen"}]

title: Law Promoting hydrogen innovation, production and use as a fuel (Directive 002 from MINAE)
description:
The Law mandates that institutions within the energy and environment areas develop an action plan, within their competences, to promote hydrogen innovation, production and use as a fuel. It declares these activities as public interest. The law was enacted in 2018 and in 2021, a draft was proposed (and no update is known by February 2025)
The incentives from the 2021 proposal include  Tax exemptions. No taxes, fees, or consular duties on the import or local purchase of machinery, equipment, accessories, parts, compressors, storage systems, fuel cells, cargo vehicles, cars, and other necessary items;  Tax exemptions for establishment. No taxes on the import or local purchase of goods needed to set up new companies, or for existing companies joining the green hydrogen industry; Income tax exemption. Exemption from income tax and any other tax based on gross or net profits and dividends paid to shareholders involved in green hydrogen research, production, and transportation; Public bank support. Public banks can provide financing for green hydrogen projects;  Environmental viability assessments for green hydrogen production projects will be expedited with priority review. Environmental impact studies or permits must be resolved within 90 calendar days; (6) Authorizes existing power plants with hydropower concessions to allocate their electricity production to green hydrogen production

title: Grants and loans for INERATEC

title: System Development Strategy
description: The system development strategy brings together findings from scenarios from a technical and systemic perspective and outlines robust transformation pathways for achieving the climate targets efficiently without losing the necessary flexibility to respond to changes in environmental conditions. It sets a framework that provides orientation for subsequent processes, such as the network development plans for electricity or gas and hydrogen, as well as the sector- and energy source-specific strategies and programs. In this way, it ensures the coherence of the various strategies and programs in terms of a cost-effective, consumer-friendly, efficient, environmentally friendly and climate-neutral overall system. It presents specifc modelling estimates for 2045 including hydrogen demand for industry, transport, and imports of hydrogen as well as other supply targets.

title: Second Emissions Reduction Plan
description: New Zealand’s second emissions reduction plan (ERP2) emphasizes hydrogen as a key component in achieving its climate goals. title: Green paper on hydrogen in New Zealand
description: The green paper outlines New Zealand’s strategy to leverage hydrogen as a key component in transitioning to a low-emissions economy.
