title: Green Industrial Initiative
description: The Green Industrial Initiative roadmap outlines Norway's commitment to becoming a leader in the green industrial transition. It aims to adapt Norwegian business to a low-emission society, achieve emission reduction targets, realize green industrial projects, create attractive jobs, increase non-oil and gas exports, and reduce vulnerabilities in key value chains. Hydrogen is a priority area, with the vision of Norway becoming a leading nation in the field. The roadmap aims to provide better framework conditions for green industrial projects and encourage investment in green projects.
policyType: [{"topic":"Fuels","family":"Framework legislation","name":"Hydrogen strategy","category":"Hydrogen"}]

title: Eksfin Concessional Loans
description: Eksfin offers financing for hydrogen projects, recognizing the capital-intensive nature and associated technological and regulatory risks. By collaborating with private capital, commercial banks, and government funding, Eksfin provides loans and guarantees to support investments across the hydrogen value chain. This initiative aims to enhance financing capacity for both large corporations and SMEs, promoting the development of hydrogen as a clean energy source
policyType: [{"topic":"Fuels","family":"Market pull","name":"Loan and loan guarantees for demand","category":"Hydrogen"},{"topic":"Fuels","family":"Resource push","name":"Loan and loan guarantees for supply","category":"Hydrogen"}]

title: Guarantee of origin for renewable hydrogen
description: The proposed amendment to the Renewable Energy Sources Act aims to enhance the development and integration of hydrogen technologies in Poland. The primary goals include promoting the use of hydrogen as a clean energy source, establishing a regulatory framework for hydrogen production and distribution, and supporting research and innovation in hydrogen technologies. This initiative aligns with the EU’s directive on renewable energy and seeks to reduce greenhouse gas emissions, improve energy security, and foster economic growth through sustainable energy solutions.
policyType: [{"topic":"Fuels","family":"Regulations","name":"Guarantees of origin","category":"Hydrogen"}]

title: Sector Deal for the Development of the Hydrogen Economy
description: Poland’s “Sectoral Agreement for the Development of the Hydrogen Economy,” aims to advance hydrogen technologies as a key element in achieving climate neutrality. The agreement, involving government, business, and scientific communities, focuses on creating a value chain for low-emission hydrogen, leveraging Poland’s position as a leading hydrogen producer. Goals include decarbonizing production, fostering innovation, creating jobs, and integrating hydrogen into transport, energy, heating, and industry sectors.
policyType: [{"topic":"Fuels","family":"Framework legislation","name":"Hydrogen strategy","category":"Hydrogen"}]

title: Overview Report on Hydrogen
description: The Swiss Federal Council’s report on hydrogen outlines its increasing importance in achieving the net-zero emissions goal by 2050. Hydrogen, primarily produced from renewable energy, is expected to play a crucial role in sectors where direct electrification is challenging, such as industry, aviation, and heavy transport. The report emphasizes the need for a robust domestic hydrogen market, supported by local production until imports become viable around 2035. It also highlights the necessity of regulatory frameworks and infrastructure development to facilitate hydrogen production, storage, and transport. The AFDD goals focus on integrating hydrogen into the energy system to enhance energy security and sustainability.
policyType: [{"topic":"Fuels","family":"Framework legislation","name":"Hydrogen strategy","category":"Hydrogen"}]

title: Singapore-Asia Taxonomy for Sustainable Finance
description: The Singapore-Asia Taxonomy for Sustainable Finance, launched by the Monetary Authority of Singapore, includes hydrogen as a component in its transition strategy. The taxonomy sets clear criteria for hydrogen production and usage, emphasizing low-carbon hydrogen as essential for achieving net-zero emissions. Goals include promoting investments in green hydrogen technologies and infrastructure, and establishing hydrogen as a sustainable energy source across various sectors, contributing to climate change mitigation and energy transition
policyType: [{"topic":"Fuels","family":"Framework legislation","name":"Hydrogen strategy","category":"Hydrogen"}]

title: Hydrogen Net Zero Investment Roadmap (2023)
description: £960 mln. The UK Hydrogen Net Zero Investment Roadmap outlines the country’s ambitious goals to develop a robust hydrogen economy, aiming for up to 10GW of low-carbon hydrogen production capacity by 2030, with a potential 27GW pipeline by 2037. Key initiatives include the Hydrogen Allocation Rounds (HAR1 and HAR2) to support commercial-scale green hydrogen projects, the  Green Industries Growth Accelerator (GIGA) fund, and the development of hydrogen transport and storage infrastructure. The roadmap emphasizes hydrogen’s role in decarbonizing hard-to-electrify sectors, enhancing energy security, and supporting the UK’s net zero targets.
policyType: [{"topic":"Fuels","family":"Framework legislation","name":"Hydrogen strategy","category":"Hydrogen"}]

title: H2U Program
description: The Uruguayan government, through Resolution No. 294/022, has launched the “H2U Program” to promote the development of green hydrogen as a key component in the country’s energy transition. The program, managed by the Ministry of Industry, Energy, and Mining, aims to leverage Uruguay’s renewable energy capabilities to produce green hydrogen, reduce greenhouse gas emissions, and support the decarbonization of the economy. Key goals include fostering innovation, attracting investments, building capacities, and enhancing international cooperation to position Uruguay as a leader in green hydrogen production and export
policyType: [{"topic":"Fuels","family":"Framework legislation","name":"Hydrogen strategy","category":"Hydrogen"}]

title: Joint declaration for the implementarion of a green hydrogen certification scheme for Latin Amercia and the Caribbean (CertHILAC)
description: The CertHiLAC certification system for clean hydrogen in Latin America and the Caribbean was announced during the Energy Week organized by OLADE. This initiative, supported by 14 countries, aims to establish a regional certification system for clean and low-carbon hydrogen production, ensuring compliance with international standards while considering the unique characteristics of the region
policyType: [{"topic":"Fuels","family":"Regulations","name":"Guarantees of origin","category":"Hydrogen"}]

title: Nordic-Baltic Hydrogen Corridor
description: The Nordic-Baltic Hydrogen Corridor project aims to develop a hydrogen infrastructure corridor from Finland through Estonia, Latvia, Lithuania, and Poland to Germany. This initiative supports the EU’s hydrogen strategy and the REPowerEU plan, promoting renewable energy and energy supply diversification. The project involves gas transmission system operators from six countries and seeks to connect green hydrogen supply with consumption points, enhance cross-border cooperation, and improve energy security.
policyType: [{"topic":"Fuels","family":"Framework legislation","name":"Master Energy Plan","category":"Hydrogen"}]

title: Smart Green mobility
description: The HyTruck project aims to develop a transnational network of hydrogen refuelling stations (HRS) for large trucks in the Baltic Sea region, supporting the EU’s goal of zero-emissions in road freight transport by 2030. The project assists public authorities in planning and constructing HRS by providing tools and guidelines to identify suitable locations, estimate technological and environmental impacts, and streamline development processes. The ultimate goal is to create a coordinated, competitive, and environmentally friendly hydrogen infrastructure, ensuring seamless and efficient refuelling for heavy-duty vehicles across the region.
policyType: [{"topic":"Fuels","family":"Framework legislation","name":"Master Energy Plan","category":"Hydrogen"}]

title: Climate and Transition Fund (KTF)
description: The Climate and Transformation Fund (KTF) in Germany, established by the Federal Government, aims to support the energy transition and climate protection efforts with a budget for 2023-2026. Key initiatives include funding for the building sector, electric mobility, hydrogen industry expansion, and energy efficiency, along with electricity price relief for consumers and businesses.
policyType: [{"topic":"Fuels","family":"Framework legislation","name":"Energy and climate strategy","category":"Hydrogen"}]

title: Energy Law
description: This is an overarching framework providing principles and setting the foundation of the development of the energy sector. It covers energy planning, development, market, science and technology, oversight, incentives. It also establishes a dual framework for control of total carbon emissions and carbon intensity. For hydrogen, Article 2 lists hydrogen as an energy carrier and Article 33 covers the promotion of the hydrogen industry. These should ease the regulatory burden for hydrogen production once specific legislation is put in place providing more details on incentives. By January 2025, hydrogen is still classified as a hazardous chemical, but the enactment of this law could lead to its reclassification as an energy carrier facilitating the regulatory approvals
policyType: [{"topic":"Fuels","family":"Framework legislation","name":"Energy and climate strategy","category":"Hydrogen"}]

title: Guarantees of Origin (GOs) for hydrogen produced
description: The Guarantees of Origin (GOs) for hydrogen produced in the Czech Republic, delivered to the transmission or distribution system, or to a filling station during one calendar month. Each GO represents 1 MWh of delivered hydrogen, valid for one year from the end date of production. The goals include ensuring accurate measurement and calculation of produced hydrogen, facilitating international transactions through the Association of Issuing Bodies (AIB), and maintaining sustainability criteria. Quantitative targets involve issuing GOs for a minimum of 1 MWh and enabling transfers within the Czech Republic and AIB member states.
policyType: [{"topic":"Fuels","family":"Regulations","name":"Guarantees of origin","category":"Hydrogen"}]

title: Garantie de traçabilité - guarantee of traceability
description: Article L821-2 of the French Energy Code specifies that renewable or low-carbon hydrogen, if not mixed with other types of hydrogen or gases from production to consumption, and if its guarantee is transferred with the hydrogen, is certified with a "guarantee of traceability" to ensure its physical tracking. The goal is to ensure the integrity and traceability of hydrogen, supporting France's broader objectives of increasing renewable and low-carbon hydrogen production to meet decarbonization targets.
policyType: [{"topic":"Fuels","family":"Regulations","name":"Guarantees of origin","category":"Hydrogen"}]

title: Team Europe Renewable Hydrogen Funding Platform
description: Joint initiative between EIB, KfW and the Delegation of the European Union in Chile. The initiative is a framework loan to Chile to promote renewable hydrogen, foster domestic supply chains and potential exports to Europe. The total budget is EUR 216.5 million (EUR 100 million from each the EIB and KfW) and EUR 16.5 million from EU Latin America and Caribbean Investment Facility (LACIF). The funding could lead to the deployment of at least 150 MW of renewables and 150 MW of electrolysis
policyType: [{"topic":"Fuels","family":"Resource push","name":"Loan and loan guarantees for supply","category":"Hydrogen"}]

title: National Hydrogen Strategic Outlook
description: Initial scoping document identifying the potential for hydrogen in a low-emissions future. The document covers scenarios and defines some broad areas for action, but it does not define quantitative targets, responsible, KPIs or timeline for the actions which are expected from a full strategy. The country currently produces about 240 ktpa of hydrogen for methanol (50%), urea (33%) and refining. Scenarios to 2050 foresee growth to 520 ktpa and 1.2 Mtpa by 2050 (Balanced and Accelerated scenario respectively) with 60-85% for exports. This would require 9-17.5 GW of renewables, out of which almost two thirds is offshore wind. Production costs for early 2030s are estimated to be EUR 2.9/kg for low-carbon hydrogen and EUR 3.6-4/kg for renewable hydrogen
policyType: [{"topic":"Fuels","family":"Framework legislation","name":"Hydrogen strategy","category":"Hydrogen"}]

title: Hydrogen Roadmap
description: The Dutch Hydrogen Roadmap outlines the country's strategy to develop a sustainable hydrogen market by 2030 and beyond, focusing on production, imports, infrastructure, and applications across various sectors. Key goals include producing at least 80 PJ of renewable hydrogen by 2030, equivalent to 6-8 GW electrolysis capacity, and scaling up offshore electrolysis. Investments will be directed towards creating a national hydrogen transport network, enhancing storage capacity, and supporting innovation in hydrogen technologies. The roadmap emphasizes collaboration between public and private sectors, setting clear targets, ensuring safety, and fostering social acceptance to achieve climate neutrality and establish the Netherlands as a central player in the global hydrogen market.
policyType: [{"topic":"Fuels","family":"Framework legislation","name":"Hydrogen strategy","category":"Hydrogen"}]

title: Decree n.º 60/2020 for the guarantees of origin of renewable and low-carbon gases
description: The Portuguese government aims to achieve carbon neutrality by 2050, emphasizing the role of renewable and low-carbon gases, including hydrogen, in the decarbonization of the economy. The decree establishes a system for issuing guarantees of origin for renewable and low-carbon gases to certify their renewable content. Hydrogen produced from renewable sources is included in the calculation of renewable energy targets, with specific goals set for renewable energy consumption: 31% by 2020, 34% by 2022, 38% by 2025, 41% by 2027, and 47% by 2030. Additionally, the use of renewable energy in transportation is targeted to reach 20% by 2030. The decree outlines the need for investments in infrastructure and monitoring systems to ensure the accurate certification and tracking of renewable hydrogen production.
policyType: [{"topic":"Fuels","family":"Regulations","name":"Guarantees of origin","category":"Hydrogen"}]

title: Power Development Master Plan IX
description: The plan proposes 5% hydrogen blending in natural gas to have a gradual ramp-up towards high hydrogen use. The plan has 5.8 GW of non-conventional renewable capacity
policyType: [{"topic":"Fuels","family":"Framework legislation","name":"Energy and climate strategy","category":"Hydrogen"}]

title: Energy Plan 2023-2050
description:
The strategic hydrogen roadmap outlines four key focus areas:

Policy and R&D (2023 onwards): Initiating research and development efforts alongside foundational policy work to support hydrogen technologies.
National Policy Framework (2023–2024): Establishing a formal regulatory and strategic framework to guide hydrogen development and deployment.
International Collaboration (2023 onwards): Engaging with global partners to share knowledge, align standards, and foster investment.
Infrastructure Development (2028–2035): Building the necessary infrastructure for hydrogen production, storage, transport, and utilization over the long term.
This phased approach aims to create a robust and internationally integrated hydrogen ecosystem.
policyType: [{"topic":"Fuels","family":"Framework legislation","name":"Energy and climate strategy","category":"Hydrogen"}]

title: Bill 52 - Energy and Utilities Statutes Amendment Act
description: Bill would remove barriers to allow hydrogen blending in the natural gas distribution system for residential and commercial heating. The blending limit suggested by the Utilities Minister was 5%, but this is not part of the legislation. The 5% is also the limit used by ATCO (local utility provider) in the pilot project in Fort Saskatchewan
policyType: [{"topic":"Fuels","family":"Infrastructure","name":"Blending","category":"Hydrogen"}]

title: National green hydrogen strategy
description: The strategy outlines five priorities: hydrogen production near the Port of Aqaba, demand creation in transport and blending, low-cost supply through regulation and incentives, continued renewable energy deployment, and an enabling environment with standards and workforce development. It includes 43 actions across three timeframes to 2050, with designated stakeholders. Plans include domestic electrolyzer manufacturing from the 2030s and a certification scheme before 2030. Three scenarios explore renewable hydrogen production of up to 3.4 Mtpa by 2050, with demand reaching 1.1 Mtpa. Estimated investment needs total USD 175 billion. Follow-up actions include forming a cross-ministerial steering committee and a dedicated hydrogen unit within the Ministry of Energy and Mineral Resources.
policyType: [{"topic":"Fuels","family":"Framework legislation","name":"Hydrogen strategy","category":"Hydrogen"}]

title: Important Project of Common Interest (IPCEI) Hy2Infra for specific projects
description: Lhyfe signs grant contract for up to EUR 149 million for its 34 tpd plant.

title: Important Project of Common Interest (IPCEI) Hy2Wave for specific projects
description: Gen Hy signs contract to receive up to EUR 100 million grant for constructing an AEM electrolyzer manufacturing plant to start operations in Q1 2026. The plant is expected to be able to produce 350 units of 0.1-2 MW per year.

title: Bavarian Electrolyzer Funding Program
description:
EUR 150 million (USD 170 million) to promote hydrogen production in the state. Minimum electrolyzer size is 1 MW for the first round and the second round targets electrolyzers of 5-10 MW
First round was awaded in July 2024 for EUR 55 million (USD 61 million) to 11 projects (each one receiving EUR 5 million) with an electrolyzer capacity of 5-8.5 MW. The call was oversubscribed by a factor of 3.5
Second round was awarded in April 2025 for EUR 65 million (USD 73 million) to 11 electrolyzer projects

title: National hydrogen and ammonia roadmap
description: The national hydrogen strategy is structured around reducing fossil fuel dependence, accelerating decarbonization, and boosting global competitiveness, with implementation across three phases: groundwork and policy development (2025–2034), scaling and integration (2035–2045), and large-scale deployment post-2045. It supports diverse hydrogen production methods—electrolysis, coal gasification, biogas reforming, and natural hydrogen—and targets sectors like transport, power, gas networks, and industry. Ammonia production includes carbon capture and is aimed at fertilizers, power, and shipping. By 2060, hydrogen demand could reach 3.4–11.8 Mtpa, with supply up to 17.5 Mtpa—30–50% of which could be exported—driven largely by renewable sources like hydropower and biogas.
policyType: [{"topic":"Fuels","family":"Framework legislation","name":"Hydrogen strategy","category":"Hydrogen"}]

title: National electricity system development program 2024-2038
description: Progressively increase the share of hydrogen in the energy mix until reaching a ratio of 25% hydrogen and 75% natural gas in the mix used by 2036, by converting 5,789 MW of installed capacity into combined cycle plants to operate with this mix
policyType: [{"topic":"Fuels","family":"Framework legislation","name":"Energy and climate strategy","category":"Hydrogen"}]

title: Hydrogen guidelines
description: The hydrogen guidelines seek to establish a comprehensive policy for the development of low-emission hydrogen in Mexico, promoting its adoption in key sectors such as energy, industry, and mobility. Their objective is to create a national strategy that promotes a sustainable energy transition, fosters technological innovation, strengthens the national industry, generates social and environmental benefits, and positions the country as a leader in the production, use, and export of internationally certified hydrogen
policyType: [{"topic":"Fuels","family":"Framework legislation","name":"Hydrogen strategy","category":"Hydrogen"}]

title: National Hydrogen Strategy
description: Draft strategy was open to public consultation from February to March 2025. The strategy showcases some scenarios for hydrogen development to 2050 with 2030 milestones. The scenarios are based on fixed technology penetrations by sector. Total investment needs are EUR 2.4 billion by 2030 and EUR 6.8 billion by 2050 for the ambitious scenario, while the conservative scenario has an investment of EUR 170 million by 2050. The 2030 plan covers 3 areas. Legislative framework;  Communication and training; and Development of heavy-duty trucks and bus fleets. The strategy proposes actions for the first two areas: First, a legislative framework to be developed by 2027; Second the use of online platforms, social media, training and cooperation for communication and training
policyType: [{"topic":"Fuels","family":"Framework legislation","name":"Hydrogen strategy","category":"Hydrogen"}]

title: National Energy and Climate Plan
description: Slovenia’s 2030 energy strategy (updated in 2023) includes hydrogen as a key element of the green transition. It estimates that 100 MW of electrolyzer capacity would be needed by 2030 increasing to 660 MW by 2050. Estimates EUR 223 million of cumulative investment in hydrogen infrastructure by 2030 (mostly for electrolyzers and pipelines) and EUR 1779 million by 2050. 2030 targets include the construction of two major electrolysis units (without a specified capacity)
policyType: [{"topic":"Fuels","family":"Framework legislation","name":"Energy and climate strategy","category":"Hydrogen"}]

description: The future strategy is expected to set long-term H₂ targets (production, use, infrastructure) to 2030–2050 in line with EU climate goals

title: Mainland China's National Development and Reform Commission (NDRC) and the National Energy Administration announced action plan to decarbonize coal power plants
description: The NDRC has asked for provincial governments as well as state-owned enterprises to voluntarily nominate coal projects that can be pilots for this program, which is the first time these technologies are being deployed in a centralized national scheme targeting coal-fired power plants. The test runs will help cut carbon intensities of coal plants by around 20% by 2025 and 50% by 2027 from the average industry levels in 2023. Cofiring renewable ammonia is one of the decarbonizing pathways that will be tested among biomass cofiring and carbon capture and storage. For cofiring of both renewable ammonia and biomass, these components have to make up at least 10% of the fuel mix, and that the projext should use renewable ammonia derived from mega-projects being constructed in mainland China's desert areas.

title: EU 2040 climate targets
description: In February 2024, the European Commission presented its assessment for a 2040 climate target for the EU whereby the commission recommends that net GHG emissions are deduced by 90% in 2040 relative to 1990 levels. Clean hydrogen is stated to play a large role in reaching these targets. Up to 35 MMt of production by 2040 is outlined, which represents up to 10% of final energy demand. The assessment published by the commission accounted for 3 million metric tons per year (MMt/y) of H2 production by 2030, which is below the target set in the EU's 2020 hydrogen strategy. Other roles for hydrogen in power generation, heavy-duty transport and long-term storage are not considered in the assessment.
policyType: [{"topic":"Fuels","family":"Framework legislation","name":"Energy and climate strategy","category":"Hydrogen"}]

title: Power Development Plan (PDP) draft
description: Thailand's latest draft Power Development Plan (PDP) includes targets to blend hydrogen into its gas-based power sector, initially at 5% and looking to increase the blending ratio to 20% between 2035 and 2037.

Framework done based on input from multiples stakeholders (public, private, academia, civil society, international actors). title: National guarantee for national development finance institution
description: The main incentive is a sovereign guarantee from the Colombian government to FDN, enabling the institution to secure external credit (loans) from multilateral organizations, governments, funds, and other international support entities. This guarantee reduces the risk for lenders, allowing FDN to access better credit terms and channel resources to support Colombia’s energy transition. The guarantee is specifically for credit operations up to USD 138.5 million (or equivalent in other currencies). The funds must be used exclusively for the Energy Transition Support Program. The document authorizes the guarantee and credit operation for the period 2024–2025

title: Bill on Long-term Energy Policy Orientation
description: The long-term orientation of the Swedish energy policy includes four principles for hydrogen developments Fossil-free hydrogen shall support the transition to fossil-free energy systems and industrial processes;  Priority shall be given to economically beneficial applications lacking cost-effective alternatives;  Production shall be efficiently integrated with electricity and heat systems to enhance energy security; Infrastructure expansion shall facilitate climate transition while maintaining Sweden’s competitive energy prices

title: State credit guarantees for green investments
description: Swedish National Debt Office (Riksgälden) offer state credit garantees for green industrial investments that contribute to Sweden's enviromental and climate targets. title: New Industry Package (Nova Indústria Brasil)
description: Brazil is investing BRL 300 billion (USD 53 billion) from 2024 to 2026 to reindustrialize the country with a focus on productivity, sustainability, and innovation. Six priority areas include food, health, infrastructure, digital industry, energy transition, and energy security. BRL 17.6 billion (USD 3.2 billion) is allocated to energy transition, aiming to cut emissions, boost biofuels and EVs, and reduce industrial carbon output. Support includes grants, loans, and subsidies. A BRL 10 billion call launched in May 2025 in the Northeast invites business plans by September, with funding decisions expected in November.

title: Tax incentives
description: In July 2025, a new bill on the "Regulatory Framework for the Promotion of Investments in the Renewable Hydrogen and Low-Emission Hydrogen and its Derivatives Industry" was submitted to the Chamber of Deputies. The bill provides for the declaration of national interest for investments in the development, production, transportation, storage, export, and use of renewable and low-emission hydrogen, as well as its derivatives, throughout the national territory. It includes a 30-year tax stability clause for investment projects linked to the hydrogen value chain, which implies that such projects would not be affected by the repeal of the law or by the creation or increase of taxes that would be more burdensome than those in force at the time of its approval. Furthermore, if the law is approved, low-emission hydrogen projects could apply, within an extended window of five years from the law's approval, to join the Large Investment Incentive Regime. (RIGI) created by Law 27,742 and regulated by Decree No. 749/2024. Projects that successfully join the RIGI are granted regulatory stability in tax, customs, and foreign exchange matters for 30 years, in addition to fiscal, tariff, and foreign exchange market access incentives.

title: Additional support for hydrogen development
description: Three measures to support hydrogen development were announced: First, creating a demand response pilot program for electrolyzers; second, exploring options to regulate hydrogen pipelines; thrid expanded hydrogen innovation fund with two streams, one for the integration of low-carbon hydrogen into the electricity grid and one to support hydrogen use in heavy industry and transport
policyType: [{"topic":"Fuels","family":"Framework legislation","name":"Master Energy Plan","category":"Hydrogen"}]

title: Multi-year funding for hydrogen as part of the Climate Package 2026
description: As part of its multi-year hydrogen program through 2030, the government has allocated over EUR 9.5 billion across key areas. Major investments include EUR 3 billion for research, EUR 2.5 billion for the hydrogen backbone, and EUR 2.1 billion for large-scale onshore electrolysis (500–1000 MW). Additional funding supports offshore electrolysis (EUR 1.19 billion), IPCEI projects (EUR 1.59 billion total for Hy2Use, Hy2Infra, and Hy2Move), demand-side subsidies (EUR 662 million), import infrastructure (EUR 500 million), and H2Global (EUR 300 million). Smaller allocations target inland shipping (EUR 30.5 million) and pilot-scale onshore electrolysis (EUR 250 million). This comprehensive funding strategy aims to scale hydrogen production, infrastructure, and market uptake across sectors.
policyType: [{"topic":"Fuels","family":"Framework legislation","name":"Master Energy Plan","category":"Hydrogen"}]

title: EU's Just Transition Fund for electrolysis (Saxony-Anhalt)
description: EUR 87 million for renewable hydrogen subsidies with focus on post-coal mining areas. Funds will come from the Just Transition Fund of the EU. Subsidy (as grants) for up to EUR 2000/kW for production, storage and end use. There are two programs in the fund EUR 58 million for "Green Hydrogen: Electrolyzers";  EUR 29 million for "Future Energies/Green Hydrogen"
policyType: [{"topic":"Fuels","family":"Resource push","name":"Grants for supply","category":"Hydrogen"}]

title: List of Demonstration projects for Advanced Green and Low-Carbon Technologies (Batch 1)
description: China's NDRC general office issued a high-priority list of 47 demo projects for advanced low-carbon/green techs.
policyType: [{"topic":"Fuels","family":"Framework legislation","name":"Master Energy Plan","category":"Hydrogen"}]

title: List of Demonstration projects for Advanced Green and Low-Carbon Technologies (Batch 2)
description: China's NDRC general office issued a high-priority list of 101 demo projects for advanced low-carbon/green techs.
policyType: [{"topic":"Fuels","family":"Framework legislation","name":"Master Energy Plan","category":"Hydrogen"}]

title: Action Plan for Low-carbon Transformation and Consturction of Coal power Plants(2024-2027)
description: China's NDRC and NEA jointly issued Action Plan to blend green hydrogen from surplas renewable energy into coal power
policyType: [{"topic":"Fuels","family":"Framework legislation","name":"Master Energy Plan","category":"Hydrogen"}]

title: Inner Mongolia plan for Green Hydrogen Pipeline Construction Development
description: The Inner Monglia Energy Bureau plans to cordinate green markets within/outside the region, starting from pilot H2 pipeline projects as a near term step, to create a comprehensive network through optimized pipeline layout, and smart dispatch systems, and peak shaving storage such as fixed H2 tanks and underground caverns.
policyType: [{"topic":"Fuels","family":"Resource push","name":"Administrative measures","category":"Hydrogen"}]

title: Key Research Directions for Green and Low-Carbon Standards in Industry and Information Technology (2025-2027)
description: The Ministry of Industry and Information Technology's 2025-2027 plan highlights six hydrogen energy applications, efficiency evaluation for alkaline water electrolysis, hydrogen production from coke oven gas, blast furnace injection of hydrogen-rich gas, hydrogen-based non-blast furnace ironmaking, and production of green methanol and ammonia from clean hydrogen.
policyType: [{"topic":"Fuels","family":"Framework legislation","name":"Master Energy Plan","category":"Hydrogen"}]

title: 11th Basic Electricity Supply and Demand Plan
description: The total power generation in 2038 is 704.5 TWh, followed by 248.3 TWh (35.2%), renewable 232.1 TWh (32.9%), gas 74.3 TWh (10.6%), coal 70.9 TWh (10.1%) and clean hydrogen and ammonia 43.9 TWh (6.2%).
policyType: [{"topic":"Fuels","family":"Framework legislation","name":"Energy and climate strategy","category":"Hydrogen"}]

title: Fujian Hydrogen Industry Innovation Development Medium and Long-term Plan (2025-2035)
description: Fujian aims to build a Southeast China full-chain H2 hub, with 2025-2030 focusing on commencing 10+ innovation platforms, 1-3 green H2 demo project(>100MW), 50 refueling stations, 10 transport routes, 6000 FCVs/y and 3Mt/y H2 production. Entering 2030-2035, green H2 capacity will grow to 10 Mt/y, 40 % total supply.
policyType: [{"topic":"Fuels","family":"Framework legislation","name":"Hydrogen strategy","category":"Hydrogen"}]

title: Renewable hydrogen strategy
description: Paraguay prioritises renewable hydrogen and defines targets for 2030 including 1 GW of electrolysis, 900 ktpa of fertilizer production and 80-100% substitution of current gas-based hydrogen. The strategy adopts a gradual approach with fertilizers as immediate hydrogen application with other uses dependent on market and technology development. Current fertilizer imports are 1.2-1.4 Mtpa out of which more than half could be replaced by 450 ktpa of renewable ammonia. The strategy defines 55 actions across 20 areas in six pillars including a regulation for additionality and temporal correlation of renewable electricity, the creation of demand hubs, the possible use of fiscal incentives and the development of a certification scheme.
policyType: [{"topic":"Fuels","family":"Framework legislation","name":"Hydrogen strategy","category":"Hydrogen"}]

title: Tax incentives for renewable hydrogen production
description:
Incentives include
- Full reimbursement of state goods and services tax for a period of 5 years from the start of operations for the renewable hydrogen sold within the state.
- Full exemption from electricity duties.
- Land lease and grid connection to the intra-state transmission grid to be allocated on a priority basis.
- Exemption from land tax payment, land use conversion charges and stamp duties.
policyType: [{"topic":"Fuels","family":"Resource push","name":"Tax incentives for supply","category":"Hydrogen"}]

title: Renewable hydrogen and ammonia production targets
description: Production targets of 0.5 Mtpa of renewable hydrogen and 2 Mtpa of ammonia (350 ktpa of hydrogen) by 2028. In July 2025, the target was updated to 1.5 Mtpa by 2029.
policyType: [{"topic":"Fuels","family":"Framework legislation","name":"Target","category":"Hydrogen"}]

title: Tax incentives for renewable hydrogen
description: Total funding of USD 2.8 billion for an exemption of the "first category" tax, which is a 25-27% tax on net taxable income (profits). A separate transition fund will be established to finance other support mechanisms pooling resources from the national economic development agency (CORFO) and the Treasury. The target is to approve the legislation before the end of the legislative term.
policyType: [{"topic":"Fuels","family":"Market pull","name":"Tax incentives for demand","category":"Hydrogen"},{"topic":"Fuels","family":"Resource push","name":"Tax incentives for supply","category":"Hydrogen"}]

title: Green Hydrogen Code
description: The Code establishes regulations for developing green hydrogen projects and provides substantial tax incentives to attract foreign and domestic investors (separate entry). This regulatory framework also created the Mauritanian Agency for Green Hydrogen (AMHV) to oversee green hydrogen operations, enhancing transparency and streamlining the process for investors entering this market. The code also establishes guarantees of origin and traceability to certify the renewable nature of the green hydrogen.
policyType: [{"topic":"Fuels","family":"Framework legislation","name":"Master Energy Plan","category":"Hydrogen"}]

title: Maritime Decarbonization Strategy
description: Strategy includes the use of low-emissions fuels to decarbonize shipping. Some of the policy measures considered that could promote the uptake of low-emissions fuels include a GHG emissions standard which might be considered for domestic shipping emissions subject to consultation in 2026, carbon pricing to which shipping will be exposed to once shipping is included in the UK ETS
policyType: [{"topic":"Fuels","family":"Framework legislation","name":"Master Energy Plan","category":"Hydrogen"}]

title: National SAF roadmap
description: The roadmap defines five actions to accelerate the decarbonization of the aviation sector including an ambition for 2030 (700 million L of SAF), innovation, a national regulatory framework, local capacity, and international collaboration. The roadmap includes scenarios to 2050 which consider synthetic fuel (power-to-liquid) reaching 0.4 Mtpa by 2030 and 2.3-11.2 Mtpa of e-SAF by 2050
policyType: [{"topic":"Fuels","family":"Framework legislation","name":"Master Energy Plan","category":"Hydrogen"}]

title: National Development Plan
description: The plan outlines Namibia's medium-term (2025-2030) national development strategy. It serves as the government's blueprint for guiding socioeconomic policies, resource allocation, and public investment priorities across various sectors for the duration of the NDP6 period. 2030 targets for hydrogen are 1.3 Mtpa of ammonia, 2 Mtpa of hydrogen-based DRI, 143 GWh of power generation from hydrogen, 30000 jobs created and 30% of domestic content. The policies considered to achieve these targets include contracts for difference, renewable hydrogen special economic zones (Walvis Bay) including streamlined permitting and infrastructure support, the development of domestic manufacturing capacity and new hydrogen infrastructure.
policyType: [{"topic":"Fuels","family":"Framework legislation","name":"Master Energy Plan","category":"Hydrogen"}]

title: Direct grant for green steel (Salzgitter)
description: EUR 700 million in federal funding and EUR 300 million in state funding has been allocated for the project "SALCOS" with the aim to produce raw green steel in Salzgitter. The complition of its first phase was due in 2025 with a planned capacity of 1.9 mtpa steel. As part of the project, the company also aims to install a 100 MW electrolyser and starting 2026, the plant will generate around 9 ktpa of renewable hydrogen.
policyType: [{"topic":"Fuels","family":"Market pull","name":"Grants for demand","category":"Hydrogen"}]

title: Direct grant for green steel (Stahl-Holding-Saar)
description: Stahl-Holding-Saar's “Power4Steel” project was initially selected as part of the IPCEI Hydrogen. The European Commission approved it as a separate project in December 2023. With the construction of a direct reduction plant and electric arc furnaces at the traditional steel sites in Dillingen/Saar and Völklingen, the companies involved are converting around two thirds of their production from coal-based blast furnace production to hydrogen-based steel production. The new plants are scheduled to go into operation in 2027. The aim is to produce more than three million tons of green steel. Funding notice was issued in January 2024.
policyType: [{"topic":"Fuels","family":"Market pull","name":"Grants for demand","category":"Hydrogen"}]

title: Direct grant for BASF Hy4Chem
description: The project comprises a 54-megawatt proton exchange membrane (PEM) electrolyzer to produce green hydrogen at BASF's Ludwigshafen site. This electrolyzer will produce up to 8 ktpa of hydrogen. The hydrogen produced will primarily be used as a raw material in BASF's production processes. Funding notice with a volume of EUR 124.3 million was provided in November 2023. The electrolyzer started operation in March 2025.
policyType: [{"topic":"Fuels","family":"Market pull","name":"Grants for demand","category":"Hydrogen"}]

title: National Action Plan for Climate-friendly Shipping (NAPS)
description:
With the National Action Plan for Climate-friendly Shipping (NAPS), the German government aims to support the maritime sector in Germany on its transformation path and strengthen its competitiveness and innovation expertise. The NAPS will be adopted by the Federal Government in 2025 and presented at the next National Maritime Conference. The NAPS accompanies the national implementation of regulations at EU, IMO and CCNR level. It is designed as an open-technology framework. For the NAPS, coordinated comprehensive measures will be developed for the five fields of action "alternative propulsion and energy systems, supply of climate-friendly energy sources, fleet modernization, maritime industrial policy and green shipping corridors", with which Germany will make a forward-looking contribution to achieving the energy transition goals for shipping. The NAPS complements existing strategies of the Federal Government, such as the National Ports Strategy and the updated National Hydrogen Strategy. 
The implementation of this National Action Plan will contribute to the following strategic goals: 
- Achieving climate protection targets
- Utilizing and expanding technological potential
- Establishing a level playing field
- Ensuring the supply of climate-friendly energy sources to the sector
- Unleashing entrepreneurial action; stimulating investment
- Seizing industrial policy opportunities
policyType: [{"topic":"Fuels","family":"Framework legislation","name":"Master Energy Plan","category":"Hydrogen"}]

title: Federal funding for industry and climate protection (BIK)
description: Supports investments in climate-friendly production facilities and technologies in the industrial sector, especially of SMEs. Projects have to reduce CO₂-emissions by at least 40% compared to previous emissions by replacing fossil fuels. The maximum financing amount is around EUR 3.3 billion in total and EUR 200 million per company. The first round is still being evaluated and a second call for projects was launched in March 2025.
policyType: [{"topic":"Fuels","family":"Market pull","name":"Grants for demand","category":"Hydrogen"},{"topic":"Fuels","family":"Resource push","name":"Grants for supply","category":"Hydrogen"}]

title: Public announcement of the first batch of green liquid fuel technology breakthrough and industrialization pilot projects
description: China's National Energy Administration(NEA) announced first batch of freen liquid fuel projects: selected projects are 9 in total, with 5 for green metahnol production, 3 for green ammonia and 1 celulosic ethanol.
policyType: [{"topic":"Fuels","family":"Framework legislation","name":"Master Energy Plan","category":"Hydrogen"}]

title: Green hydrogen roadmap
description: The roadmap outlines a vision for integrating renewable hydrogen in the national energy mix. The roadmap identifies 16 milestones across three phases (feasibility and demonstration in 2024-2027, deployment in 2028-2035, and expansion and integration in 2036-2050). Targets include 0.5-1 GW of electrolysis by 2027, 1.2-3 GW by 2028 and 3-6 GW by 2036. Investment needs for the across the three phases are USD 6.2-13.5 billion. Expected outcomes by 2050 include fossil fuel displacement in electricity production, 60% reduction in fertilizer imports and the creation of 27000-54000 jobs. The main electricity source is envisioned to be hydropower and the main use for domestic fertilizer production due to ongoing scarcity and growing domestic concerns about food security.
policyType: [{"topic":"Fuels","family":"Framework legislation","name":"Hydrogen strategy","category":"Hydrogen"}]

title: Tax incentives for renewable hydrogen
description: In alignment with the Economic Modernization Vision, the Cabinet approved the Incentives and Exemptions Committee’s decision at the Ministry of Investment to grant green hydrogen projects located outside the Aqaba Special Economic Zone a comprehensive incentives package. The approved package includes a 5% income tax rate with a 1% national contribution; exemptions from customs duties, general sales tax, and other levies on all project equipment, fixed assets, and spare parts; as well as exemptions from stamp duties on contracts related to financing, supply, installation, and operation. Additional benefits include exemption from withholding tax on imported services, a grace period of up to five years before public treasury land rents are collected, and tax exemptions for non-resident financiers on interest, fees, and related loan payments for the duration of project agreements.
policyType: [{"topic":"Fuels","family":"Market pull","name":"Tax incentives for demand","category":"Hydrogen"}]

title: Climate Investment Fund for industrial decarbonization
description: Namibia has been invited by the Climate Investment Fund (CIF) to develop a Sectoral Transformation Investment Plan (STIP) — unlocking up to USD 250 million in catalytic funding for industrial-scale commercial projects that support Namibia’s hashtag industrialisation and decarbonisation ambitions. Matching contributions are anticipated from global development banks and financial institutions. Targeted applications are hard-to-abate sectors
policyType: [{"topic":"Fuels","family":"Market pull","name":"Grants for demand","category":"Hydrogen"}]

title: Green Hydrogen Production Chain Development Program (H2V)
description: BRL 102.4 million (USD 18.8 million) to be awarded in the form of grants with up to BRL 30 million per project. The aim of the call for proposals is to boost the green hydrogen production chain in Rio Grande do Sul, enabling the production, transmission, storage, and use of this sustainable fuel, both for domestic consumption and for international markets. 16 proposals were submitted and 12 projects satisfied the technical criteria. The next step is the analysis of economic-financial capacity and counterparts which is expected to be finalized by October 2025 with contracts awarded by January 2026
policyType: [{"topic":"Fuels","family":"Resource push","name":"Grants for supply","category":"Hydrogen"}]

title: Legal Framework for Green Hydrogen and Green Industry
description: The framework sets clear definitions and incentives to develop hydrogen-based industries, support energy transition projects, and create an attractive legal environment for investors. The framework will be overseen by a steering committee which includes 21 institutions and six thematic chambers covering market development, infrastructure, research, training, and innovation.
policyType: [{"topic":"Fuels","family":"Framework legislation","name":"Master Energy Plan","category":"Hydrogen"}]

title: Renewable hydrogen exchange market trial in Tokyo
description: The Tokyo Commodity Exchange (Tocom), on behalf of the Tokyo Metropolitan Government, launched hydrogen tenders in December 2024. On the supply side, one winner offered JPY 300/Nm³ (USD 21.2/kg). On the demand side, two winners bid JPY 89/Nm³ (USD 6.3/kg) and JPY 230/Nm³ (USD 16.3/kg). The government will subsidize the price gap. Deliveries ran from January to March 2025. A second trial is planned for July–September 2025. Supplier and buyer tenders were scheduled for May, with results expected in early June and contracts signed the same month. In June 2025, bids were split into two categories: - Cargo trailers: Demand-side winner bid JPY 100/Nm³ (USD 7.7/kg); supply-side JPY 280/Nm³ (USD 21.6/kg). - Cylinders: Demand-side winner bid JPY 280/Nm³ (USD 21.6/kg); supply-side JPY 355/Nm³ (USD 27.4/kg).
policyType: [{"topic":"Fuels","family":"Resource push","name":"Contracts for difference","category":"Hydrogen"}]

title: Port of Tokyo will waive entry fee for LNG and H2 powered ships
description: Port of Tokyo will waive an entry fee for ships powered by LNG and hydrogen, as well as LNG bunkering ships, to promote the use of cleaner marine fuels.
policyType: [{"topic":"Fuels","family":"Market pull","name":"Tax incentives for demand","category":"Hydrogen"}]

title: Norwegian Hydrogen Strategy
description: Presented by the Minister for Petroleum and Energy and the Minister for Climate and Environment in June 2020, the Norwegian Hydrogen Strategy lays the foundation for the future work on hydrogen in Norway and contributes to the development of low emissions technologies for the greenhouse gases reduction goal. The strategy defines how clean hydrogen will be produced and the sectors of the economy where this energy carrier is going to contribute more to decarbonisation. Focus is posed on industrial processes and the heavy transport, with the maritime sector in particular, where the country is already committed in investments and research. It highlights also the importance of international collaboration both for the development of the technologies needed and for the establishment of a functioning market.
policyType: [{"topic":"Fuels","family":"Framework legislation","name":"Hydrogen strategy","category":"Hydrogen"}]

title: Revised Green Growth Strategy
description:
The government originally unveiled the growth strategy in December 2020 as part of an action plan for 2050 carbon neutrality. The revised strategy targets to accelerate the country’s shift to EVs, develop carbon-neutral synthetic fuels, and switch to ammonia and hydrogen for fossil use

It also aims to begin 30% co-burning of hydrogen at gas-fired power plants and mono-burning of hydrogen for power generation, as well as commence 20% co-burning of ammonia at coal-fired power plants
policyType: [{"topic":"Fuels","family":"Framework legislation","name":"Energy and climate strategy","category":"Hydrogen"}]

title: France 2030 - Hydrogen
description:
President Emmanuel Macron announced France 2030, an investment plan centred on the modernisation of several sectors of the French economy by 2030. The energy sector is highly concerned by the plan, accounting for five out of ten objectives stated, among which the aim for France to become a green hydrogen world leader by 2030, with at least two electrolysers gigafactories in France.
On 16th Nov, Macron announced 1.9b EUR for the development of clean hydrogen production technologies, through financing of projects; these resources are additional to the 7b EUR from the hydrogen strategy.
policyType: [{"topic":"Fuels","family":"Framework legislation","name":"Hydrogen strategy","category":"Hydrogen"}]

title: Flemish Hydrogen Vision and Strategy (Economy, Science and Innovation)
description:
The Flemish Hydrogen Vision & Strategy has a dual purpose. Through Research and Innovation reinforce our Flemish industrial ecosystem, in view of positioning our technology providers in the European and global value chain of hydrogen technologies and systems (reinforce technological leadership);  Support the implementation of hydrogen in our Flemish economy and society, in view of the sustainable transition of our industry and other societal sectors (e.g. mobility)
5 Strategic Goals identified. Supporting excellent research in hydrogen in Flanders knowledge centres (universities and strategic research centres); Strengthening the industrial ecosystem in Flanders; Stimulating the use of hydrogen and the roll out of hydrogen technologies; Facilitate international partnerships; and Favourable framework conditions for hydrogen
policyType: [{"topic":"Fuels","family":"Framework legislation","name":"Hydrogen strategy","category":"Hydrogen"}]

title: Newfoundland and Labrador Hydrogen Development Action Plan
description: Newfoundland and Labrador’s Hydrogen Development Action Plan aims to leverage the province’s abundant renewable resources, such as wind and water, to produce green hydrogen through electrolysis, positioning it as a global clean energy supplier. The plan outlines 31 action items over three years, focusing on export and domestic markets, regulatory frameworks, industry support, and workforce development. It emphasizes international collaboration, particularly with European countries, to meet growing global demand for green hydrogen and ammonia, and aims to create economic growth, job opportunities, and support Canada’s net-zero emissions target by 2050.
policyType: [{"topic":"Fuels","family":"Framework legislation","name":"Hydrogen strategy","category":"Hydrogen"}]

title: Inner Mongolia 6th provincial Hydrogen Development Plan
description:
China’s northern province Inner Mongolia established two critical hydrogen policies – a Hydrogen Industry 14th Five-Year Plan and a Hydrogen Industry Development Execution Plan, aiming to take a leading position in China’s embryonic green hydrogen sector.
The two policies outline the ambition to build a green hydrogen production base in the province totalling 0.5 million tons per year renewable hydrogen production capacity, 100 refuelling stations, and 5000 fuel cell heavy-duty trucks by the end of 2025.
Meanwhile, the province also will unleash ten demo projects in the fields of green hydrogen metallurgy, green hydrogen power-to-chemical, green hydrogen distributed energy supply, and heating co-production.
policyType: [{"topic":"Fuels","family":"Framework legislation","name":"Hydrogen strategy","category":"Hydrogen"}]

title: Bavaria Hydrogen Roadmap
description: Bavaria has set the goal of being climate-neutral by 2040. With the Hydrogen Roadmap, the Free State highlight the perspectives and actions to ramp-up the hydrogen economy. Demand is expected to come mainly from mobility, petrochemical, power and heat generation (central and in the industrial sector). Capacity for electrolytic hydrogen production is limited due to the low renewable resources potential, so Bavaria will have to rely on imports in the long term. Anyway, by 2030 at least 1 GW of electrolysis must be installed in Bavaria (300 MW by 2025) to meet the assumed additional hydrogen demand. In addition, connection to the European Hydrogen Backbone must be accelerated.
policyType: [{"topic":"Fuels","family":"Framework legislation","name":"Hydrogen strategy","category":"Hydrogen"}]

title: Inner Mongolia Policy to promote the hydrogen energy industry
description:
Provincial Hydrogen Development Plan – High-Quality Growth Strategy (2025 Targets)
As the fourth hydrogen-related policy issued in two months, this execution plan builds on the province’s 14th Five-Year Hydrogen Industry Plan (Feb 2025). It sets more ambitious targets than the national plan, aiming to accelerate hydrogen deployment across sectors. By 2025, the province targets:

15+ green hydrogen demonstration projects
500,000 tons/year green hydrogen production capacity
1 million tons/year industrial by-product hydrogen recovery capacity
100+ hydrogen refueling stations
10,000+ fuel cell vehicles (FCVs), including 5,000+ heavy-duty trucks
10+ demonstration projects applying green hydrogen in chemicals, non-ferrous metals, steel, distributed power, and CHP systems
policyType: [{"topic":"Fuels","family":"Framework legislation","name":"Hydrogen strategy","category":"Hydrogen"}]

title: National Green Hydrogen Mission
description: Target to produce 5 Mt of “green” hydrogen by 2030 (with associated 125 GW of renewable capacity additions) with additional potential to reach 10 Mt/yr with exports. Interest in developing a domestic electrolyser manufacturing industry
policyType: [{"topic":"Fuels","family":"Framework legislation","name":"Hydrogen strategy","category":"Hydrogen"}]

title: Hydrogen Strategy
description: The Government has formulated the Hydrogen Strategy to address the technical challenges in the six major areas of safety, suitable technologies, infrastructure, cost-effectiveness, capacity building and public acceptance. The Strategy sets out the four major strategies of improving legislations, establishing standards, aligning with the market and advancing with prudence to create an environment conducive to the development of hydrogen energy in Hong Kong so that Hong Kong would be able to capitalize on the environmental and economic opportunities brought about by hydrogen. Hong Kong, like the rest of Asia, takes a view that blue hydrogen molecules are appropriate transitional fuel provided the upstream emission is adequately controlled. Hong Kong government will fund 14 projects focused around transport, power generation and hydrogen transport (blended into gas pipelines). There was no consumption/production target defined in the strategy
policyType: [{"topic":"Fuels","family":"Framework legislation","name":"Hydrogen strategy","category":"Hydrogen"}]

title: National Hydrogen Strategy and Roadmap
description: Focus on renewable hydrogen due to declining production of natural gas. Potential for exports, especially to Brazil by pipeline. Consideration of e-fuels to replace oil imports. Target of 150 ktpa of renewable hydrogen production by 2030 (out of which 85 ktpa are to be exported). This increases to 1.35 Mtpa by 2040 and 4.15 Mtpa by 2050. LCOH target of USD 1.8/kg by 2030 and USD 1/kg by 2050. Cumulative investment needs of USD 26-34.4 billion by 2050. A large demand foreseen for hydrogen derivatives including 1.33 Mtpa of e-methanol by 2050. Roadmap has the cost, potential, challenges and 2050 vision, while the strategy focuses more on the actions needed to achieve that 2050 vision
policyType: [{"topic":"Fuels","family":"Framework legislation","name":"Hydrogen strategy","category":"Hydrogen"}]

title: Abu Dhabi Public Policy on Low-Carbon Hydrogen
description: Lays out the goverenance of hydrogen policy making by defining institutional responsibilities and mandates. It mentions some general principles for hydrogen valleys, electricity demand centers, allocation of land and public corridors but does not give details. There is a section on a low-carbon hydrogen certification scheme which will be voluntary, they might develop a domestic scheme or adopt an international one and does not impose the use of this scheme for the national production
policyType: [{"topic":"Fuels","family":"Regulations","name":"Certification scheme thresholds","category":"Hydrogen"}]

title: Provincial support for hydrogen for data centers
description: The government has a target of 1200 data centers country-wide by 2032 Chungcheongnam-do province announced plans to use clean hydrogen in 3x300 MW fuel cells in Dangjin. The total project cost is KRW 4.5 trillion (USD 3.23 billion), out of which the fuel cells are KRW 2.4 trillion Gyeongsangbuk-do province approved funding for a 108 MW fuel cell in the Gangdong industrial complex. The total investment is USD 556 million with the amount of public funding undisclosed
policyType: [{"topic":"Fuels","family":"Market pull","name":"Grants for demand","category":"Hydrogen"}]

title: Baden-Württemberg Hydrogen Roadmap
description: The Hydrogen Roadmap, adopted by the state government in December 2020, aims to position the region as a leading hub for the hydrogen and fuel cell industry, with a focus on producing components and subsystems for both national and international markets. It outlines specific objectives and measures across production, infrastructure, and application areas, each with defined timelines. A Progress Report evaluating advancements and updates was released in 2024.
policyType: [{"topic":"Fuels","family":"Framework legislation","name":"Hydrogen strategy","category":"Hydrogen"}]

title: National green hydrogen and ammonia roadmap
description: The roadmap defines four phases of hydrogen development: a pilot and research phase, an implementation phase, a commercialisation phase and an exporting phase. Targets for the second phase include USD 250 million investment, 100% import replacement of urea, 15% co-firing in cement and 120 MW of electrolyser capacity. The last phase includes targets of 8-9 GW of electrolysis across nine hubs and 8 Mtpa of ammonia production. The roadmap defines 44 actions across nine areas to achieve these targets including tax incentives, credit guarantee schemes, public procurement, certification and knowledge exchange
policyType: [{"topic":"Fuels","family":"Framework legislation","name":"Hydrogen strategy","category":"Hydrogen"}]

title: Action Plan for Green Maritime Fuel Bunkering
description: Targets include a 7% of its registered ships using green marine fuels by 2030 and 55% of the diesel-fuelled vessels in the government fleet switching to green fuels by 2026. The government estimates that the demand triggered by these targets could be 200 ktpa of green maritime fuels. CO2 emission reduction targets of 11% by 2026 (vs 2019) and 20% by 2030 (vs 2008) and 70% by 2040. Hong Kong will complete its draft Code of Practice for green methanol bunkering by 2026 as part of its multi-fuel strategy. The plan sets out five strategies and 10 actions to develop the supply and infrastructure for green maritime fuels. Actions include to establish a Green Maritime Fuel Bunkering Incentive Scheme and simplify the approval process for green maritime fuel bunkering

title: Broad-Based Socio-Economic Empowerment Charter for the Mining and Minerals Industry
description:
The regulation aims to facilitate sustainable transformation, growth and development of the mining industry while redressing historical socio-economic inequalities, by promoting the participation of Historically Disadvantaged Persons (as defined therein) in the mining and minerals industry. 
Some of the benefits that the complying companies are entitled to are to offset a certain percentage of the amount spent on qualifying beneficiation investments against procurement obligations and the possibility to apply for equity equivalent credits. The policy is also used to promote investment in the mineral sector. 
The guidelines for implementation of this policy can be found in the Implementation Guidelines for the Broad-Based Socio-Economic Empowerment Charter for the Mining and Minerals Industry, 2018.

title: Tax Incentives and Exemptions in Zambia
description:
The Zambia Revenue Authority promotes various fiscal incentives in the mining sector. One of those is that dividends paid by a mining company with a mining licence and carrying on mining operations is 0% taxed. Another is 25% of mining deductions on capital expenditure on buildings, railway lines, equipment, or similar works, as well as zero rating of capital on certain equipment and machinery when supplied to a large-scale mining licence. 
In contrast, in 2025 the tax rate for manufacturers of products made from copper cathodes increased from 15% to 20%. Also, another tax on minerals is the Mineral Royalty. It is a payment owed for the extraction of minerals in the Republic of Zambia which depends on the mineral and price of the mineral. Cobalt and Vanadium have the highest percentage of minerals due as Mineral Royalty Rate at 8%, compared to 5% being the lowest for base metals and energy and industrial minerals.

title: Bottom-Up Economic Transformation Agenda for Inclusive Growth
description:
Bottom-Up Economic Transformation Agenda for Inclusive Growth (BETA) is the Fourth Medium Term Plan developed by the National Council for Population and Development to accelerate socio-economic transformation to a more competitive economy in many sectors, including the mining sector. Such policy resulted in reforms in the mining sector such as the declaration of fourteen minerals as strategic due to their importance, therefore reserved for exploitation with government involvement. 
Other modifications and proposals include amendments to the Mining Act to facilitate investments, speeding the development of mining cadastre system and review of royalty rates and fees, development of a Mineral Value Addition and Processing Policy to develop those areas and audit of mineral rights to avoid illegal mining.

title: Strategy of the Energy, Mining and Geology Sectors
description:
To comply with the Strategy of the Energy, Mining and Geology Sectors, the government published the Morocco Mining Plan 2021. The Plan focuses on developing the non-phosphate mining sector through four pillars: (1) development of a network of competitive stakeholders; (2) institutional overhaul of the sector's organisation; (3) strengthening the social impact and the responsible and sustainable nature of the mining sector; and (4) adapting financing, legal, and fiscal resources to the sector's new ambitions.
In the field of geology, following the Strategy, the government published the National Geology Plan 2021-2030. Such Plan which aims to strengthen the Moroccan Geological Survey capacities and to advance the development of the country's mineral potential as part of the work of a National Committee for Strategic Minerals. Some results are the development of a Geoscientific Mapping Program of geological, geophysical and geochemical potential areas, the development of geoinformation sharing platforms and integration of analysis services.

title: Mineral Beneficiation Strategy for Namibia
description:
The goal of this strategy is for Namibia to develop their mineral industry from one that exports most of its minerals as concentrates and semi-processed forms to one who manufactures high-value intermediates and finished products. One of the goals is for copper and zinc to be refined in the country to pure metals before being exported. Such strategy also identifies lithium and graphite as pilot projects for mineral beneficiation and prioritising higher control on exports of unprocessed materials and incentives for local processing of lithium, rare earths, and uranium. 

To achieve this aim, there was a recent proposal to reform the Minerals (Prospecting and Mining) Act 33 of 1992 (amended on 2008) which is under public consultation (as of September 4, 2025).

title: Roadmap for the growth and development of Nigerian mining industry
description:
To diversify economic activity and export composition, the government launched the Roadmap for Solid Minerals in 2016 with the purpose of increasing mining’s contribution to GDP to 10% by 2026. The plan is divided into three phases: rebuilding the market confidence and win over domestic users of imported industrial minerals; focussing on expanding domestic processing industry; and seeking to return to global markets and a market competitive price point.
Even though not all of them are a direct result of the policy, currently, there are various incentives for the investment in the mining sector. One is the Tax Holiday incentive provided for new companies in the mining of solid minerals sector under which they are exempt from tax for the first three years of their operation. Another is the Export Expansion Grant Scheme, which grants the export credit certificates rates of 5 up to 15%, depending on the level of manufacturing of the goods  to be used to settle all federal government taxes and to purchase government bonds and repay government credit facilities and debts.

title: A Beneficiation Strategy for the Minerals Industry of South Africa
description:
The Beneficiation Strategy was enacted to provide a framework to align the sector with the objectives of the New Growth Path published by the government in 2009 which identified mineral beneficiation as one of the priority areas to create jobs. 
The Strategy selects 10 strategic mineral commodities from which five value chains are prioritised. These include energy minerals and Platinum Group Minerals such as coal, uranium, thorium, iron, steel, pigment and titanium metal production. The policy also seeks to address import-parity pricing especially of steel and heavy chemicals by strengthening economic relationships and expanding infrastructure to support it. 
To achieve this, the policy proposes to review and strengthen the legal framework, including the Income Tax Act in regard to the Income Tax Allowance Incentive (new applications ended in March 2020), the Policy Action Plan, and Research and Development (R&D) tax incentives. 
Another important item in the programme is encouraging beneficiation instead of the export of raw materials; therefore, then plan recommends reviewing the Minerals and Mining policy for South Africa (1998), and the Mineral and Petroleum Resources Development Act, 2002 (MPRDA).

On 21 September 2025, ARECOMS extended the ban further to 15 October 2025, along with a new policy establishing an export quota, to be implemented from 16 October 2025.

title: Fiscal incentives made available for investors
description:
The Republic of Zimbabwe provides certain tax benefits to mining investments in the country. According to the Income Tax Act, the taxable income of a holder of a special mining lease (mines which investment is made mostly in foreign currency or intended principally for export) has an especial 15% rate. Another important benefit is that the Minister of Mines may exempt, by statutory instrument the holder of a special mining lease wholly or partly from any non-resident shareholder’s tax, non-resident tax on fees, non-resident tax on remittances or non-resident tax on royalties. 
Also, expenditures related to mining operations incurred during the year of assessment on certain prospecting and exploratory works before and after acquiring rights to mine minerals, together with some others, are allowed deductions. They can be deducted in the year of assessment in which they are incurred; or carried forward and allowed against income from mining operations in any subsequent year of assessment.
Regarding Value Added Tax, the supply of mining goods used exclusively in mining can charged with a tax rate of 0% under certain conditions.  Furthermore, the Commissioner may authorize a deferment of payment on the tax of imported goods for the use of mining for up to 3 years, compared to the standard 180 day-period.

title: Nationally Determined Contribution (NDC) to the Paris Agreement: Nigeria
description:
Nigeria has submitted its updated Nationally Determined Contribution (NDC) to the Paris Agreement. The updated NDC sets economy-wide absolute emissions reduction targets instead of previous percentage reduction targets relative to a business-as-usual scenario. 

The NDC sets an economy-wide absolute emissions reduction target of 168.2 Mt CO2e in 2030 and 184.9 Mt CO2e in 2035 from base year 2018. This represents 29% and 32% of net national emissions in 2018, in 2030 and 2035, respectively. Nigeria aims to achieve net zero emissions by 2060.  

With respect to oil and gas emissions, the NDC commits to achieving zero routine gas flaring by 2030. It also sets a target of 60% reduction in fugitive emissions (leaks and venting) from the oil and gas industry by 2035 and 95% reduction by 2050.

title: Gas Flaring, Venting and Methane Emissions (Prevention of Waste and Pollution) Regulations, 2023
description:
These Regulations have been enacted under the Petroleum Industry Act, 2021 and seek to reduce the environmental and social impact of flaring and venting of natural gas and fugitive methane emissions and create social and economic benefits from gas flaring and venting. They apply to all licensees, lessees and producers of gas in upstream petroleum operations.

Rights over flare gas: The Regulations grant the Nigerian Upstream Petroleum Regulatory Commission (NUPRC) the right to take all gas at a flare point, free of charge and without payment of royalty. The NUPRC may award permits to applicants selected through a competitive bid process to access the disposed gas for commercialisation or utilisation.

Monetisation: Producers of gas are required to submit a Flare Elimination and Monetisation Plan for NUPRC’s approval, setting out the methodology and implementation plan for the elimination and monetisation of gas flaring from a licence or lease area. After its approval, producers are to enter into a Milestone Development Agreement with the NUPRC for its implementation.

Permitted gas flaring: Except in the case of emergencies, the Regulations permit gas flaring within a threshold approved by the NUPRC and upon payment of a flaring fee.

Monitoring and reporting: Producers and permit holders are required to maintain daily records of gas flaring, venting and fugitive methane emissions. In addition, permit holders are responsible for the provision and installation of metering equipment used for measuring disposed gas pursuant to their permit. The Regulations also stipulate reporting requirements for data, including natural gas wasted by deliberate venting, incomplete combustion, and fugitive emissions. NUPRC shall publish an annual report of the submissions by regulated entities on its website with data on each producer made available.

description:
These Regulations seek to regulate, monitor and enforce health and environmental measures relating to midstream and downstream petroleum operations. 

In terms of the provisions, licensees and permit holders are required to conduct monitoring and control of methane emissions from new and existing facilities and projects engaged in (a) processing, transportation, and distribution of hydrocarbons, and (b) storage of petroleum liquids and gas. They must also take inventory of equipment and components identified as sources or possible sources of methane emissions and implement LDAR and MRV programmes. Operators must also register new and existing emissions point sources in their facilities with the Authority and obtain a valid permit before discharging gaseous effluents into the environment 

In addition, the Regulations require licensees and permit holders to monitor and report GHG emissions generated from their operations and submit a strategy for carbon capture, decarbonisation and achievement of net-zero targets, for approval from the Nigerian Midstream and Downstream Petroleum Regulatory Authority.

title: Nigeria Tax Act, 2025
description:
The Nigeria Tax Act, 2025, taking effect from 1 January 2026 streamlines the taxation regime in Nigeria. 

In relation to petroleum operations, it levies a hydrocarbon tax on the profits of any company engaged in upstream petroleum operations. It permits the deduction of certain expenses in the computation of profit, including the costs of gas reinjection wells that re-inject natural gas that otherwise would be flared. However, any penalty, natural gas flare fees or imposition relating to natural gas flaring may not be deducted. 

The Act also lists the following fiscal incentives for the utilisation of associated gas:
  1. the investment required to separate crude oil and gas from the reservoir into usable products shall be considered as part of the oil field development;
  2. capital investment on facilities or equipment to deliver associated gas in usable form at utilisation or designated custody transfer points shall be treated as part of the capital investment for oil development

title: Angola's National Determined Contribution
description:
Angola has submitted its updated Nationally Determined Contribution (NDC) to the Paris Agreement. 
 
Angola has commitment to reducing its GHG emissions by 5% by 2035 unconditionally, using the 2020 Business-As-Usual scenario as a reference point, and by 11% conditional on international financial, technical and technological support.   
 
With respect to oil and gas emissions, the NDC notes reduced gas flaring at oil fields as a measure that could strongly contribute towards achieving the unconditional target, estimating a reduction of around 394 million standard cubic feet per day (MMSCF/day) with a reduction potential of 8.9 ktCO2e.

title: Decree Decree No. 2023/232 of 4 May 2023 to lay conditions for implementing Law No. 2019/008 of 25 April 2019 to institute the Petroleum Code
description:
This decree lays down the conditions for implementing Law No. 2019/008 to institute the Petroleum Code. 
In terms of Article 26, to obtain an exploitation authorisation, an operator is required to submit an application to the Ministry in charge of hydrocarbons. The application must include a recovery plan for associated gas, where liquid hydrocarbons are produced, and proposals for eliminating gas flaring and upgrading associated gas. 
In addition, authorisation holders are required to keep records of the quantities of gas flared and regularly submit reports to the mandated public body and Ministry in charge of hydrocarbons containing the gross volume and quality of gas flared (Articles 70 and 137). 
Further, contract holders are also required to conduct an environmental and social impact assessment that is required to include a plan to offset and mitigate environmental damage, including measure relating to test gas flaring (Article 90).
